la-mancha.s: La Mancha is a high plateau region of central Spain, south of Toledo. After the Almohad victory at the Battle of Alarcos in 1195, Almohad forces raided through the Tagus valley and La Mancha up to the walls of Toledo.

la-noche-triste.s: La Noche Triste, the 'Night of Sorrows', was the night in 1520 when Hernan Cortes and his Spanish forces and allies fled Tenochtitlan under attack by the Aztecs. Many Spaniards and allied warriors were killed during the retreat across the causeways.

lacquerware.s: Lacquerware is objects coated with lacquer made from the sap of the lacquer tree, producing a durable, glossy finish. It was highly developed in Han Dynasty China, where lacquered cups, boxes and trays were luxury goods produced in organised workshops.

lagash.s: Lagash was an ancient Sumerian city-state in southern Mesopotamia. Under rulers such as Gudea, it flourished in the period between the fall of the Akkadian Empire and the rise of the Third Dynasty of Ur.

lagos.s: Lagos, known in Yoruba as Eko, is a coastal city in south-western Nigeria. Oba Orhogbua of the Benin Empire established a garrison there in the sixteenth century, extending Benin's control along the coast.

lahore.s: Lahore is a major city in the Punjab, in present-day Pakistan, with a long history as a centre of political power. It was the capital of the Sikh Empire from 1799, when Ranjit Singh took it, and the seat of the Lahore Darbar.

lak.s: The Lak are an Iranian tribal people of the Zagros Mountains of western Iran. Karim Khan Zand, founder of the Zand Empire, came from a Lak branch of the Zand tribe.

lake-chad.s: Lake Chad is a large, shallow lake in the central Sahel, bordered today by Chad, Cameroon, Niger and Nigeria. Its basin was the heartland of the Kanem-Bornu Empire, whose economy depended on its resources and on trade routes across the Sahara.

lake-tana.s: Lake Tana is the largest lake in Ethiopia and the source of the Blue Nile. Its islands are home to ancient monasteries that are important centres of Ethiopian Christianity.

lake-tanganyika.s: Lake Tanganyika is a long, deep lake in the African Great Rift Valley, bordered by present-day Tanzania, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi and Zambia. Under rulers such as Kumwimbe Ngombe, military expeditions of the Luba Empire extended eastward towards the lake.

lake-texcoco.s: Lake Texcoco was a large lake in the Valley of Mexico, now largely drained. The Aztecs founded Tenochtitlan on an island in the lake, connecting it to the shore by causeways.

lalibela.s: Lalibela is a town in northern Ethiopia famous for its rock-hewn churches, built under the Zagwe dynasty that succeeded Aksum. These churches show clear influence from Aksumite architecture, demonstrating the survival of the Aksumite Empire's cultural legacy.

lamtuna.s: The Lamtuna were a Sanhaja Berber tribe of the western Sahara. They were the core tribal group of the Almoravid movement, providing its leaders, including Abu Bakr ibn Umar and Yusuf ibn Tashfin.

lancashire.s: Lancashire is a county in north-west England that became the centre of the British cotton textile industry during the Industrial Revolution. Its mills processed raw cotton imported from overseas and exported finished cloth across the world, including to India.

lance.s: A lance is a long spear designed for use by mounted soldiers, especially in the charge. In the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, lancers formed the elite of the cavalry, most famously the winged hussars, whose charges won several notable victories in the sixteenth and…

land-of-punt.s: The Land of Punt was a region known to the ancient Egyptians as a source of incense, myrrh, ebony, gold and exotic animals. Its exact location is uncertain but is generally placed along the southern Red Sea coast or the Horn of Africa.

land-of-the-bow.s: The Land of the Bow, Ta-Seti in Egyptian, was a name used by the ancient Egyptians for Nubia, reflecting the renown of Nubian archers. Skilled archery was a long-standing hallmark of Nubian warfare.

land-tenure.s: Land tenure refers to the rules and arrangements by which land is held, used, granted and transferred. In many empires, grants of land or of the revenue from land were used to reward soldiers, officials and religious institutions in return for service.

laos.s: Laos is a landlocked country in mainland South-East Asia along the middle Mekong. In earlier centuries, parts of its territory fell within the sphere of the Khmer Empire.

larsa.s: Larsa was an ancient city-state in southern Mesopotamia that rose to prominence after the fall of the Neo-Sumerian Empire. Under its king Rim-Sin it was one of the main rivals of Babylon in the early second millennium BCE.

late-bronze-age.s: The Late Bronze Age is the period of roughly the sixteenth to the twelfth centuries BCE in the Near East and eastern Mediterranean. It was an era of great territorial powers, including the Egyptian New Kingdom, the Hittite Empire, Mitanni, Babylon and Assyria, linked by…

late-bronze-age-collapse.s: The Late Bronze Age collapse was a period of widespread destruction and political breakdown in the eastern Mediterranean and Near East around 1200 BCE. Its causes are debated and probably combined drought, famine, migrations including the Sea Peoples, internal unrest and…

late-middle-ages.s: The Late Middle Ages is the period of European and wider Eurasian history from about 1300 to about 1500. It saw expanding long-distance trade, the Black Death and major political changes.

later-liang.s: The Later Liang was the first of the Five Dynasties that ruled northern China after the fall of the Tang Dynasty. It was founded in 907 by the warlord Zhu Wen, who deposed the last Tang emperor.

later-zhou.s: The Later Zhou was the last of the Five Dynasties that ruled northern China in the tenth century. Zhao Kuangyin, one of its military commanders, seized power in a coup in 960 and founded the Song Dynasty.

lateral-succession.s: Lateral succession is a system of inheritance in which power passes among brothers or members of the same generation before descending to the next. In the Elamite Confederation it formed part of a governing hierarchy that the site describes as unusually stable.

latifundium.s: A latifundium was a large agricultural estate in the Roman world, typically owned by a wealthy landowner and worked by enslaved labour or tenants. Such estates spread in Italy and the provinces as wealth became concentrated after Roman conquests.

latin.s: Latin is the language of ancient Rome, which spread across the western Mediterranean with Roman rule and became the root of the Romance languages. It remained the language of the Church, learning and administration in medieval Europe, including the Carolingian Empire and the…

latin-america.s: Latin America is the region of the Americas where Romance languages, chiefly Spanish and Portuguese, predominate. It was shaped by the colonial rule of the Spanish and Portuguese empires, which transformed its religion, languages and societies.

latins.s: Latins, or Latin Christians, was the term used in the Byzantine world for Western Christians following the Roman Church. Relations between Byzantines and Latins deteriorated over religious disputes, Italian commercial privileges and the Crusades.

law-of-the-free-womb.s: The Law of the Free Womb was a law passed in the Brazilian Empire in 1871 declaring that children born to enslaved women would be free. It was a gradual emancipation measure that did not free existing slaves.

league-of-nations.s: The League of Nations was the international organisation founded after the First World War to preserve peace and settle disputes. It placed the former colonies of the German Empire and Ottoman territories under the mandate system, much of it administered by the British Empire.

league-of-nations-mandate.s: A League of Nations mandate was a territory taken from the defeated German Empire or the Ottoman Empire after the First World War and placed under the administration of an Allied power. Mandatory powers were supposed to govern in the interests of the inhabitants under League…

leather.s: Leather is animal hide tanned and prepared for making goods such as bags, sandals, saddles and book covers. The Hausa cities of the Sokoto Caliphate, particularly Kano, were renowned for fine dyed leather.

lebanon.s: Lebanon is a mountainous country on the eastern Mediterranean coast, historically famous for its cedar forests. The Assyrian Empire drew on the timber of Lebanon for its building projects.

legal-amazon.s: The Legal Amazon is a large administrative region of Brazil covering the Amazon basin and adjacent areas, defined in modern Brazilian law. Accounts of the Brazilian Empire use the term for the vast northern territories that the nineteenth-century empire administered with…

legal-codification.s: Legal codification is the recurring process by which rulers gathered, standardised and proclaimed laws, strengthening central authority and the uniform administration of justice. Codes such as the Laws of Hammurabi in the Babylonian Empire, Justinian's codification in the…

legalism.s: Legalism was a school of Chinese political thought emphasising strict laws, harsh punishments and strong central control as the basis of order. It underpinned the Qin state that unified China in 221 BCE.

legatus.s: A legatus, or legate, was a senior Roman official or military commander acting on delegated authority. Under the Roman Empire, legates commanded legions and governed imperial provinces on the emperor's behalf.

legion.s: A legion was the principal unit of the Roman army, made up of several thousand heavy infantry citizen soldiers with supporting troops. Its discipline, training and engineering skill underpinned the expansion and defence of the Roman Empire.

lei-aurea.s: The Lei Aurea, or Golden Law, was the law of 1888 that abolished slavery in the Brazilian Empire. It was signed by Princess Isabel while acting as regent for her father Pedro II.

lend-lease.s: Lend-Lease was the United States programme that supplied Britain and other Allies with war materials during the Second World War. Its abrupt end in August 1945 left Britain facing a severe financial crisis and large dollar debts.

leo-africanus.s: Leo Africanus was a Moroccan-born traveller and writer who visited West Africa in the early sixteenth century. His description of Africa, later published in Europe, was for centuries a key European source on the region.

leo-iii-the-isaurian.s: Leo III the Isaurian was a Byzantine emperor who reigned from 717 to 741 and founded the Isaurian dynasty. He successfully defended Constantinople against the great Arab siege of 717 to 718, a decisive moment in the survival of the Byzantine Empire.

leo-tolstoy.s: Leo Tolstoy was a Russian novelist and moral thinker of the nineteenth century, author of War and Peace and Anna Karenina. He is regarded as one of the greatest writers in world literature.

leopold-ii.s: Leopold II was King of the Belgians from 1865 to 1909 and personal ruler of the Congo Free State, a regime notorious for its brutal exploitation. Forces of the Congo Free State absorbed the remnants of the Luba Empire after 1893.

leptis-magna.s: Leptis Magna was a major city on the coast of Tripolitania, in present-day Libya, founded by Phoenicians and later a prosperous Roman city. It was linked by trade to the Garamantian Empire of the Fezzan, which supplied goods such as wild animals for Roman arenas.

levant.s: The Levant is the region along the eastern Mediterranean coast, roughly corresponding to present-day Syria, Lebanon, Israel, Palestine and Jordan. Its position between Egypt, Mesopotamia and Anatolia made it a crossroads of trade and a frequent battleground.

lex-talionis.s: Lex talionis is the principle of retributive justice in which punishment mirrors the injury caused, often summarised as an eye for an eye. It is prominent in the Laws of Hammurabi of the Babylonian Empire, which often varied penalties according to social status.

li-hongzhang.s: Li Hongzhang was a leading Chinese statesman and general of the late Qing Empire. He played a major role in suppressing the Taiping Rebellion and promoted the Self-Strengthening Movement, building arsenals, industries and a modern navy.

li-jiancheng.s: Li Jiancheng was the eldest son of Li Yuan, founder of the Tang Dynasty, and the designated crown prince. Rivalry with his younger brother Li Shimin ended in the Xuanwu Gate Incident of 626, in which Li Jiancheng was killed.

li-jing.s: Li Jing was a leading general of the early Tang Dynasty. In 630 CE he led the campaign that conquered the Eastern Turkic Khaganate, capturing its qaghan after a surprise night attack.

li-zicheng.s: Li Zicheng was the leader of a peasant rebellion that overthrew the Ming Empire. His forces captured Beijing in 1644, after which the last Ming emperor took his own life.

li-zicheng-rebellion.s: The Li Zicheng rebellion was a peasant uprising in northern China lasting from the 1630s to 1644, fuelled by famine, heavy taxation and the weakness of the Ming state. It culminated in the rebels' capture of Beijing in 1644 and the death of the last Ming emperor.

liao-dynasty.s: The Liao dynasty was a state founded by the Khitans that ruled northern China, Manchuria and Mongolia from the tenth to the early twelfth century. It was the Song Dynasty's principal northern rival, and the Treaty of Chanyuan in 1005 obliged the Song to make annual payments to…

liberal-party-brazil.s: The Liberal Party was one of the two main political parties of the Brazilian Empire, alternating in government with the Conservative Party. It generally favoured greater provincial autonomy and political reform.

liberal-revolution-of-1820.s: The Liberal Revolution of 1820 was a constitutionalist uprising in Portugal, beginning in Porto. It demanded a constitution and the return of King John VI from Brazil, where the court had lived since 1808.

liberation-of-ethiopia-1941.s: The liberation of Ethiopia in 1941 was the defeat of Italian occupation forces by British and Commonwealth troops working with Ethiopian patriots during the Second World War. It ended the Italian occupation that had begun in 1936.

liberum-veto.s: The liberum veto was a parliamentary rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth allowing any single deputy of the Sejm to dissolve the session and annul its legislation. It reflected the nobility's commitment to unanimity and liberty.

library-of-alexandria.s: The Library of Alexandria was the great library founded under the Ptolemaic kings in Alexandria in the third century BCE, part of the Mouseion research institution. It aimed to collect all known Greek writing and became the leading centre of scholarship in the Hellenistic world.

library-of-nineveh.s: The Library of Nineveh, also known as the Library of Ashurbanipal, was a collection of thousands of cuneiform tablets assembled by the Assyrian king Ashurbanipal in the seventh century BCE. It contained literary, religious, scholarly and administrative texts, including the…

libya.s: Libya is a country in North Africa on the Mediterranean coast, comprising the historical regions of Tripolitania, Cyrenaica and the Fezzan. The Fezzan was the heartland of the Garamantian Empire, and the coast was conquered by Arab armies under the Rashidun Caliphate.

libyans.s: Libyans refers to the inhabitants of Libya and, in antiquity, to the indigenous Berber-speaking peoples of North Africa. In the Punic Empire, Libyan subjects were heavily taxed and supplied soldiers to Carthaginian armies, and their discontent fed revolts such as the Mercenary…

licchavi.s: The Licchavi were an ancient clan-based polity of north-eastern India, with an old republican tradition. Chandragupta I married the Licchavi princess Kumaradevi, an alliance that brought the early Gupta Empire territory and legitimacy.

lijia-system.s: The lijia system was a household registration and local administration system of the Ming Empire. Households were grouped into units responsible for collecting taxes, providing labour service and keeping order.

limes-germanicus.s: The Limes Germanicus was the fortified frontier of the Roman Empire along the Rhine and Danube and the land between them. It consisted of forts, watchtowers, walls and palisades guarding Roman provinces against Germanic peoples.

limes-tripolitanus.s: The Limes Tripolitanus was a Roman frontier zone of forts and fortified farms in Tripolitania, in present-day Libya, developed from about 75 CE. It protected the coastal cities and controlled movement from the desert interior.

limmu.s: The limmu was an Assyrian official whose name was used to identify each year, so that every year was named after its holder. The office rotated among the king and senior officials.

limpopo.s: The Limpopo is a major river of southern Africa, flowing through South Africa, Botswana, Zimbabwe and Mozambique to the Indian Ocean. It marks the southern edge of the Zimbabwe plateau, where Great Zimbabwe and its successor states developed.

linear-elamite.s: Linear Elamite is an ancient script used in Elam in the late third millennium BCE. Kutik-Inshushinak promoted it around 2100 BCE alongside Akkadian cuneiform during the foundation of the Elamite Confederation.

lingua-franca.s: A lingua franca is a language used for communication between speakers of different native languages. Akkadian served this role in the ancient Near East, Aramaic in the Achaemenid Empire, Nahuatl in Mesoamerica under the Aztecs, and Old Malay in the trading world of Srivijaya.

lion-hunt-of-ashurbanipal.s: The Lion Hunt of Ashurbanipal is a series of carved stone reliefs from the palace at Nineveh, dating from the seventh century BCE. They show King Ashurbanipal hunting lions, a royal ritual demonstrating the king's role as protector of order against chaos.

lisbon.s: Lisbon is the capital of Portugal, on the estuary of the Tagus. It was the centre of the Portuguese Empire, from which fleets sailed to Africa, Asia and Brazil and where imperial trade was concentrated.

literary-inquisition.s: The Literary Inquisition refers to the persecution of writers and suppression of books under the Qing Empire, especially in the eighteenth century. Works judged anti-Manchu or seditious were banned or destroyed, and authors and their families could be severely punished.

lithuania.s: Lithuania is a country on the Baltic coast that was the core of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, once one of the largest states in Europe. The Grand Duchy entered a personal union with Poland in 1386 and was joined with it by the Union of Lublin in 1569, forming the…

liu-bang.s: Liu Bang was the founder of the Han Dynasty, ruling as Emperor Gaozu from 202 BCE. A commoner who rose in the revolts against the Qin, he defeated his rival Xiang Yu to unify China.

livonia.s: Livonia is a historical region on the eastern Baltic coast, covering parts of present-day Latvia and Estonia. It was contested by Russia, Poland-Lithuania and Sweden after the Livonian War.

livonian-war.s: The Livonian War was a conflict from 1558 to 1583 over control of Livonia, fought by Russia under Ivan IV against Poland-Lithuania, Sweden and Denmark. The war encouraged the closer union of Poland and Lithuania, which led to the Union of Lublin in 1569 and the formation of…

lodi-dynasty.s: The Lodi dynasty was an Afghan dynasty that ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1451 to 1526, the last of its ruling houses. Its final sultan, Ibrahim Lodi, was defeated and killed by Babur, a Timurid prince, at the First Battle of Panipat in 1526.

lombard-league.s: The Lombard League was an alliance of cities in northern Italy formed in 1167 to resist the authority of the Holy Roman Emperor Frederick Barbarossa. Its forces defeated Barbarossa at the Battle of Legnano in 1176.

lombardy.s: Lombardy is a region of northern Italy centred on Milan, one of the wealthiest parts of the peninsula. It came under Austrian Habsburg rule in the eighteenth century and formed part of the Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia after 1815.

london.s: London is the capital of the United Kingdom, on the River Thames. Founded by the Romans as Londinium, it was a significant city of Roman Britain.

lord-dalhousie.s: Lord Dalhousie was Governor-General of India from 1848 to 1856. Following the Second Anglo-Sikh War, he annexed the Punjab in 1849, bringing the Sikh Empire to an end.

lorraine.s: Lorraine is a region of north-eastern France on the border with Germany, whose name derives from Lotharingia, the share of Lothair II after the division of the Carolingian Empire. It was long contested between French and German rulers.

lotf-ali-khan.s: Lotf Ali Khan was the last ruler of the Zand Empire in Iran. A brave and capable soldier, he resisted the rising Qajar leader Agha Mohammad Khan for several years.

lothair-i.s: Lothair I was the eldest son of Louis the Pious and Carolingian emperor from 840 to 855. He fought his brothers Louis the German and Charles the Bald for control of the Carolingian Empire.

louis-pasteur.s: Louis Pasteur was a nineteenth-century French scientist whose work on microbes, fermentation and vaccines founded modern microbiology. He was among the scientists befriended by Emperor Pedro II of Brazil, who took a keen interest in science.

louis-the-german.s: Louis the German was a son of Louis the Pious and king of East Francia. He fought alongside Charles the Bald against their brother Lothair I in the civil wars after their father's death.

louis-the-pious.s: Louis the Pious was the son and successor of Charlemagne, ruling the Carolingian Empire from 814 to 840. His attempts to arrange the succession among his sons provoked rebellions and civil wars.

louis-xiv.s: Louis XIV was King of France from 1643 to 1715, whose long reign marked the height of royal absolutism. Under his minister Colbert, France expanded its colonies, navy and overseas trading companies, laying foundations of the French Empire.

louisiana.s: Louisiana was a vast French colonial territory in North America covering the Mississippi basin, named after Louis XIV. It was claimed for France in the late seventeenth century and was part of the first French colonial empire.

louvre.s: The Louvre is a former royal palace in Paris and now one of the world's largest art museums. It holds major Mesopotamian antiquities, including the Victory Stele of Naram-Sin of the Akkadian Empire and the stele bearing the Code of Hammurabi of the Babylonian Empire.

low-countries.s: The Low Countries is the coastal region of north-western Europe comprising present-day Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg. Much of it lay within the Holy Roman Empire and later passed to the Habsburgs.

lower-egypt.s: Lower Egypt is the northern part of Egypt, consisting of the Nile Delta and the area around Memphis. Its unification with Upper Egypt was the foundation of the Egyptian state, and pharaohs bore the title of ruler of both lands.

luba-empire.s: The Luba Empire was a Central African state in the Upemba region of the south-eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, flourishing from about the sixteenth to the late nineteenth century. It was built around a sacred kingship and a network of tributary chiefdoms, with…

luba-stools.s: Luba stools are carved wooden seats of authority from the Luba Empire, often supported by a female caryatid figure. They symbolised royal power and the role of women in Luba kingship and memory.

lubeck.s: Lubeck is a port city on the Baltic coast of northern Germany and was the leading city of the Hanseatic League. As a free imperial city of the Holy Roman Empire, it dominated much of the medieval Baltic and North Sea trade.

lublin.s: Lublin is a city in eastern Poland. It gave its name to the Union of Lublin, agreed there in 1569, which joined the Kingdom of Poland and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania into a single Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth.

lucius-cornelius-balbus.s: Lucius Cornelius Balbus was a Roman general and proconsul of Africa. In 19 BCE he led a punitive expedition against the Garamantian Empire, capturing fifteen Garamantian settlements including the capital Garama.

ludwig-wittgenstein.s: Ludwig Wittgenstein was a philosopher born in Vienna in 1889 into one of the wealthiest families of the Austro-Hungarian Empire. He became one of the most influential philosophers of the twentieth century, working mainly in Cambridge.

lufwa-river.s: The Lufwa is a river in the Luba heartland of Central Africa. According to the Luba Empire's profile, the founding ruler Kalala Ilunga extended Luba territory east to the Lufwa River.

lugal-zage-si.s: Lugal-zage-si was a Sumerian king of Umma and Uruk who brought much of Sumer under his rule in the twenty-fourth century BCE. He was defeated and captured by Sargon of Akkad.

lukeni-lua-nimi.s: Lukeni lua Nimi is the traditional founder of the Kingdom of Kongo in the late fourteenth century. According to tradition, he established the capital at Mbanza Kongo and unified surrounding territories through conquest and political integration.

lullubi.s: The Lullubi were a people of the Zagros Mountains on the eastern edge of Mesopotamia. The Akkadian king Naram-Sin defeated them, and the Victory Stele of Naram-Sin shows him ascending a mountain over fallen Lullubi enemies.

lunda-empire.s: The Lunda Empire was a Central African state in the south of the present-day Democratic Republic of the Congo and parts of Angola and Zambia, flourishing from the seventeenth to the nineteenth century. Its kingship drew on Luba political models, and it expanded through a…

luoyang.s: Luoyang is a city in the Yellow River valley of central China and one of China's ancient capitals. Under the Tang Dynasty it served as the eastern capital alongside Chang'an.

lutheranism.s: Lutheranism is the branch of Protestant Christianity based on the teachings of Martin Luther, who launched the Reformation in 1517. Its spread divided the Holy Roman Empire along religious lines and led to wars ended by settlements such as the Peace of Augsburg.

luxor.s: Luxor is a city on the Nile in Upper Egypt, built on the site of ancient Thebes. Its great temple complexes, including Luxor Temple and nearby Karnak, were developed during the Egyptian New Kingdom.

lwena.s: The Lwena, also known as the Luvale, are a people of eastern Angola and north-western Zambia. They were active traders in Central Africa.

lydia.s: Lydia was a kingdom in western Anatolia with its capital at Sardis, famous for its wealth and for early coinage. Its last king, Croesus, was defeated by Cyrus the Great around 547 BCE.

lydians.s: The Lydians were the people of the kingdom of Lydia in western Anatolia. They were known for their cavalry and wealth, and for being among the first to mint coins.

lysimachus.s: Lysimachus was one of the Diadochi, the successors of Alexander the Great, who ruled Thrace and later parts of Asia Minor and Macedon. He was defeated and killed by Seleucus I at the Battle of Corupedium in 281 BCE.

lake-constance.s: Lake Constance is a large lake on the Rhine at the northern foot of the Alps, bordered by Germany, Switzerland and Austria. Its shores were settled by the Alemanni and later filled with monasteries such as Reichenau and Saint Gall, the bishopric of Constance and free imperial…

livonian-brothers-of-the-sword.s: The Livonian Brothers of the Sword were a military order founded in 1202 by Bishop Albert of Riga to conquer pagan Livonia. Over two decades they subdued the Livs, Latgalians and southern Estonians.

liu-yu-qi.s: Liu Yu was a former Song official who surrendered to the Jurchen Jin and was installed by them in 1130 as emperor of a puppet state called Qi, ruling Henan and Shaanxi from Kaifeng. He served as a buffer and attacked the Southern Song, but his campaigns failed.

louis-ii-of-hungary.s: Louis II of Hungary was the Jagiellonian king of Hungary and Bohemia from 1516. Faced with a weak treasury and quarrelling nobles, he could not resist the Ottoman advance.

louis-ii-of-italy.s: Louis II of Italy was the eldest son of Lothair I, king of Italy from 844 and Carolingian emperor from 855. When his father's Middle Francia was divided he received Italy, and he shared Provence with his brother Lothair II.

louis-ii-duke-of-bourbon.s: Louis II, Duke of Bourbon, called the Good Duke, was a French prince who fought in the Hundred Years' War and led a crusade to Mahdia in 1390. His marriage to Anne, heiress of Forez, and his inheritance of Beaujolais greatly enlarged the Bourbon lands, which became one of the…

louis-ii-duke-of-bavaria.s: Louis II, Duke of Bavaria, known as the Strict, was a Wittelsbach duke and Count Palatine of the Rhine. In the first Wittelsbach partition of 1255 he received Upper Bavaria with Munich and the Palatinate, while his brother Henry took Lower Bavaria.

leeward-islands.s: The Leeward Islands are the northern group of the Lesser Antilles in the Caribbean, from the Virgin Islands to Dominica. England settled several of them in the 17th century, and from 1671 the British islands of Saint Kitts, Nevis, Antigua and Montserrat were governed together…

leeward-islands-society-islands.s: The Leeward Islands are the western group of the Society Islands in French Polynesia, including Raiatea, Huahine and Bora Bora. Their chiefdoms stayed independent of the Kingdom of Tahiti, and an Anglo-French declaration of 1847 guaranteed their independence.

louis-ix-of-france.s: Louis IX of France, king from 1226 to 1270, was revered as a model Christian ruler and canonised in 1297. He led the Seventh Crusade to Egypt, where he was captured, then spent years refortifying crusader towns such as Caesarea.

louis-ix-duke-of-bavaria.s: Louis IX, Duke of Bavaria-Landshut, called the Rich, ruled from 1450 to 1479. Like his father Henry XVI and his son George, he drew great wealth from his well-managed duchy.

lake-malawi.s: Lake Malawi, also called Lake Nyasa, is a long lake in the southern part of the East African Rift, bordered by Malawi, Mozambique and Tanzania. Its shores were home to the Maravi states and later to Ngoni, Yao and Swahili rulers who traded ivory and slaves to the coast.

london-missionary-society.s: The London Missionary Society was a Protestant missionary society founded in London in 1795. Its missionaries reached Tahiti and the Society Islands in 1797, southern Africa, where Robert Moffat and David Livingstone worked among the Tswana, and later New Guinea.

lake-van.s: Lake Van is the largest lake in Turkey, a salty soda lake on the high plateau of eastern Anatolia. Its shores were the centre of the Iron Age kingdom of Urartu, whose capital Tushpa stood at Van, and later of the Armenian kingdom of Vaspurakan.

lake-victoria.s: Lake Victoria is the largest lake in Africa, shared by Uganda, Kenya and Tanzania, and the main source of the White Nile. Kingdoms grew on its shores, including Buganda in the north, the Busoga principalities and the Haya kingdoms such as Karagwe and Kianja in the west.

lushunkou.s: Lüshunkou, known to Europeans as Port Arthur, is a port at the tip of the Liaodong peninsula in north-east China. Russia leased it from the Qing in 1898 as an ice-free naval base, prompting Britain to take Weihaiwei.

louis-iv-landgrave-of-thuringia.s: Louis IV was Landgrave of Thuringia from 1217 to 1227, a son of Hermann I, patron of the Wartburg poets. He married Elizabeth of Hungary, who became famous for her charity and was canonised in 1235.

louis-iv-landgrave-of-hesse-marburg.s: Louis IV was Landgrave of Hesse-Marburg from 1567 to 1604, the second son of Philip the Magnanimous, who received about a quarter of Hesse, centred on Marburg and its university, in the division of 1567. A strict Lutheran, he defended orthodoxy against the Calvinist leanings…

leke-dukagjini.s: Lekë Dukagjini was an Albanian nobleman of the Dukagjini family, which ruled lands in northern Albania. A contemporary of Skanderbeg, he fought the Ottomans as part of the League of Lezhë, though he also quarrelled with Skanderbeg, and continued the resistance after…

li-cunxu.s: Li Cunxu was the son of the Shatuo Turk warlord Li Keyong and his successor as Prince of Jin from 908. A gifted soldier, he repeatedly defeated the Later Liang, annexed the Yan of Liu Shouguang in 913 and took most of Hebei.

liu-bei.s: Liu Bei was a warlord of the late Eastern Han who claimed descent from the Han imperial house. With the strategist Zhuge Liang and in alliance with Sun Quan, he defeated Cao Cao at Red Cliffs in 208, then took Jing and Yi provinces.

liu-shouguang.s: Liu Shouguang was a warlord of the late Tang who in 907 imprisoned his father Liu Rengong, military governor of Lulong, and seized Youzhou, near modern Beijing. In 911 he proclaimed himself emperor of Yan, one of the short-lived states of the Five Dynasties period.

louis-botha.s: Louis Botha was a Boer general and statesman. He helped found the Nieuwe Republiek in 1884, rose to command the Transvaal forces in the Second Boer War and afterwards worked for reconciliation with Britain.

louis-riel.s: Louis Riel was a Métis leader of the Red River settlement. When the Hudson's Bay Company's Rupert's Land passed to Canada in 1869 without consulting its people, he formed a provisional government whose negotiations led to the creation of the province of Manitoba in 1870.

louis-xi.s: Louis XI was King of France from 1461 to 1483. He fought the great nobles of the League of the Public Weal and above all Charles the Bold of Burgundy, whose death at Nancy in 1477 allowed him to seize the Duchy of Burgundy, Picardy and Boulogne.

lower-nubia.s: Lower Nubia is the stretch of the Nile valley between the First and Second Cataracts, in southern Egypt and northern Sudan. Home to the A-Group culture, it was repeatedly conquered by Egypt, which ruled it as Wawat under the Viceroy of Kush in the New Kingdom.

lake-titicaca.s: Lake Titicaca is a large freshwater lake in the high Andes on the border of Peru and Bolivia, at about 3,800 metres. Its shores were the heartland of the Tiwanaku civilisation and later of Aymara kingdoms such as the Lupaca and Pacajes.

late-classic-period.s: The Late Classic is the period of Maya history from about 600 to 900 CE, when lowland Maya civilisation reached its height. Dozens of royal courts such as Tikal, Calakmul, Yaxchilan and Bonampak competed and built temples, palaces and carved monuments with hieroglyphic texts.

leszek-the-black.s: Leszek the Black was a Piast duke who received Sieradz on the division of his father Casimir I's lands in 1267. In 1279 he inherited Kraków and Sandomierz and became High Duke of Poland.

li-keyong.s: Li Keyong was a Shatuo Turkic military leader in the last decades of the Tang dynasty. His cavalry drove Huang Chao's rebels from Chang'an in 883, and the Tang made him Prince of Jin, ruling from Taiyuan.

liu-yao.s: Liu Yao was a Xiongnu general and the last emperor of Han Zhao. With Shi Le he captured the Jin capitals Luoyang in 311 and Chang'an in 316.

lothair-ii.s: Lothair II was the second son of Emperor Lothair I and received the northern part of Middle Francia at the Treaty of Prüm in 855, a kingdom later named Lotharingia after him. His long attempt to divorce his wife Theutberga embroiled him with the papacy.

louis-rudolph-duke-of-brunswick-luneburg.s: Louis Rudolph was a younger son of Duke Anthony Ulrich of Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel, who gave him Blankenburg in the Harz. In 1707 Emperor Joseph I raised Blankenburg to a principality for him.

louis-xvi.s: Louis XVI was King of France from 1774. He supported the American War of Independence, which worsened the crown's debts, and in 1789 he summoned the Estates-General, opening the French Revolution.

league-of-the-ten-jurisdictions.s: The League of the Ten Jurisdictions was an alliance of communities in north-eastern Graubünden, formed in 1436 after the death of the last Count of Toggenburg. With the League of God's House and the Grey League it made up the Three Leagues, the Free State of the Grisons, an…

latvian-war-of-independence.s: The Latvian War of Independence was fought by the Republic of Latvia against the Latvian Socialist Soviet Republic, German Freikorps and the West Russian Volunteer Army of Pavel Bermondt-Avalov. With Estonian help, Latvian forces won at Cēsis in 1919 and drove the Bermontians…

lands-of-the-crown-of-saint-stephen.n: Lands of the Crown of Saint Stephen
lands-of-the-crown-of-saint-stephen.s: The Lands of the Crown of Saint Stephen were the territories joined to the Kingdom of Hungary under its Holy Crown, including Croatia, Slavonia and, at times, Transylvania. The idea of the crown as the bearer of sovereignty bound these lands to the Hungarian king while they…

lake-bolsena.s: Lake Bolsena is a crater lake in northern Lazio, Italy, the largest lake of volcanic origin in Europe. In Etruscan times its shores belonged to the territory of Volsinii, and the federal sanctuary of the Etruscans, the Fanum Voltumnae, lay nearby.

lake-garda.s: Lake Garda is the largest lake in Italy, lying at the foot of the Alps between Lombardy, Veneto and Trentino. Romans built villas on its shores, notably at Sirmione, and in the Middle Ages its towns were contested by Verona, Brescia and Milan before Venice ruled most of them…

lake-sevan.s: Lake Sevan is the largest lake in Armenia and the Caucasus, lying at about 1,900 metres above sea level. Urartian kings conquered the tribes around it in the 8th century BCE and left inscriptions on its shores, and the monastery of Sevanavank was founded on its peninsula in 874.

le-loi.s: Lê Lợi was a landowner from Lam Son in Thanh Hoa who led a ten-year war of resistance, from 1418, against the Ming occupation of Vietnam. After his victory at Chi Lang in 1427 the Ming withdrew, and in 1428 he proclaimed himself emperor as Lê Thái Tổ, founding the Later Le…

le-mans.s: Le Mans is a city on the Sarthe in north-western France. As Vindinum it was the chief town of the Gallic Cenomani, and its late Roman walls are among the best preserved in France.

leon-ii-of-abkhazia.s: Leon II was the ruler of Abasgia who, around 778, threw off Byzantine authority with the help of his mother's kin, the Khazars, took the title of king and joined Abasgia with Egrisi to form the Kingdom of Abkhazia. He moved his seat to Kutaisi, and his dynasty ruled western…

leonard-wood.s: Leonard Wood was a United States army doctor and general who commanded the Rough Riders with Theodore Roosevelt in 1898. He was military governor of Cuba from 1899 to 1902, governor of the Moro Province in the southern Philippines from 1903 to 1906, and army chief of staff…

leonce-lagarde.s: Léonce Lagarde was a French colonial administrator who became commandant of Obock in 1884 and extended French influence by treaties with the Sultanate of Tadjoura and Issa Somali clans. He founded the port of Djibouti and governed French Somaliland until 1899.

leopold-iii-margrave-of-austria.s: Leopold III was the Babenberg margrave of Austria from 1095 to 1136. He married Agnes, daughter of Emperor Henry IV, and supported her brother Henry V against their father.

leopold-iii-duke-of-austria.s: Leopold III was a Habsburg duke of Austria. By the Treaty of Neuberg of 1379 he and his brother Albert III divided the family lands, Leopold taking Styria, Carinthia, Carniola, Tyrol and the western territories later called Further Austria, founding the Leopoldine line.

little-zab.s: The Little Zab is a river that rises in the Zagros mountains of north-western Iran and flows south-west through Iraqi Kurdistan to join the Tigris. With the Great Zab to the north it framed the Assyrian heartland around Arbela, later the Kingdom of Adiabene, while ancient…

li-gao.s: Li Gao was a Chinese official of the Longxi Li family who governed Dunhuang under Northern Liang and in 400 declared himself duke, founding Western Liang, the westernmost of the Sixteen Kingdoms. He moved his capital to Jiuquan in 405 and kept Chinese learning alive on the far…

li-gui.s: Li Gui was a wealthy notable of Wuwei in the Hexi Corridor who was chosen by local leaders in 617, as the Sui dynasty collapsed, to resist the rebel Xue Ju. He proclaimed himself prince and then emperor of Liang.

li-maozhen.s: Li Maozhen, born Song Wentong, was a Tang general granted the imperial surname Li, who became military governor of Fengxiang west of Chang'an and was made Prince of Qi. For a time he held the emperor Zhaozong.

liu-chong.s: Liu Chong was a Shatuo general, brother of Liu Zhiyuan, founder of the Later Han, who governed Hedong from Taiyuan. When Guo Wei overthrew the Later Han in 951, Liu Chong proclaimed himself emperor at Taiyuan, founding the Northern Han as a client of the Khitan Liao dynasty.

liu-zhiyuan.s: Liu Zhiyuan was a Shatuo general who governed Taiyuan under the Later Jin. When the Khitan Liao army took Kaifeng in 947 and ended that dynasty, he proclaimed himself emperor, and as the Khitan withdrew he entered Kaifeng and founded the Later Han, the shortest of the Five…

lon-nol.s: Lon Nol was a Cambodian general and politician who served as defence minister and prime minister under Norodom Sihanouk. On 18 March 1970, while Sihanouk was abroad, he and the national assembly deposed him, and Lon Nol proclaimed the Khmer Republic, becoming its president in…

louis-xii-of-france.s: Louis XII, born at Blois as duke of Orléans, became king of France in 1498. He had his first marriage annulled to marry Anne of Brittany, widow of Charles VIII, keeping Brittany tied to the crown.

louis-xiii-of-france.s: Louis XIII, son of Henry IV, was king of France from 1610. In 1620 he united Béarn and Lower Navarre with the French crown and restored Catholicism there.

lower-burma.s: Lower Burma is the southern, coastal part of Myanmar, centred on the Irrawaddy delta and the cities of Pegu and Rangoon. It was long the land of Mon kingdoms such as Hanthawaddy, often at war with the Burman rulers of Upper Burma.

lu-guang.s: Lü Guang was a Di general of Former Qin whom the emperor Fu Jian sent to the Tarim Basin in 382. He took Kucha in 384 and carried off the Buddhist monk and translator Kumarajiva.

lucas-meyer.s: Lucas Meyer was a Boer leader who in 1884 led volunteers, among them the young Louis Botha, to back Dinuzulu in the Zulu civil war, in return claiming a large tract of Zululand. There they founded the Nieuwe Republiek with its capital at Vryheid, and Meyer served as its…

laws-in-wales-acts-1535-and-1542.s: The Laws in Wales Acts were statutes of Henry VIII that annexed Wales to the Kingdom of England. They abolished the marcher lordships, created new shires such as Glamorgan, Brecknockshire and Pembrokeshire, gave Wales seats in Parliament and applied English law.

leopold-i-holy-roman-emperor.s: Leopold I was Holy Roman Emperor from 1658 to 1705. His reign saw the Ottoman siege of Vienna in 1683 and the Great Turkish War, in which the Habsburgs reconquered Hungary, and long wars against Louis XIV.

louis-iv-holy-roman-emperor.s: Louis IV, called the Bavarian, was a Wittelsbach duke elected King of Germany in 1314 and crowned emperor in Rome in 1328 without papal consent. He defeated his rival Frederick the Fair at Mühldorf in 1322 and fought a long struggle with the Avignon popes.

la-navidad.s: La Navidad was the first European settlement in the Americas, built on the north coast of Hispaniola by Christopher Columbus at Christmas 1492 from the timbers of the wrecked Santa María. Columbus left some 39 men there, in the territory of the Taíno chief Guacanagarí of Marién.

la-paz.s: La Paz is a city in the Andes of western Bolivia, founded by the Spanish in 1548 and today the seat of Bolivia's government. Its uprising of July 1809, following that of Chuquisaca, was among the first movements towards independence in Spanish South America.

la-paz-baja-california-sur.s: La Paz is a port city on the Gulf of California and the capital of the Mexican state of Baja California Sur. Spanish attempts to settle its bay began with Hernán Cortés in 1535.

lady-six-sky.s: Lady Six Sky was a princess of Dos Pilas who arrived at Naranjo in 682 CE and restored its royal dynasty after defeats by Caracol. She governed for her young son K'ak' Tiliw Chan Chaak and was shown on monuments in the guise of a warrior ruler.

lake-ngami.s: Lake Ngami is a shallow, often seasonal lake in north-western Botswana, fed by overflow from the Okavango delta. David Livingstone's party reached it in 1849, bringing it to European attention.

lake-peipus.s: Lake Peipus is a large lake on the border between Estonia and Russia. In the Middle Ages it marked the frontier between the lands of the Estonians, conquered by the Livonian crusaders in the 13th century, and the Novgorod Republic.

lake-urmia.s: Lake Urmia is a large salt lake in north-western Iran, between the provinces of East and West Azerbaijan. In the early 1st millennium BCE the Mannaeans lived on its southern shores, and the region was contested between Assyria and Urartu and raided by Scythians.

lalitaditya-muktapida.s: Lalitaditya Muktapida was the most powerful king of the Karkota dynasty of Kashmir, ruling in the first half of the 8th century. Kalhana's Rajatarangini describes far-reaching campaigns, and he defeated Yashovarman of Kannauj.

lancaster-house.s: Lancaster House is a 19th-century mansion near St James's Palace in London used by the British government for conferences. In the era of decolonisation it hosted talks on the constitutions of many colonies, including the Kenya conferences of 1960–1963.

louis-i-grand-duke-of-hesse.n: Louis I, Grand Duke of Hesse
louis-i-grand-duke-of-hesse.s: Louis I was the last landgrave of Hesse-Darmstadt, as Louis X from 1790, and the first grand duke of Hesse. Allied with Napoleon, he joined the Confederation of the Rhine in 1806 and took the grand-ducal title.

louis-v-landgrave-of-hesse-darmstadt.s: Louis V was landgrave of Hesse-Darmstadt from 1596 to 1626. A Lutheran loyal to the Habsburg emperors, he founded the University of Giessen in 1607 and gained much of the disputed Marburg inheritance during the Thirty Years' War.

lat-sukaabe-fall.s: Lat Sukaabe Fall was a Wolof ruler who united the thrones of Cayor and Baol in Senegal around 1697, taking the combined title of damel-teigne. He strengthened royal power with firearms and slave soldiers and dealt with the French trading posts on the coast.

lateran-treaty.s: The Lateran Treaty was signed on 11 February 1929 by Cardinal Pietro Gasparri for Pope Pius XI and Benito Mussolini for the Kingdom of Italy. It settled the Roman Question, the dispute that had followed Italy's seizure of Rome in 1870, by creating the independent state of…

latin-war.s: The Latin War of 340–338 BCE was fought between Rome and its former allies of the Latin League, joined by the Campanians and Volsci. Rome won and in 338 BCE dissolved the league, making separate treaties with each town.

le-dai-hanh.s: Le Dai Hanh, born Le Hoan, was the founder of the Early Le dynasty of Vietnam, ruling from 980 to 1005. A commander under the Dinh dynasty, he took the throne with the backing of the queen mother Duong Van Nga.

lee-kuan-yew.s: Lee Kuan Yew was the first prime minister of Singapore, holding office from 1959 to 1990. As leader of the People's Action Party he took Singapore into Malaysia in 1963 and, after its separation in 1965, led it as an independent state.

leo-sgouros.s: Leo Sgouros was a Byzantine Greek magnate who ruled Nauplia, Argos and Corinth in the years around the Fourth Crusade. Taking advantage of weakening imperial authority, he extended his power into central Greece.

leopold-i-prince-of-anhalt-dessau.s: Leopold I, Prince of Anhalt-Dessau, known as the Old Dessauer, ruled the principality from 1693 to 1747 and served as a Prussian field marshal. He drilled the Prussian infantry, introducing the iron ramrod and cadenced marching.

leopold-i-prince-of-lippe.s: Leopold I was count and, from 1789, the first prince of Lippe, a small state in north-western Germany. He took up the princely rank granted to the family earlier in the century, turning the County of Lippe-Detmold into the Principality of Lippe.

lesser-poland.s: Lesser Poland is a historical region of south-eastern Poland centred on Kraków and the upper Vistula. Added to the Piast realm by the 990s, it became the political heart of the kingdom, with Kraków as the royal capital.

letsie-iii.s: Letsie III is the king of Lesotho. He first came to the throne in 1990, after the military government exiled his father Moshoeshoe II, stood aside when his father was restored in 1995, and became king again after Moshoeshoe's death in 1996.

levon-ter-petrosyan.s: Levon Ter-Petrosyan was the first president of independent Armenia, serving from 1991 to 1998. A philologist and a leader of the Karabakh Committee, he became chairman of the Armenian Supreme Council in 1990 and led the country through independence and the First Karabakh War.

li-bian.s: Li Bian, born Xu Zhigao, was the founder of the Southern Tang, one of the Ten Kingdoms of China. Adopted son of the regent Xu Wen, he took the throne of Wu in 937 and in 939 adopted the surname Li, claiming descent from the Tang imperial family.

li-congke.s: Li Congke was the last emperor of the Later Tang in the Five Dynasties period, reigning from 934 to 937. An adopted son of Emperor Mingzong, he seized the throne from Mingzong's son.

li-xiong.s: Li Xiong was the founding emperor of Cheng Han, one of the Sixteen Kingdoms, in Sichuan. Son of the refugee leader Li Te, he took Chengdu in 304 and proclaimed himself emperor of Cheng in 306.

li-yuanhao.s: Li Yuanhao was the founder and first emperor of Western Xia, the Tangut state of north-western China. In 1028, while still heir, he captured Ganzhou from the Uyghurs, and in 1038 he proclaimed himself emperor of Great Xia.

liang-hongzhi.s: Liang Hongzhi was a Chinese politician who had served the Beiyang government before collaborating with Japan. In March 1938 he became head of the Reformed Government of the Republic of China, a Japanese-sponsored regime at Nanjing.

liang-shidu.s: Liang Shidu was a local officer in Shuofang, on the northern bend of the Yellow River, who killed the Sui governor in 617 and proclaimed himself emperor of Liang. As a client of the Eastern Turks he held out against the Tang longer than any other regime born of the Sui collapse.

ligdan-khan.s: Ligdan Khan was the last great khan of the Northern Yuan, ruling the Chahar Mongols from 1604. He tried to restore central authority over the Mongols by force and patronised Tibetan Buddhism, sponsoring a Mongolian translation of the Kanjur.

liu-chang.s: Liu Chang was the last emperor of Southern Han, one of the Ten Kingdoms, ruling from Guangzhou from 958 to 971. His reign was notorious for misrule, with thousands of eunuchs dominating the government.

liu-chengyou.s: Liu Chengyou was the second and last emperor of the Later Han in the Five Dynasties period. He succeeded his father Liu Zhiyuan in 948 as a youth guided by senior ministers and generals.

liu-futong.s: Liu Futong was a leader of the Red Turban rebellion against the Yuan dynasty in China. After Han Shantong was killed in 1351, he continued the revolt, and in 1355 he enthroned Han's son Han Lin'er as emperor of a restored Song at Bozhou.

liu-shan.s: Liu Shan was the second and last emperor of Shu Han in the Three Kingdoms period, reigning from 223 to 263. For his first decade the chancellor Zhuge Liang governed on his behalf and led campaigns against Cao Wei.

liu-yuan.s: Liu Yuan was a Southern Xiongnu noble, descended from the shanyus and educated in the Chinese classics, who founded Han Zhao, the first of the Sixteen Kingdoms. He rebelled during the War of the Eight Princes, proclaiming himself king of Han in 304 and emperor in 308.

lough-leane.s: Lough Leane is the largest of the Lakes of Killarney in County Kerry, south-western Ireland. In the early Middle Ages it gave its name to the Eoganacht Locha Léin, a branch of the Munster dynasties who ruled the kingdom of Iarmumu around it.

louis-mountbatten.s: Louis Mountbatten was a British naval officer who became the last Viceroy of India in 1947. He brought forward the transfer of power and oversaw the partition of British India into India and Pakistan in August 1947.

lough-erne.s: Lough Erne is a pair of connected lakes on the River Erne in County Fermanagh, Northern Ireland. Ptolemy's Erdini are usually placed around it.

louis-archinard.s: Louis Archinard was a French army officer who led the conquest of much of the western Sudan, now Mali. As commander of French Sudan from 1888 he took Segou in 1890 and campaigned against Ahmadu Tall of the Toucouleur Empire and Samori Toure.

louis-bonaparte.s: Louis Bonaparte was a younger brother of Napoleon, who made him king of Holland in 1806. Louis learned Dutch, moved the court to Amsterdam and tried to protect Dutch interests, which brought him into conflict with his brother.

louis-i-of-hungary.s: Louis I of Hungary, known as Louis the Great, was king of Hungary and Croatia from 1342 and king of Poland from 1370 until his death in 1382. A member of the Angevin dynasty, he forced Venice to give up Dalmatia in 1358 and made Hungary a leading power of central Europe.

louis-of-mousson.s: Louis of Mousson was an 11th-century nobleman who held the county of Montbéliard and, through his marriage to Sophie of Bar around 1038, the county of Bar. Their descendants, the house of Montbéliard-Bar, ruled Bar as a separate principality between Champagne and Lorraine.

louis-i-count-of-flanders.s: Louis I, known as Louis of Nevers, was count of Flanders, Nevers and Rethel from 1322 until his death at the Battle of Crécy in 1346. Firmly allied with the French crown, he faced the Flemish peasant revolt of 1323–1328 and later the rising of Ghent under Jacob van Artevelde.

louis-xv.s: Louis XV was king of France from 1715 to 1774, succeeding his great-grandfather Louis XIV at the age of five. His reign saw French defeat in the Seven Years' War and the loss of most of New France.

louis-gustave-binger.s: Louis-Gustave Binger was a French officer and explorer of West Africa. Between 1887 and 1889 he travelled from the Niger bend to the Gulf of Guinea by way of Kong, signing treaties that extended French influence in the interior.

louisiana-purchase.s: The Louisiana Purchase was the acquisition by the United States of France's territory of Louisiana in 1803 for about 15 million dollars. Spain had returned the colony to France shortly before, and Napoleon sold it after failing to hold Saint-Domingue.

luang-prabang.s: Luang Prabang is a city on the Mekong in northern Laos, the early royal capital of Lan Xang and later the seat of the Kingdom of Luang Phrabang, formed when Lan Xang split in 1707. Under French rule from 1893 its kings kept their thrones as a protectorate.

luchino-visconti-lord-of-milan.s: Luchino Visconti was lord of Milan from 1339 until his death in 1349, ruling jointly with his brother Giovanni, archbishop of Milan. He greatly enlarged Visconti power in northern Italy, acquiring cities including Asti, Parma and Alessandria in the 1340s.

luis-jose-de-orbegoso.s: Luis José de Orbegoso was a Peruvian general and president of Peru from 1833. Facing rebellion, he invited the Bolivian president Andrés de Santa Cruz into Peru in 1835, which led to the creation of the Peru-Bolivian Confederation.

ly-nam-de.s: Ly Nam De, born Ly Bi, led a rising against the Liang dynasty's rule of Jiaozhou in northern Vietnam. By 544 he had expelled the Liang officials and proclaimed himself emperor of the south, naming his state Van Xuan and founding the Early Ly dynasty.

ly-phat-tu.s: Ly Phat Tu was the last ruler of the Early Ly dynasty in northern Vietnam, holding power from 571 to 602. He took the throne from Trieu Quang Phuc and held the Red River delta through a mix of warfare and negotiation.

london-conference-of-1912-1913.s: The London Conference of 1912–1913 was a meeting of the ambassadors of the six great powers in London, chaired by Sir Edward Grey, to settle the outcome of the First Balkan War. In July 1913 it recognised Albania as an independent principality under great-power guarantee, but…

lothair-iii-holy-roman-emperor.s: Lothair III, Holy Roman Emperor, was Duke of Saxony from 1106, King of Germany from 1125 and emperor from 1133. As duke he granted Holstein and Stormarn to Adolf I of Schauenburg in 1111 and encouraged expansion against the Slavs east of the Elbe.

legio-ii-augusta.s: Legio II Augusta was a Roman legion that took part in the invasion of Britain in 43 CE under the future emperor Vespasian, who captured more than twenty hillforts in the south-west. It built a fortress at Exeter around 55 and later moved to Caerleon in Wales, its base for two…

la-centinela.s: La Centinela is an archaeological site in the Chincha valley on the south coast of Peru, the capital of the Chincha lordship from around 1000. Its adobe pyramids, plazas and residential compounds reflect a society of farmers, fishermen and long-distance merchants.

la-maddukelleng.s: La Maddukelleng was a Bugis noble of Wajo in South Sulawesi who spent years in exile in eastern Borneo, where he built up a fleet and following. Returning in 1735, he became arung matowa, the elected ruler of Wajo, and fought the neighbouring kingdom of Bone and the Dutch East…

la-mappanyukki.s: La Mappanyukki was a Bugis prince of the royal house of Gowa who became king of Bone when the Dutch restored the kingdom in 1931. After the Second World War he declared Bone's support for the Indonesian Republic, and the Dutch removed him in 1946.

la-patiware-daeng-parabung.s: La Patiware Daeng Parabung was the datu, or ruler, of the Bugis kingdom of Luwu in South Sulawesi. In 1605 he accepted Islam from Minangkabau preachers, taking the name Sultan Muhammad, and became one of the first rulers in South Sulawesi to convert.

la-pawawoi-karaeng-sigeri.s: La Pawawoi Karaeng Sigeri was king of Bone in South Sulawesi from 1895 to 1905. He refused Dutch demands for control of Bone's ports and revenues, and in 1905 a Dutch expedition conquered the kingdom.

la-tene-culture.s: The La Tène culture was the late Iron Age culture of Celtic Europe, from about 450 BCE until the Roman conquest. It is named after the site of La Tène on Lake Neuchâtel in Switzerland, where large numbers of weapons and other offerings were found.

labib-al-amiri.s: Labib al-Amiri was a slav freedman of the Amirid household who seized Tortosa after the Caliphate of Córdoba collapsed in civil war in 1009, founding the taifa of Tortosa. He is reported to have shared for a time in the government of Valencia with the freedmen Mubarak and…

lachlan-macquarie.s: Lachlan Macquarie was a Scottish army officer who served as Governor of New South Wales from 1810 to 1821, after the deposition of William Bligh. He restored order, built roads, churches and public buildings and sponsored the first crossing of the Blue Mountains.

ladislaus-kan.s: Ladislaus Kán was voivode of Transylvania from about 1294 until his death in 1315 and one of the great oligarchs of Hungary at the end of the Árpád dynasty. He ruled Transylvania almost as an independent prince and in 1307 seized the Holy Crown from the claimant Otto of…

ladislaus-of-naples.s: Ladislaus of the Anjou-Durazzo house was King of Naples from 1386 until his death in 1414. He also claimed the crown of Hungary against Sigismund of Luxembourg and was crowned at Zadar in 1403, rewarding supporters such as Hrvoje Vukčić Hrvatinić.

lady-kabal-xook.s: Lady K'ab'al Xook was the principal wife of Itzamnaaj B'ahlam, the Shield Jaguar king of the Maya city of Yaxchilan, in the late 7th and early 8th centuries. She commissioned the carved Lintels 24 to 26 of Structure 23, which show her drawing blood from her tongue and…

lady-kabel.s: Lady K'abel was a princess of the Kaan dynasty of Calakmul who married K'inich B'ahlam II, king of Waka' (El Perú) in Guatemala, in the 7th century. She held the title kaloomte', supreme warrior, ranking above her husband, and sealed the alliance between the two cities.

lady-of-cao.s: The Lady of Cao is the name given to a Moche woman of high rank whose richly furnished tomb was found in 2006 at Huaca Cao Viejo, part of the El Brujo complex on the north coast of Peru. Her tattooed mummy was buried around 450 CE with gold and copper ornaments and war clubs,…

laguna-de-bay.s: Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, lying south-east of Manila on Luzon and draining into Manila Bay through the Pasig River. Before Spanish rule its shores were settled by Tagalog communities that farmed rice, fished and traded with Chinese merchants.

lai-chau.s: Lai Chau is a town on the Black River in the mountains of north-western Vietnam, long the seat of the Tai chiefly family of Deo. Under French rule it was the base of Deo Van Long and capital of the Tai Federation from 1948 to 1954.

lajos-kossuth.s: Lajos Kossuth was a Hungarian lawyer, journalist and statesman, the leading figure of the Hungarian Revolution of 1848. As finance minister and head of the National Defence Committee he organised resistance to the Habsburgs, and after the Declaration of Independence of April…

lake-atitlan.s: Lake Atitlán is a deep crater lake in the highlands of south-western Guatemala, surrounded by volcanoes. From about the 13th century its southern shore was the heartland of the Tz'utujil Maya kingdom, whose capital stood at Chuitinamit near Santiago Atitlán.

lake-copais.s: Lake Copais was a large shallow lake in Boeotia, central Greece, fed by the Cephissus river. In the Mycenaean period the people of Orchomenos drained much of it with dykes, canals and channels into natural sinkholes, one of the great engineering works of the Bronze Age.

lake-erhai.s: Lake Erhai is a large highland lake in western Yunnan, China, lying beneath the Cang mountains. The plain beside it was the centre of the six chiefdoms united as Nanzhao in the 8th century and of the later Dali Kingdom, whose capitals, Taihe and Yangjumie, stood near its…

lake-fitri.s: Lake Fitri is a shallow freshwater lake in the Sahel of central Chad, whose size varies greatly with the rains. It was the homeland of the Bulala, whose rulers fought the Sayfawa kings of Kanem in the 14th century and drove them west to Bornu.

lake-guatavita.s: Lake Guatavita is a small circular lake in the eastern Andes of Colombia, north-east of Bogotá, sacred to the Muisca. In the installation of a new ruler, the chief was covered in gold dust and made offerings of gold on a raft in the lake, the origin of the legend of El Dorado.

lake-lucerne.s: Lake Lucerne is a lake in central Switzerland bordered by the four forest cantons of Uri, Schwyz, Unterwalden and Lucerne, from which its German name derives. It linked these communities by water and lay on the route to the Gotthard Pass.

lake-mjosa.s: Lake Mjøsa is the largest lake in Norway, lying in the inland districts north of Oslo. Its fertile shores made Hedmark, Toten and Hadeland among the richest farming lands of medieval Norway, and petty kingdoms there played a part in the sagas of Halfdan the Black, Harald…

lake-nicaragua.s: Lake Nicaragua is the largest lake in Central America, connected to the Caribbean by the San Juan River. Before the Spanish conquest the Nahua-speaking Nicarao lived on the isthmus of Rivas between the lake and the Pacific.

lake-ohrid.s: Lake Ohrid is one of the oldest and deepest lakes in Europe, on the border between North Macedonia and Albania. Greek writers placed the Illyrian Enchelei, the eel people, near its shores.

lake-peten-itza.s: Lake Petén Itzá is a lake in the Petén lowlands of northern Guatemala and the setting of several Maya polities. Motul de San José, seat of the Classic Ik' kingdom, stood on its northern side, and in the Postclassic the Itza capital Nojpetén occupied an island in the lake, with…

lake-prile.s: Lake Prile, the Roman Lacus Prilius, was a coastal lagoon in southern Etruria near modern Grosseto, fed by the Ombrone and once open to the sea. The Etruscan cities of Vetulonia and Rusellae stood on hills above its shores and used it as a harbour.

lake-skadar.s: Lake Skadar, also called Lake Scutari or Lake Shkodër, is the largest lake in the Balkans, lying on the border of Montenegro and Albania. Its shores and the town of Shkodër formed the core of medieval Zeta, ruled from the 14th century by the Balšić family and then by the…

lakhajirajsinhji-ii.s: Lakhajirajsinhji II was Thakore Sahib of Rajkot, a princely state in Kathiawar in western India, from 1907 until his death in 1930. A reforming ruler, he set up a representative assembly in Rajkot in the 1920s and supported public works and education.

lam-son.s: Lam Sơn is a village in Thanh Hóa province in northern Vietnam, the home of the landowner Lê Lợi. From there he launched the Lam Sơn uprising in 1418 against Ming rule over Jiaozhi Province, a ten-year war that ended with the Ming withdrawal in 1427.

lao-chakkaraj.s: Lao Chakkaraj is the legendary founder of the ruling line of Ngoenyang, the Tai principality on the upper Mekong around Chiang Saen. Northern Thai chronicles place him in the 7th century and describe him as descending from the heavens, but these early dates rest on legend.

lars-porsenna.s: Lars Porsenna was an Etruscan king of Clusium (modern Chiusi) who, in Roman tradition, attacked Rome around 508 BCE after the expulsion of its last king, Tarquinius Superbus. Roman legends of Horatius at the bridge, Mucius Scaevola and Cloelia are set during his siege.

lars-tolumnius.s: Lars Tolumnius was king of the Etruscan city of Veii in the late 5th century BCE. Roman tradition says he incited the Roman colony of Fidenae to revolt and had Roman envoys killed, and that he was slain in single combat by Aulus Cornelius Cossus, who dedicated his armour as…

las-khorey.s: Las Khorey, or Laasqoray, is a port town on the Gulf of Aden coast of the Sanaag region in northern Somalia. It was the main centre of the Warsangali Sultanate, whose gerads traded livestock, frankincense and other goods across the gulf to Arabia.

lat-dior.s: Lat Dior Diop was Damel, or king, of the Wolof kingdom of Cayor in present-day Senegal, ruling at intervals between 1862 and 1886. He became a Muslim and resisted French expansion, above all the railway from Dakar to Saint-Louis that crossed his territory.

late-preclassic.s: The Late Preclassic is the period of Mesoamerican, and especially Maya, history from about 400 BCE to 250 CE. In it the first large Maya cities emerged, with monumental temple platforms, early writing and divine kingship, at sites such as El Mirador, Tikal and Kaminaljuyu in…

latin-christendom.s: Latin Christendom is the community of Christian peoples in western and central Europe who followed the Roman pope and used Latin in worship and learning, as distinct from the Greek-speaking Orthodox world. Its expansion in the 10th century brought in new realms such as Poland…

latvian-riflemen.s: The Latvian Riflemen were Latvian units formed in the Russian Imperial Army in 1915 to defend Latvia against Germany. After heavy losses many turned to the Bolsheviks, and in 1917–1918 the Red Latvian Riflemen became one of the most reliable forces of the Soviet regime.

laurens-storm-van-s-gravesande.s: Laurens Storm van 's Gravesande was a Dutch colonial administrator, commander and later director-general of Essequibo from 1743 to 1772 for the Dutch West India Company. In 1745–1746 he opened the neighbouring Demerara river to settlement, granting land to planters, many of…

lavrentiy-beria.s: Lavrentiy Beria was a Georgian Bolshevik and Soviet security chief. He led the Communist Party of the Transcaucasian SFSR and of Georgia from the early 1930s, carrying out the purges there, and in 1938 became head of the NKVD under Stalin, running the Gulag and mass repressions.

lazaro-cardenas.s: Lázaro Cárdenas was president of Mexico from 1934 to 1940. A general of the Revolution, he carried out the largest land reform in Mexican history, distributing millions of hectares as ejidos, and supported organised labour.

le-chieu-thong.s: Lê Chiêu Thống was the last emperor of Vietnam's Later Lê dynasty, reigning from 1786 to 1789. When the Tây Sơn overthrew the Trịnh lords and took Thăng Long, he appealed to the Qing for help.

le-duan.s: Lê Duẩn was a Vietnamese communist leader who served as first secretary, later general secretary, of the Communist Party from 1960 until his death in 1986. He was the main architect of the war to reunify Vietnam by force and led the country after Ho Chi Minh's death, through…

le-long-dinh.s: Lê Long Đĩnh was the last ruler of Vietnam's Early Lê dynasty, reigning from 1005 to 1009 after killing his brother in the succession struggle that followed the death of their father Lê Đại Hành. Vietnamese chronicles remember him as cruel and so ill that he held audience…

le-thanh-tong.s: Lê Thánh Tông was emperor of Vietnam's Later Lê dynasty from 1460 to 1497, its most celebrated ruler. He built a Confucian bureaucratic state with regular civil service examinations and reorganised provincial government.

leabua-jonathan.s: Leabua Jonathan was the first prime minister of Lesotho, leading the Basotho National Party from independence in 1966. When he was losing the 1970 election he annulled it, suspended the constitution and ruled by decree, sidelining King Moshoeshoe II.

leander-starr-jameson.s: Leander Starr Jameson was a Scottish doctor and associate of Cecil Rhodes who served as administrator for the British South Africa Company in Mashonaland and led the conquest of the Ndebele Kingdom in 1893. In 1895–1896 he led the failed Jameson Raid on the South African…

lee-hsien-loong.s: Lee Hsien Loong is a Singaporean politician, the eldest son of Lee Kuan Yew, who served as the country's third prime minister from 2004 to 2024 as leader of the People's Action Party. His government oversaw Singapore's growth as a centre of finance and technology and its…

leif-erikson.s: Leif Erikson was a Norse explorer, son of Erik the Red, the founder of the Norse settlements in Greenland. According to the Icelandic sagas he sailed from Greenland around 1000 to lands he called Helluland, Markland and Vinland, making him one of the first Europeans to reach…

lelantine-war.s: The Lelantine War was a conflict between the Euboean cities of Chalcis and Eretria over the fertile Lelantine plain that lay between them, fought around the late 8th or early 7th century BCE. Thucydides said it drew allies from much of the Greek world, making it the first war…

leo-gabalas.s: Leo Gabalas was a Byzantine Greek magnate who seized Rhodes and nearby islands after the Fourth Crusade broke up the Byzantine Empire in 1204. He ruled them as an independent lord with the title of Caesar, recognising the Empire of Nicaea only loosely and making a treaty with…

leo-i-king-of-armenia.s: Leo I, called the Magnificent, was the Rubenid prince of Armenian Cilicia from 1187 (as Leo II) and its first king from 1198 to 1219. He secured a crown from the Holy Roman Emperor Henry VI and Pope Celestine III and was crowned at Tarsus, turning the principality into a kingdom.

leo-i-of-galicia.s: Leo I of Galicia, Lev Danylovych, was a son of King Daniel of Galicia and ruled the Kingdom of Galicia–Volhynia from 1264, uniting most of its lands by 1269. He founded or developed the city of Lviv, which bears his name, and moved his capital there.

leon-mba.s: Léon M'ba was a Gabonese politician who led Gabon to independence from France on 17 August 1960 and became its first president. He kept close economic and military ties with France and built a one-party state.

leonard-calvert.s: Leonard Calvert was the first proprietary governor of the Province of Maryland, the younger brother of Cecil Calvert, 2nd Baron Baltimore. In 1634 he led the first settlers aboard the Ark and the Dove to St Mary's City on the lower Potomac.

leonard-woolley.s: Sir Leonard Woolley was a British archaeologist best known for excavating Ur in southern Iraq from 1922 to 1934. There he uncovered the Royal Cemetery, with the tomb of Queen Puabi, the Standard of Ur and the golden helmet of Meskalamdug.

leonardo-iii-tocco.s: Leonardo III Tocco was the last Tocco ruler of the County Palatine of Cephalonia and Zakynthos and titular despot of Epirus, from 1448. He lost his remaining mainland territories to the Ottomans, and in 1479 Ottoman forces took Cephalonia, Zakynthos and Lefkada, forcing him to…

leonel-fernandez.s: Leonel Fernández is a Dominican politician of the Dominican Liberation Party who served as president of the Dominican Republic from 1996 to 2000 and again from 2004 to 2012. His governments promoted economic liberalisation, tourism and infrastructure, including the Santo…

leonid-kravchuk.s: Leonid Kravchuk was a Ukrainian politician who rose through the Communist Party of the Ukrainian SSR and became chairman of its Verkhovna Rada in 1990. He oversaw the declaration of independence on 24 August 1991 and was elected the first president of independent Ukraine in…

leonidas-i.s: Leonidas I was a king of Sparta of the Agiad line who commanded the Greek force defending the pass of Thermopylae against the Persian invasion of Xerxes in 480 BCE. After the Persians outflanked the pass, he sent most of the allies away and fell fighting with his 300 Spartans…

leopold-prince-of-anhalt-kothen.s: Leopold, Prince of Anhalt-Köthen from 1704 (ruling in person from 1715) to 1728, was a Calvinist ruler of a small German principality and a keen amateur musician. He is remembered for employing Johann Sebastian Bach as his Kapellmeister from 1717 to 1723, when Bach composed…

leopold-grand-duke-of-baden.s: Leopold was Grand Duke of Baden from 1830 to 1852. A comparatively liberal ruler, he allowed press freedom and reforms under Baden's constitution, and Baden joined the German Customs Union in 1835.

leopold-iii-frederick-franz.s: Leopold III Friedrich Franz ruled Anhalt-Dessau from 1758, as prince and from 1807 as duke, until his death in 1817. A model Enlightenment ruler, he laid out the Dessau-Wörlitz Garden Realm, the first large English-style landscape park in continental Europe, now a World…

leopoldine-diploma.s: The Leopoldine Diploma was the charter issued by Emperor Leopold I in 1691 that settled the government of Transylvania under Habsburg rule after the Ottoman retreat. It confirmed the rights of the Transylvanian estates, the privileges of the three recognised nations and the…

lester-bird.s: Lester Bird was an Antiguan politician, son of Vere Bird, who succeeded his father as leader of the Antigua Labour Party and served as prime minister of Antigua and Barbuda from 1994 to 2004. His family's long dominance of Antiguan politics was marked by corruption scandals.

leszek-the-white.s: Leszek the White was a Piast duke of Sandomierz and, with interruptions, high duke of Kraków from 1194 until his death. A son of Casimir II the Just, he struggled with his uncle Mieszko III and other relatives for the senior throne, and he intervened repeatedly in Galicia.

levan-ii-dadiani.s: Levan II Dadiani was prince of Mingrelia in western Georgia from 1611 to 1657. He made Mingrelia the strongest power in western Georgia, warring against the kingdom of Imereti and the princes of Guria and Abkhazia.

lewanika.s: Lewanika was the Litunga, or king, of the Lozi of Barotseland in present-day western Zambia from 1878, with a brief interruption, until 1916. Seeking protection against the Ndebele and the Portuguese, he signed concessions with the British South Africa Company from 1890.

lhazang-khan.s: Lhazang Khan was the last khan of the Khoshut Khanate that ruled Tibet. In 1705 he killed the regent Sangye Gyatso and deposed the Sixth Dalai Lama, Tsangyang Gyatso, who died on the way to China, making many Tibetans hostile to him.

li-dingguo.s: Li Dingguo was a Chinese general, one of the adopted sons of the rebel leader Zhang Xianzhong of the Great Xi regime in Sichuan. After Zhang's death in 1647 he led part of his army into the south-west and served the Southern Ming Yongli Emperor, winning notable victories over…

li-jishen.s: Li Jishen was a Chinese general and politician of the Kuomintang who repeatedly broke with Chiang Kai-shek. In 1933 he joined the leaders of the 19th Route Army in proclaiming the Fujian People's Government, which was quickly crushed.

li-shi-cheng-han.s: Li Shi was the last ruler of Cheng-Han, the Sixteen Kingdoms state in Sichuan, reigning from 343 to 347. The son of Li Shou, he was unpopular and faced revolts.

li-shou.s: Li Shou was emperor of Cheng-Han in Sichuan from 338 to 343. A cousin of the founder Li Xiong, he seized the throne from Li Qi in 338 and renamed the state Han.

li-si.s: Li Si was a Legalist statesman, chancellor to Qin Shi Huang, the First Emperor of China. He helped plan the unification of China in 221 BCE and advised abolishing hereditary fiefs in favour of commanderies run by appointed officials.

li-thai.s: Li Thai, who reigned as Maha Thammaracha I, was king of Sukhothai from about 1347 to 1368. A devout Theravada Buddhist and scholar, he is credited with writing the Traiphum, or Three Worlds, a treatise on Buddhist cosmology that shaped Thai thought for centuries.

li-xin-western-liang.s: Li Xin was the second ruler of Western Liang, the Sixteen Kingdoms state at Dunhuang and Jiuquan in the Hexi Corridor, reigning from 417 to 420 as the son of its founder Li Gao. Against advice, he attacked Juqu Mengxun of Northern Liang and was killed in battle in 420.

li-xun-western-liang.s: Li Xun was a son of Li Gao and the last ruler of Western Liang. After his brother Li Xin was killed by Northern Liang in 420, he held out at Dunhuang.

li-yu-southern-tang.s: Li Yu was the last ruler of Southern Tang, reigning from 961 to 975, and one of the great poets of Chinese literature. Already reduced to a Song tributary, his state fell when Song armies took his capital Nanjing in 975.

liaquat-ali-khan.s: Liaquat Ali Khan was a leader of the All-India Muslim League and close associate of Muhammad Ali Jinnah who became the first prime minister of Pakistan in 1947. He led the new state through partition, the refugee crisis and the first war with India over Kashmir, and moved the…

lig-myirhya.s: Lig Myirhya was the last king of Zhangzhung, the kingdom of western Tibet centred on the region of Mount Kailash. The Tibetan emperor Songtsen Gampo allied with him by marrying his sister Sad mar kar to the king, but she reportedly helped her brother against her husband, and…

lion-gardiner.s: Lion Gardiner was an English military engineer who had served in the Netherlands and was hired in 1635 to build a fort at the mouth of the Connecticut River for the Saybrook Colony. He commanded the fort during the Pequot War of 1636–1638.

liu-asheng.s: Liu Asheng was the last leader of the Lanfang Republic, the Hakka Chinese mining kongsi at Mandor in West Borneo, under growing Dutch supervision. Lanfang had cooperated with the Dutch longer than other kongsis.

liu-jiyuan.s: Liu Jiyuan was the last ruler of Northern Han, the Shatuo-led state at Taiyuan that was the last of the Ten Kingdoms to resist the Song, reigning from 968 to 979. Supported by the Khitan Liao, Northern Han withstood Song sieges in 968 and 969.
