liu-kun.s: Liu Kun was a Western Jin general, poet and governor of Bingzhou in northern China who held out against the Xiongnu state of Han Zhao after the collapse of Jin authority in the north. He relied on alliances with the Tuoba chief Tuoba Yilu, whom Jin made Duke and then Prince of…

liu-yongfu.s: Liu Yongfu was a Chinese soldier and leader of the Black Flag Army, which fought the French in northern Vietnam in the 1870s and 1880s. In 1895, when the Qing ceded Taiwan to Japan, he joined the short-lived Republic of Formosa and became its leader after President Tang…

ljudevit-posavski.s: Ljudevit Posavski was duke of Lower Pannonia, the Slavic duchy between the Drava and Sava centred on Sisak, under Frankish overlordship. In 819 he rebelled against the harsh rule of the Frankish margrave of Friuli, drawing in neighbouring Slavs and fighting the Duchy of Croatia.

llanbadarn-fawr.s: Llanbadarn Fawr is a village near Aberystwyth in Ceredigion, Wales, the site of an early medieval monastery associated with St Padarn. It was one of the leading church centres of Wales and the seat of a bishop in the early Middle Ages, and a centre of learning in the 11th…

lluis-companys.s: Lluís Companys was a Catalan lawyer and leader of the Republican Left of Catalonia who became president of the Generalitat of Catalonia in 1934 after Francesc Macià. In October 1934 he proclaimed a Catalan State within a federal Spanish republic and was imprisoned.

llywelyn-ap-gruffudd.s: Llywelyn ap Gruffudd, known as Llywelyn the Last, was prince of Gwynedd and the only native ruler formally recognised by England as Prince of Wales, by Henry III in the Treaty of Montgomery in 1267. Conflict with Edward I led to English invasions in 1277 and 1282.

llywelyn-the-great.s: Llywelyn the Great, Llywelyn ap Iorwerth, was prince of Gwynedd who made himself the dominant ruler of Wales. He married Joan, daughter of King John of England, and at Aberdyfi in 1216 the other Welsh rulers accepted his overlordship.

loango-bay.s: Loango Bay is a bay on the Atlantic coast of the present-day Republic of the Congo, north of Pointe-Noire. It was the main harbour of the Kingdom of Loango, whose capital Mbanza Loango (Buali) lay nearby.

long-bien.s: Long Biên was an ancient city in the Red River delta near present-day Hanoi, the administrative seat of Chinese-ruled Jiaozhi under the Han and later dynasties. During the revolt of Lý Bí, who proclaimed himself Lý Nam Đế in 544, it served as his base, and he built the Khai…

long-bien-bridge.s: The Long Biên Bridge is a cantilever railway and road bridge across the Red River in Hanoi, built by the French between 1899 and 1902 and originally named after Governor-General Paul Doumer. Part of the railway linking Hanoi with Haiphong and later Yunnan, it was the longest…

long-yunus.s: Long Yunus was a Malay ruler of Pattani descent who unified Kelantan on the east coast of the Malay Peninsula around 1762 and ruled it until his death in 1795. He founded the dynasty that still reigns in Kelantan, whose rulers took the title of sultan in the early 19th century.

lop-nur.s: Lop Nur is a former salt lake, now largely dry, in the eastern Tarim Basin in Xinjiang, China. The ancient oasis kingdom of Kroraina, called Loulan in Chinese, lay on its north-western shore, on the Silk Road between China and the western oases.

lord-chak.s: Lord Chak, recorded as Chan Chak K'ak'nal Ajaw, was a ruler of the Maya city of Uxmal in the Puuc hills of Yucatán around 900. Inscriptions associate him with major building works, and he is thought to have commissioned the Governor's Palace and other monumental structures…

lord-charles-somerset.s: Lord Charles Somerset was a British soldier and politician who governed the Cape Colony from 1814 to 1826. He ruled in an autocratic manner, made English the official language of government and encouraged the settlement of the 1820 Settlers in the Eastern Cape.

lord-meng-of-huang.s: Lord Meng of Huang was a ruler of the small Zhou-era state of Huang in southern Henan in the 7th century BCE. His tomb and that of his wife were excavated at Guangshan in 1983 and yielded fine bronze vessels, jades and lacquerware, which show an aristocratic culture close to…

lord-of-sipan.s: The Lord of Sipán is the name given to a Moche ruler whose undisturbed tomb was discovered in 1987 at Huaca Rajada near Sipán on the north coast of Peru by the archaeologist Walter Alva. Buried around 250 CE with gold, silver and copper regalia and sacrificed attendants, he is…

lordship-of-argos-and-nauplia.s: The Lordship of Argos and Nauplia was a Frankish fief in the Argolid created after the Principality of Achaea captured the strongholds of Leo Sgouros in 1212. Held by the de la Roche family as part of the Duchy of Athens and later by the house of Enghien, it passed in 1388 to…

lothar-franz-von-schonborn.s: Lothar Franz von Schönborn was prince-bishop of Bamberg from 1693 and archbishop-elector of Mainz from 1695 until his death. A great patron of Baroque architecture, he built the New Residence in Bamberg and the palaces of Weissenstein at Pommersfelden and Gaibach.

lough-corrib.s: Lough Corrib is the largest lake in the Republic of Ireland, lying north of Galway city in Connacht. It divided the lowlands of east Galway from Connemara to the west.

louis-fadrique.s: Louis Fadrique was count of Salona in central Greece and a member of the Fadrique family, a branch of the royal house of Sicily. He served as vicar-general of the Catalan duchies of Athens and Neopatras from 1375 to 1381.

louis-faidherbe.s: Louis Faidherbe was a French general and colonial governor of Senegal from 1854 to 1861 and 1863 to 1865. He pushed French rule inland along the Senegal River, fought the Toucouleur Empire of El Hadj Umar Tall and the Wolof kingdoms such as Cayor, and founded the port of Dakar…

louis-ii-of-poitiers.s: Louis II of Poitiers was the last count of Valentinois and Diois in the Rhône valley, of the Poitiers family that had ruled there since the 12th century. Childless and in long conflict with the bishops of Valence and the house of Savoy, he bequeathed his counties to the…

louis-i-duke-of-orleans.s: Louis I, Duke of Orléans, was the younger brother of King Charles VI of France. During the king's bouts of madness he struggled for control of the government with the dukes of Burgundy.

louis-the-blind.s: Louis the Blind, son of Boso, was king of Provence, or Lower Burgundy, from 887 and king of Italy from 900. He was crowned emperor in Rome in 901 as Louis III.

louis-the-child.s: Louis the Child was king of East Francia from 900 to 911, the son of Emperor Arnulf of Carinthia and the last of the East Frankish Carolingians. Crowned at the age of six, he reigned under the guidance of bishops while Magyar raids devastated the kingdom and regional dukes…

louis-viii-duke-of-bavaria.s: Louis VIII, known as Louis the Hunchback, was duke of Bavaria-Ingolstadt and the son of Louis VII the Bearded. He took the side of his father's enemies, and in 1443 he captured his own father and handed him over to the duke of Bavaria-Landshut.

louis-vii-duke-of-bavaria.s: Louis VII the Bearded was duke of Bavaria-Ingolstadt from 1413. Brother of Queen Isabeau of France, he spent years at the French court and returned with great wealth, building the New Castle and the Church of Our Lady in Ingolstadt.

louis-the-stammerer.s: Louis the Stammerer was the son of Charles the Bald, who made him king of Aquitaine in 867. He succeeded his father as king of West Francia in 877 but reigned only until his death in 879.

louis-viii-of-france.s: Louis VIII, called the Lion, was king of France from 1223 to 1226 and son of Philip II Augustus. As prince he invaded England in 1216 at the invitation of rebel barons but was defeated at Lincoln in 1217.

louis-william-margrave-of-baden-baden.s: Louis William, Margrave of Baden-Baden from 1677, was an imperial field marshal known as the Turkish Louis for his victories over the Ottomans, above all at Slankamen in 1691. He later commanded imperial armies on the Rhine in the wars against Louis XIV.

louis-xviii.s: Louis XVIII, brother of Louis XVI, was king of France from 1814 to 1824, apart from the Hundred Days of 1815. Restored by the allies after Napoleon's abdication, he granted the Charter of 1814, which kept a constitutional monarchy with a parliament and preserved many…

louise-michel.s: Louise Michel was a French schoolteacher and anarchist who fought for the Paris Commune of 1871, serving in its National Guard and as an ambulance worker. After its suppression she was deported to New Caledonia, where she taught Kanak people and sympathised with their revolt…

louis-joseph-papineau.s: Louis-Joseph Papineau was a lawyer and leader of the Parti canadien, later the Parti patriote, in Lower Canada, and speaker of its assembly for most of 1815 to 1837. He demanded control of revenues and an elected legislative council, set out in the Ninety-Two Resolutions of 1834.

lower-lusatia.s: Lower Lusatia is a historical region in eastern Germany and western Poland, around Cottbus and the Spree Forest, home to the Lower Sorbian Slavic minority. Ruled as a margraviate under Wettin, Brandenburg and Bohemian lords, it passed with the Bohemian crown and then to Saxony…

lower-styria.s: Lower Styria is the southern, Slovene-speaking part of the historical Duchy of Styria, around Maribor, Celje and Ptuj, now in north-eastern Slovenia. Part of the Habsburg lands for centuries, it was exposed to Ottoman raids in the 15th and 16th centuries.

lu-bu.s: Lü Bu was a Chinese warlord of the late Eastern Han dynasty, famed for his martial skill and notorious for betraying his patrons. He killed Ding Yuan and then the tyrant Dong Zhuo in 192, later seized Xu Province and fought both Yuan Shu, who had proclaimed his own dynasty,…

lu-long.s: Lü Long was the last ruler of Later Liang, the Sixteen Kingdoms state at Guzang in the Hexi Corridor founded by his uncle Lü Guang. He seized the throne in 401 amid succession struggles.

lucas-watzenrode.s: Lucas Watzenrode was prince-bishop of Warmia from 1489 until his death, a powerful figure in Royal Prussia who defended his see's autonomy against both the Teutonic Order and the Polish crown. He was the uncle and patron of Nicolaus Copernicus, whom he brought into the…

lucien-murat.s: Lucien Murat was the second son of Joachim Murat, King of Naples, and Caroline Bonaparte, Napoleon's sister. In 1812 Napoleon granted him the principality of Pontecorvo after Bernadotte gave it up, but he lost it at the Congress of Vienna in 1815.

lucius-aemilius-paullus-macedonicus.s: Lucius Aemilius Paullus Macedonicus was a Roman general who defeated King Perseus of Macedon at Pydna in 168 BCE, ending the Third Macedonian War and the Antigonid monarchy. Rome then divided Macedon into four republics.

lucius-mummius-achaicus.s: Lucius Mummius Achaicus was a Roman consul and general who defeated the Achaean League in 146 BCE. After his victory he destroyed Corinth, killing many of its men, enslaving women and children and shipping its art treasures to Rome.

lucjan-zeligowski.s: Lucjan Żeligowski was a Polish general who in October 1920, in a staged mutiny secretly approved by Józef Piłsudski, seized Vilnius from Lithuania. He proclaimed the Republic of Central Lithuania, nominally for the local Polish-speaking population, which was annexed by Poland…

lucrezia-borgia.s: Lucrezia Borgia was the daughter of Pope Alexander VI and sister of Cesare Borgia. Her first marriage, to Giovanni Sforza, lord of Pesaro, was annulled in 1497, and her second husband, Alfonso of Aragon, was murdered in 1500.

lucus-augusti.s: Lucus Augusti, modern Lugo in Galicia, north-western Spain, was a Roman town founded around 25 BCE. It became a leading centre of Roman Gallaecia and later its provincial capital.

luc-en-diois.s: Luc-en-Diois is a village in the Drôme valley in south-eastern France, the site of Lucus Augusti, one of the two chief towns of the Celtic Vocontii under Roman rule, alongside Vasio (Vaison-la-Romaine). Its role as a centre was later taken over by nearby Dea Augusta, modern Die.

lugdunum-convenarum.s: Lugdunum Convenarum was the Roman town of the Convenae in the upper Garonne valley of south-western France, traditionally founded by Pompey around 72 BCE. It had a forum, temples, baths and a theatre and became an important town of Roman Aquitania.

ludovico-manin.s: Ludovico Manin was the last doge of the Republic of Venice, elected in 1789. In May 1797, under pressure from Napoleon's army, the Great Council voted to dissolve the republic and Manin abdicated, ending more than a thousand years of independence.

ludovico-sforza.s: Ludovico Sforza, called il Moro, ruled the Duchy of Milan as regent from 1480 and as duke from 1494 to 1499. A great patron of the Renaissance, he employed Leonardo da Vinci, who painted the Last Supper and planned an equestrian monument for him.

louis-i-prince-of-anhalt-kothen.s: Louis I, Prince of Anhalt-Köthen from 1603 until his death, was the first ruler of the separate principality of Anhalt-Köthen. In 1617 he founded the Fruchtbringende Gesellschaft, the first society devoted to refining and standardising the German language, and he made Köthen a…

ludwig-i-of-bavaria.s: Ludwig I was king of Bavaria from 1825 to 1848. A patron of art and classical architecture, he rebuilt Munich with buildings such as the Glyptothek and the Ludwigstrasse and moved the university there.

ludwig-ii-of-bavaria.s: Ludwig II was king of Bavaria from 1864 to 1886. He was a patron of Richard Wagner and built the romantic castles of Neuschwanstein, Linderhof and Herrenchiemsee.

luigi-carlo-farini.s: Luigi Carlo Farini was an Italian physician, historian and statesman of the Risorgimento. In 1859 he became dictator of Modena and Parma and united them with Romagna as Emilia, which voted in 1860 to join the Kingdom of Sardinia.

luis-abinader.s: Luis Abinader is a Dominican economist and businessman who leads the Modern Revolutionary Party. He won the presidency of the Dominican Republic in 2020, ending sixteen years of government by the Dominican Liberation Party, and was re-elected in 2024.

luis-galvez-rodriguez-de-arias.s: Luis Gálvez Rodríguez de Arias was a Spanish journalist and adventurer in the Amazon. On 14 July 1899, backed by Brazilian rubber interests in Acre, then Bolivian territory, he proclaimed the Independent State of Acre at Puerto Alonso and made himself president.

luis-munoz-marin.s: Luis Muñoz Marín was a Puerto Rican poet, journalist and politician who founded the Popular Democratic Party and became the island's first elected governor in 1948, serving until 1965. He led the creation of the Commonwealth, or Estado Libre Asociado, with its own constitution…

luiz-inacio-lula-da-silva.s: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is a Brazilian trade unionist and founder of the Workers' Party who served as president of Brazil from 2003 to 2010 and again from 2023. His first governments expanded social programmes such as Bolsa Família and lifted millions out of poverty during a…

luka-bych.s: Luka Bych was a Kuban Cossack politician who led the government of the Kuban People's Republic in 1918–1919. He belonged to the Ukrainian-minded faction of the Kuban Rada that favoured federation with Ukraine and resisted General Denikin's aim of a united Russia.

lulu-al-kabir.s: Lu'lu' al-Kabir was a slave commander and chamberlain of the Hamdanid emirs of Aleppo who became the real power behind them. In 1004 he deposed the last Hamdanid heirs and ruled Aleppo in his own name, balancing between the Fatimid caliphate and the Byzantine Empire and…

luo-fangbo.s: Luo Fangbo was a Hakka scholar and migrant from Guangdong who organised Chinese gold miners in West Borneo. In 1777 he founded the Lanfang kongsi at Mandor near Pontianak, a self-governing community of miners with elected leaders, sometimes called the first republic in Asia.

ly-chieu-hoang.s: Lý Chiêu Hoàng was the only reigning empress in Vietnamese history and the last ruler of the Lý dynasty, enthroned as a child in 1224. In 1225 the regent Trần Thủ Độ arranged her marriage to his young nephew Trần Cảnh and her abdication in his favour.

ly-thai-to.s: Lý Thái Tổ, born Lý Công Uẩn, was the founder of Vietnam's Lý dynasty. Raised in a Buddhist monastery, he became a palace commander and was chosen as king in 1009 after the death of Lê Long Đĩnh, the last Early Lê ruler.

lycomedes-of-mantinea.s: Lycomedes of Mantinea was the leading statesman of the Arcadian League, formed in 370 BCE after Sparta's defeat at Leuctra. With Theban support he organised the federation and the foundation of its new capital, Megalopolis.

lygdamis-ii.s: Lygdamis II was tyrant of Halicarnassus in Caria in the mid-5th century BCE, a grandson of Artemisia I, ruling under Achaemenid overlordship. The historian Herodotus opposed him and went into exile on Samos.

lyuh-woon-hyung.s: Lyuh Woon-hyung was a Korean independence activist and moderate leftist politician. On Japan's surrender in August 1945 he formed the Committee for the Preparation of Korean Independence, which proclaimed the People's Republic of Korea in September, but the American occupation…

luis-antonio-de-sousa-botelho-mourao.n: Luís António de Sousa Botelho Mourão
luis-antonio-de-sousa-botelho-mourao.s: Luís António de Sousa Botelho Mourão, known by his title as the Morgado de Mateus, was a Portuguese nobleman who governed the restored Captaincy of São Paulo from 1765 to 1775. Sent under the Marquis of Pombal, he rebuilt the captaincy's administration and militia, promoted…

leopold-ii-holy-roman-emperor.s: Leopold II, known in Tuscany as Peter Leopold, was a son of Francis Stephen of Lorraine and Maria Theresa who ruled the Grand Duchy of Tuscany from 1765 to 1790. An enlightened reformer, he freed the grain trade, reorganised the administration and in 1786 made Tuscany the…

lazar-of-serbia.s: Lazar Hrebeljanović, known as Prince Lazar, was the most powerful Serbian ruler after the collapse of the Serbian Empire, governing Moravian Serbia from about 1371. Allied with Tvrtko I of Bosnia, he defeated the rival lord Nikola Altomanović in 1373.

leopold-iv-prince-of-lippe.s: Leopold IV was the last reigning prince of Lippe, ruling from 1905 after the long succession dispute over the principality was settled in favour of his Lippe-Biesterfeld line. He abdicated on 12 November 1918 during the German Revolution, and Lippe became a free state within…

ludger.s: Ludger was a Frisian missionary educated at Utrecht and York who preached among the Frisians and Saxons under Charlemagne. Around 800 he founded a monastery at Werden on the Ruhr, which became an imperial abbey ruling a small territory for a thousand years.

league-of-lezhe.s: The League of Lezhë was an alliance of Albanian noble families founded at Lezhë in March 1444 under the leadership of Skanderbeg, with Venetian-protected Lezhë as its meeting place. Members such as the Dukagjini and the Crnojević of Zeta pledged men and money for war against…

laguna-de-terminos.s: The Laguna de Términos is a large coastal lagoon in the Mexican state of Campeche, separated from the Gulf of Mexico by the island of Carmen. It was named by Spanish explorers in 1518.

lugal-anne-mundu.s: Lugal-Anne-mundu was a king of Adab in Sumer and the only ruler of that city named in the Sumerian King List, which credits him with a reign of 90 years. Old Babylonian copies of inscriptions attributed to him claim conquests from the Mediterranean to Elam.

lysander.s: Lysander was a Spartan admiral and statesman who won the Peloponnesian War for Sparta. With Persian money from Cyrus the Younger he built a fleet that destroyed the Athenian navy at Aegospotami in 405 BCE, then blockaded Athens into surrender in 404 BCE.

lachit-borphukan.s: Lachit Borphukan was a general of the Ahom kingdom of Assam. Appointed Borphukan, commander of the western region, by King Chakradhwaj Singha, he led the recapture of Guwahati from the Mughals in 1667 and in 1671 won the Battle of Saraighat on the Brahmaputra.

lake-albano.s: Lake Albano, the ancient Alban Lake, is a volcanic crater lake in the Alban Hills south-east of Rome. Its shores were settled from the early Iron Age and were traditionally associated with Alba Longa, which Roman writers placed nearby.

lavinium.s: Lavinium was an ancient city of Latium, near modern Pratica di Mare about 30 km south of Rome. Roman legend held that Aeneas founded it and named it after his wife Lavinia, and it was revered as a religious centre where Roman magistrates sacrificed to the Penates.

los-angeles.s: Los Angeles is the largest city of California and the second largest in the United States. It was founded in 1781 as a Spanish farming pueblo on the Los Angeles River, remained a small ranching town under Mexican rule, and passed to the United States in 1848.

lucius-licinius-lucullus.s: Lucius Licinius Lucullus was a Roman general and politician who commanded against Mithridates VI of Pontus in the Third Mithridatic War from 74 BCE. He relieved Cyzicus, conquered Pontus and invaded Armenia, defeating Tigranes II at Tigranocerta in 69 BCE, but his troops…

li-bing.s: Li Bing was a governor of Shu under the state of Qin in the 3rd century BCE, traditionally credited with building the Dujiangyan irrigation system on the Min river near Chengdu. The system divided and channelled the river without a dam, controlling floods and irrigating the…

lee-stack.s: Sir Lee Stack was a British army officer who served as Governor-General of the Sudan and Sirdar of the Egyptian Army from 1917. He was shot by Egyptian nationalists in Cairo in November 1924 and died the next day.

lower-saxony.s: Lower Saxony (Niedersachsen) is a state in north-western Germany, with its capital at Hanover, stretching from the North Sea and the Frisian islands to the Harz mountains. It was formed by the British occupation authorities in 1946 from the Prussian province of Hanover and the…

lake-jackson-mounds.s: The Lake Jackson Mounds are a group of earthen platform mounds on the shore of Lake Jackson, just north of Tallahassee, Florida. Built by people of the Fort Walton culture between about 1100 and 1500, the site was the leading Mississippian ceremonial centre of the region, and…

little-aden.s: Little Aden is a rocky peninsula on the western side of the bay of Aden in southern Yemen. Britain bought it from the Aqrabi sheikh in the 1860s and attached it to the Aden Settlement.

lakshadweep.s: Lakshadweep is a group of coral islands in the Arabian Sea off the coast of Kerala, forming a union territory of India. Formerly called the Laccadive Islands in English, most of them were long held by the Kolathiri rulers and then the Arakkal family of Cannanore, until the…

la-mazorca.s: La Mazorca was the armed wing of the Sociedad Popular Restauradora, a club of supporters of Juan Manuel de Rosas in Buenos Aires. Its members terrorised Unitarian opponents with threats, beatings and murders, with waves of killings in 1840 and 1842.

lago-oil-and-transport-company.s: The Lago Oil and Transport Company ran a large oil refinery at San Nicolaas in southern Aruba from 1929 to 1985. Owned by Standard Oil of New Jersey, later Exxon, it processed Venezuelan crude and was for a time among the largest refineries in the world, drawing workers from…

limagne.s: The Limagne is a fertile plain in the Auvergne in central France, a rift valley drained by the Allier river between the volcanic Chaîne des Puys and the Forez mountains. Its rich black soils made it one of the most productive farming areas of Gaul and supported the power of…

luernios.s: Luernios was a king of the Arverni in Gaul in the 2nd century BCE. The Greek writer Posidonius, quoted by Athenaeus, described how he sought popularity by scattering gold and silver from his chariot and holding a vast feast in a great enclosure.

lawrence-stager.s: Lawrence Stager was an American archaeologist, a professor at Harvard University and a leading scholar of the ancient Levant. From 1985 he directed the Leon Levy Expedition to Ashkelon in Israel, which uncovered Canaanite, Philistine and later remains, including the city's…

lancia.s: Lancia was the chief stronghold of the Astures on the plain of the river Esla, near modern León in north-western Spain. Roman historians record that the legate Titus Carisius besieged and took it during the Cantabrian Wars around 25 BCE, sparing the town so that it would stand…

las-medulas.s: Las Médulas is a former Roman gold-mining area near Ponferrada in the province of León, in north-western Spain. From the 1st century CE Roman engineers brought water through long canals and used it to collapse whole hillsides, a method Pliny the Elder called ruina montium.

laurion.s: Laurion is a district at the southern tip of Attica, in Greece, whose silver and lead mines were the main source of Athenian wealth in the classical period. A rich new vein discovered in 483 BCE paid, on the proposal of Themistocles, for the fleet that won at Salamis.

lim-river.s: The Lim is a river of the western Balkans, about 220 km long, which rises near Plav in Montenegro and flows north through Serbia and Bosnia and Herzegovina to join the Drina. Its valley, with the towns of Bijelo Polje, Prijepolje and Priboj, has long been a route between the…

limerick.s: Limerick is a city in the south-west of Ireland, on the River Shannon, and gives its name to County Limerick. Founded as a Norse settlement in the 10th century, it became the capital of the O'Brien kings of Thomond before falling to the Anglo-Normans.

lushnje.s: Lushnjë is a town in central Albania, on the edge of the Myzeqe plain. In January 1920 it hosted the Congress of Lushnjë, at which Albanian delegates rejected plans to partition the country, formed a new government and chose Tirana as the provisional capital, a decisive step…

lucknow.s: Lucknow is the capital of the state of Uttar Pradesh in northern India, on the river Gomti. It became the capital of the Nawabs of Awadh in 1775 and flourished as a centre of Urdu poetry, music, architecture and cuisine.

lake-biwa.s: Lake Biwa is the largest freshwater lake in Japan, in Shiga prefecture north-east of Kyoto. One of the oldest lakes in the world, it supplies water to Kyoto and Osaka.

lynden-pindling.s: Lynden Pindling was a Bahamian politician who led the Progressive Liberal Party to power in 1967, ending the rule of the white merchant elite known as the Bay Street Boys. As premier and then prime minister he led the Bahamas to independence in 1973 and governed until 1992,…

lake-balaton.s: Lake Balaton is a freshwater lake in western Hungary and the largest lake in Central Europe, about 77 kilometres long and almost 600 square kilometres in area. It lay in the Roman province of Pannonia and, in the 9th century, in the Frankish-ruled principality of Pribina and…

lalitpur-district.s: Lalitpur district is a district in the Bundelkhand region of Uttar Pradesh, India, bordered on three sides by Madhya Pradesh, with its headquarters at the town of Lalitpur. Rocky and forested, it contains the Jain temple complex at Deogarh and the Gupta-period Dashavatara Temple.

lalitpur.s: Lalitpur, also known as Patan, is a city in the Kathmandu Valley of Nepal, separated from Kathmandu by the Bagmati river. It was one of the three Newar kingdoms of the valley under the Malla dynasty until Prithvi Narayan Shah of Gorkha conquered it in 1768.

lakshmi-vilas-palace.s: Lakshmi Vilas Palace is the residence of the Gaekwad family in Vadodara, Gujarat, completed in 1890 for Maharaja Sayajirao Gaekwad III. Designed by Major Charles Mant and completed by Robert Fellowes Chisholm in the Indo-Saracenic style, it is among the largest private…

litunga.s: Litunga, meaning 'keeper of the earth', is the title of the king of the Lozi people of Barotseland in western Zambia. The Litunga ruled through a council (kuta) of titled officials and controlled land, labour and tribute across the Zambezi floodplain.

lady-of-baza.s: The Lady of Baza is an Iberian limestone sculpture of a seated woman on a winged throne, painted in bright colours and dated to the first half of the 4th century BCE. It was found in 1971 in a tomb of the necropolis of Basti near Baza, Granada, where it served as a cinerary urn.

lerotholi.s: Lerotholi was Paramount Chief of Basutoland from 1891 to 1905, son of Letsie I and grandson of Moshoeshoe I. He led the Basotho resistance in the Gun War of 1880–1881 against the Cape Colony's attempt to disarm them.

letsie-i.s: Letsie I was the eldest son of Moshoeshoe I and Paramount Chief of the Basotho from his father's death in 1870 until 1891. His rule saw Basutoland's annexation to the Cape Colony, the Gun War of 1880–1881 and the return to direct British rule in 1884.

letsholathebe-i.s: Letsholathebe I was chief of the Batawana in the Lake Ngami region of present-day Botswana in the mid-19th century. In his time the Batawana extended their authority over neighbouring peoples and grew rich from the ivory trade with hunters and traders from the Cape.

lubemba.s: Lubemba is the heartland of the Bemba people on the plateau of north-eastern Zambia, around the modern town of Kasama. It is the territory of the Chitimukulu, the Bemba paramount, and the site of the royal villages and burial groves.

llobregat.s: The Llobregat is a river in Catalonia, north-eastern Spain, about 170 km long. It rises in the Pre-Pyrenees near Castellar de n'Hug, flows south through the Berguedà and past Montserrat, and enters the Mediterranean in a delta just south of Barcelona, where the city's port and…

la-rioja-spain.s: La Rioja is an autonomous community of northern Spain in the upper Ebro valley, with Logroño as its capital. It is famous for Rioja wine.

logrono.s: Logroño is a city on the Ebro in northern Spain and the capital of the autonomous community of La Rioja. Near the Roman town of Vareia, it grew in the Middle Ages as a crossing point on the pilgrim route to Santiago de Compostela, and received a charter in 1095.

lohagarh-fort.s: Lohagarh, the 'Iron Fort', is the fortress of Bharatpur in Rajasthan, India, built by the Jat ruler Suraj Mal in the 18th century with massive earthen ramparts and a moat. In 1805 it withstood four British assaults under Lord Lake, a rare defeat for the East India Company, but…

lalitagiri.s: Lalitagiri is a Buddhist site in the Cuttack district of Odisha, India, one of the 'Diamond Triangle' with Ratnagiri and Udayagiri. Occupied from about the 1st century BCE to the 13th century CE, it has the remains of monasteries, a large stupa in which relic caskets were…

loire.s: The Loire is the longest river in France, about 1,000 km long. It rises in the Massif Central and flows north and then west through Orléans, Tours and Nantes to the Atlantic at Saint-Nazaire.

lame-bull-treaty.s: The Lame Bull Treaty was signed on 17 October 1855 at the mouth of the Judith River in present-day Montana between the United States and the Blackfoot, together with neighbouring tribes. Negotiated by Isaac Stevens and named after a Piikani chief, it set aside a large common…

lucius-postumius-albinus-consul-234-bc.s: Lucius Postumius Albinus was a Roman general, consul in 234 and 229 BCE. In 216 BCE, after Cannae, he was sent against the Gauls of the Po valley, but the Boii ambushed and destroyed his army in the Litana forest.

lacandon-maya.s: The Lacandon Maya are a Maya people of the rainforest of eastern Chiapas in Mexico, near the Guatemalan border. They speak a Yucatecan Maya language and long kept their own religion and customs in relative isolation.

louis-philippe-i.s: Louis Philippe I was King of the French from 1830 to 1848. Head of the Orléans branch of the Bourbons and son of a prince who had backed the Revolution, he was placed on the throne after the July Revolution of 1830 as a constitutional 'citizen king'.

li-hualong.s: Li Hualong was a Ming dynasty official who served as supreme commander in the south-west during the reign of the Wanli Emperor. In 1600 he led a large army against the rebellious chieftain Yang Yinglong of Bozhou, storming his fortress of Hailongtun, in one of the 'three great…

lohana.s: The Lohana are a Hindu trading and merchant community originating in Sindh, now living mainly in Gujarat, Kutch and Sindh and in a wide diaspora in East Africa and Britain. Some groups of Lohana origin, such as the Khojas and Memons, converted to Islam.

la-cabana.s: La Cabaña, the Fortaleza de San Carlos de la Cabaña, is an 18th-century fortress on the heights overlooking the entrance to Havana harbour in Cuba. Spain built it after the British capture of the city in 1762, and it was the largest Spanish fortification in the Americas.

luis-vicente-de-velasco.s: Luis Vicente de Velasco was a Spanish naval officer who commanded the defence of the Morro Castle at Havana during the British siege of 1762. He held out for weeks and was mortally wounded when the British stormed the fortress at the end of July.

levers-pacific-plantations.s: Lever's Pacific Plantations was a subsidiary of the British soap maker Lever Brothers, formed in the early 20th century to grow coconuts for copra in the Solomon Islands. It became the largest landholder and plantation company in the British Solomon Islands Protectorate,…

lucius-stertinius.s: Lucius Stertinius was a Roman officer who served under Germanicus in his campaigns in Germany in 15–16 CE. In 15 CE he defeated the Bructeri and recovered the eagle of the Nineteenth Legion, lost in the Varian disaster of 9 CE, and in 16 CE he fought at the Battle of Idistaviso.

lake-kyoga.s: Lake Kyoga is a large, shallow lake in central Uganda, through which the Victoria Nile flows on its way from Lake Victoria to Lake Albert. Much of it is fringed with papyrus swamps and floating vegetation.

lakilaponto.s: Lakilaponto was the sixth king of Buton, an island state off south-eastern Sulawesi, and its first sultan. Around 1540 he adopted Islam under the influence of a teacher from the Malay world and took the name Sultan Murhum, turning the kingdom into the Sultanate of Buton.

liberius-praetorian-prefect.s: Liberius was a Roman aristocrat and official who served Odoacer, the Ostrogothic king Theodoric and finally the emperor Justinian. He was praetorian prefect of Italy and then of Gaul, and later governed Egypt for Justinian.

lingayen-gulf.s: The Lingayen Gulf is a large inlet of the South China Sea on the west coast of Luzon, Philippines, bordered by Pangasinan and La Union. Its coast was home to the trading polity of Caboloan and was visited by Japanese and Chinese merchants.

leogane.s: Léogâne is a coastal town in Haiti, west of Port-au-Prince. It stands near the site of Yaguana, seat of the Taíno chiefdom of Jaragua, and under French rule it was a sugar-producing district and for a time the capital of the colony of Saint-Domingue.

lucterius.s: Lucterius was a leader of the Cadurci in southern Gaul and one of the chief commanders in the Gallic revolt of 52 BCE under Vercingetorix, when he raised the peoples of the south against the Roman Province. In 51 BCE he and the Senonian Drappes held Uxellodunum against Caesar.

lillebonne.s: Lillebonne is a town in Normandy, France, in the Pays de Caux near the Seine estuary. As Juliobona it was the chief town of the Caleti under Rome, and its Roman theatre is among the best preserved in northern France.

lake-okeechobee.s: Lake Okeechobee is the largest freshwater lake in Florida, in the south of the state, feeding the Everglades to its south. Its basin was home to the Belle Glade culture, whose people built earthworks and canals and paid tribute to the Calusa.

linth.s: The Linth is a river of eastern Switzerland that rises in the Glarus Alps and flows north through the canton of Glarus towards Lake Walen and Lake Zurich. Its valley formed the heart of the land of Glarus.

leodegar.s: Leodegar, known in French as Saint Léger, was Bishop of Autun in Merovingian Gaul and a leading opponent of the mayor of the palace Ebroin. After years of conflict he was blinded, deposed and put to death in 679, and was soon venerated as a martyr.

landammann.s: Landammann is the title of the chief magistrate in several Swiss cantons. In the rural cantons of the Old Swiss Confederacy, such as Uri, Schwyz, Unterwalden, Glarus and Appenzell, the Landammann was elected by the Landsgemeinde, presided over it and led the government and…

landsgemeinde.s: The Landsgemeinde is the open-air assembly of all qualified citizens of a Swiss canton or district, meeting once a year to elect officials and vote on laws by show of hands. It governed the rural cantons of central and eastern Switzerland from the Middle Ages and is one of the…

leventina.s: The Leventina is the upper valley of the River Ticino in southern Switzerland, running from Airolo at the foot of the Gotthard Pass down to Biasca. Uri took control of it in the 15th century, securing its hold after the victory at Giornico in 1478, and ruled it as a subject…

lake-zug.s: Lake Zug is a lake in central Switzerland, lying mostly in the canton of Zug with its southern part in Schwyz and Lucerne. The town of Zug stands on its north-eastern shore and the Rigi rises above its southern end.

lautaro.s: Lautaro was a Mapuche military leader in the early Arauco War. Captured as a youth, he served Pedro de Valdivia as a groom and learned Spanish tactics, then escaped and led the Mapuche to victory at Tucapel in December 1553, where Valdivia was killed.

la-isabela.s: La Isabela was the first Spanish town in the Americas, founded by Christopher Columbus on the north coast of Hispaniola, in the modern Dominican Republic, during his second voyage at the start of 1494. Disease, hunger and quarrels plagued the settlers, and it was abandoned…

lima.s: Lima is the capital and largest city of Peru, on the central coast in the Rímac valley. Francisco Pizarro founded it in January 1535 as the City of Kings, and it became the capital of the Viceroyalty of Peru and the centre of Spanish power in South America, with the University…

loarn-mac-eirc.s: Loarn mac Eirc is a legendary founder of Dál Riata, said in medieval genealogies to be a brother of Fergus Mór who crossed from Ireland to Argyll around 500. The Cenél Loairn, one of the main kindreds of Dál Riata, claimed descent from him, and the district of Lorn in Argyll…

lionel-dunsterville.s: Lionel Dunsterville was a British Army general who led Dunsterforce, the 1918 mission through Persia to the Caucasus, and briefly defended Baku against the Ottomans that August and September. A schoolfriend of Rudyard Kipling, he was the model for the hero of Kipling's Stalky…

llivia.s: Llívia is a Spanish town in the Cerdanya valley entirely surrounded by French territory, an exclave of Catalonia. As Iulia Libica it was the Roman centre of the Cerretani and the old capital of Cerdanya.

little-st-bernard-pass.s: The Little St Bernard Pass is an Alpine pass at about 2,188 m between the Tarentaise valley in Savoie, France, and the Aosta Valley in Italy. Used since prehistory and controlled by the Ceutrones and Salassi, it carried a Roman road from Augusta Praetoria into Gaul, and some…

lake-chalco.s: Lake Chalco was a freshwater lake in the south-east of the Valley of Mexico, joined to Lake Xochimilco and part of the lake system that included Lake Texcoco. Its shores were home to the Chalca city-states, and chinampa fields in its shallows helped feed Tenochtitlan.

lokamahadevi.s: Lokamahadevi was a queen of the Chalukya king Vikramaditya II in the 8th century. She commissioned the Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal, originally called Lokeshvara after her, to commemorate her husband's victory over the Pallavas at Kanchipuram around 740.

lakshmi-narayan-temple-chamba.s: The Lakshmi Narayan Temple is a group of stone temples in Chamba, Himachal Pradesh, India, dedicated to Vishnu and Shiva. The main shrine is traditionally attributed to Raja Sahil Varman, founder of Chamba town in the 10th century, and the complex was enlarged by later rulers.

lake-choclococha.s: Choclococha is a high Andean lake at about 4,600 metres in the Huancavelica region of Peru. The Chanka regarded it as their pacarina, the sacred place from which their ancestors emerged.

lalitpur-nepal.s: Lalitpur, also called Patan, is a city in the Kathmandu Valley of Nepal, across the Bagmati river from Kathmandu. An ancient Buddhist city of the Newar people, it became the seat of one of the three Malla kingdoms of the valley in the 17th century and was conquered by Prithvi…

lanzon.s: The Lanzón is a carved granite monolith about 4.5 metres tall standing at the heart of the Old Temple at Chavín de Huántar in the Peruvian Andes. Shaped like a lance, it depicts a fanged deity with claws and snake-like hair and was the chief cult image of the Chavín culture,…

li-te.s: Li Te was a Ba-Di leader who led refugees fleeing famine in the north-west into Sichuan around 298, under the Western Jin dynasty. When Jin officials tried to force the refugees back, he rebelled in 301 and fought the provincial governor Luo Shang around Chengdu, but was…

lake-poyang.s: Lake Poyang is the largest freshwater lake in China, in northern Jiangxi province, fed by the Gan and other rivers and draining into the Yangtze. Its area varies greatly between the summer flood season and the dry winter months.

liloa.s: Līloa was ruler (aliʻi nui) of the island of Hawaiʻi in the late 15th century, ruling from Waipiʻo Valley. Hawaiian tradition remembers him as a respected ruler and the father of Hākau, his heir, and of ʻUmi-a-Līloa, born to a woman of lower rank, whom he acknowledged as his son.

lahaina.s: Lahaina is a town on the west coast of Maui, Hawaii. Long a royal centre of Maui's chiefs, it served as the capital of the Kingdom of Hawaii from about 1820 to 1845, and in the mid-19th century it was a major port of the Pacific whaling fleet and a centre of missionary activity.

lanai.s: Lānaʻi is the sixth-largest of the main Hawaiian Islands, lying west of Maui and south of Molokaʻi. Dry and sparsely settled, it usually fell under the rule of Maui's chiefs.

long-march.s: The Long March was the retreat of the Chinese Communist Red Army from its bases in southern China in 1934–35, after Chiang Kai-shek's fifth encirclement campaign. The Central Red Army left Jiangxi in October 1934 and marched some 10,000 kilometres through western China, losing…

lazare-hoche.s: Lazare Hoche was a French Revolutionary general who rose from the ranks to command an army at the age of 25. He defeated the Austrians and Prussians in Alsace in 1793, crushed the émigré landing at Quiberon in 1795, pacified the Vendée and led the failed expedition to Ireland…

loughrea.s: Loughrea is a town in County Galway in the west of Ireland, on the shore of the lake from which it takes its name. Richard Mór de Burgh founded it around 1236 with a castle, and a Carmelite friary followed.

louis-delgres.s: Louis Delgrès was a free man of colour from Martinique and an officer of the French Revolutionary army who led resistance in Guadeloupe to the restoration of slavery. When Napoleon's expedition under General Richepance arrived in May 1802, he issued a proclamation of…

les-trois-ilets.s: Les Trois-Îlets is a commune on the south-west coast of Martinique, across the bay from Fort-de-France. Joséphine de Beauharnais, the first wife of Napoleon and Empress of the French, was born on her family's sugar estate of La Pagerie there in 1763.

la-soufriere-saint-vincent.s: La Soufrière is an active volcano forming the northern part of Saint Vincent in the Caribbean, the island's highest peak at about 1,234 metres. Its eruption of May 1902, a day before that of Mount Pelée on Martinique, killed about 1,600 people, many of them Kalinago and estate…

lekwungen.s: The Lekwungen, also known as the Songhees, are a Coast Salish people of southern Vancouver Island whose territory includes the site of Victoria, British Columbia. The Hudson's Bay Company built Fort Victoria on their land in 1843, and in 1850 they signed some of the Douglas…

levellers.s: The Levellers were a radical political movement of the English Civil War era, led by John Lilburne, Richard Overton and William Walwyn. In pamphlets and the Agreement of the People they demanded sovereignty of the people, a wide male franchise, religious toleration and…

lake-iseo.s: Lake Iseo is a lake in Lombardy, northern Italy, lying between the provinces of Bergamo and Brescia and fed and drained by the Oglio river. Its island of Monte Isola is one of the largest lake islands in southern Europe.

lake-como.s: Lake Como is a glacial lake in Lombardy, northern Italy, shaped like an inverted Y and fed and drained by the Adda river. One of the deepest lakes in Europe, it lies on routes from Milan to the Alpine passes, which gave the city of Como at its southern tip strategic importance.

lodi-vecchio.s: Lodi Vecchio is a town in Lombardy on the site of Roman Laus Pompeia and of medieval Lodi. Milan destroyed the old city in 1111 and again in 1158, after which Frederick Barbarossa refounded Lodi on a new site on the Adda a few miles away.

lanfranco-architect.s: Lanfranco was the architect of Modena Cathedral, begun in 1099, one of the masterpieces of Italian Romanesque. He is known from an inscription on the building and from a chronicle of the translation of Saint Geminianus in 1106, which praises his skill.

luca-signorelli.s: Luca Signorelli was an Italian Renaissance painter from Cortona, known for his powerful nude figures. His greatest work is the fresco cycle of the Last Judgement and the end of the world in the San Brizio Chapel of Orvieto Cathedral, painted from 1499 to 1504, which influenced…

lomellina.s: The Lomellina is a lowland district of south-western Lombardy, in the province of Pavia, between the Ticino, the Po and the Sesia, named after the town of Lomello. Fought over by Pavia, Milan, Novara and Savoy in the Middle Ages, it passed to Savoy in 1707.

lazio.s: Lazio is a region of central Italy around Rome, its capital, stretching from the Apennines to the Tyrrhenian Sea. Ancient Latium was home to the Latins, from whom Rome emerged.

lisle-sur-la-sorgue.s: L'Isle-sur-la-Sorgue is a town in Provence, south-eastern France, built on islands in the Sorgue river below the spring of Fontaine-de-Vaucluse. Part of the papal Comtat Venaissin until 1791, it held one of the four Jewish communities of the Pope's Jews.

luis-alves-de-lima-e-silva-duke-of-caxia.n: Luís Alves de Lima e Silva, Duke of Caxias
luis-alves-de-lima-e-silva-duke-of-caxia.s: Luís Alves de Lima e Silva, Duke of Caxias, was a Brazilian general and statesman, the patron of the Brazilian army. He suppressed regional revolts such as the Balaiada and ended the Ragamuffin War in 1845 through negotiation, then commanded allied forces in the Paraguayan War.

lodz.s: Łódź is a city in central Poland that grew from a small town into a great textile centre in the 19th century, after the government of Congress Poland promoted cloth-making there from the 1820s. Its factories made it the Manchester of Poland and drew Polish, Jewish and German…

la-alcudia-elche.s: La Alcudia is an archaeological site 2 km south of Elche in south-eastern Spain, the remains of the Iberian town of Ilici and the Roman colony of Colonia Iulia Ilici Augusta. Settled from the Bronze Age to the Visigothic period, it was a centre of the Contestani.

lucentum.s: Lucentum was an Iberian and Roman town on the hill of Tossal de Manises in the modern city of Alicante, south-eastern Spain. A fortified Iberian settlement of the Contestani, it became a Roman municipium under Augustus and declined in the 3rd century CE.

lady-of-elche.s: The Lady of Elche is a limestone bust of a woman wearing elaborate jewellery and large wheel-shaped headdresses, carved by Iberian artists probably in the 4th century BCE. It was found in 1897 at La Alcudia near Elche, taken to the Louvre and returned to Spain in 1941.

leicester.s: Leicester is a city in the East Midlands of England, on the River Soar. It began as Ratae Corieltauvorum, the Roman capital of the Corieltauvi, became an Anglo-Saxon bishopric and one of the Five Boroughs of the Danelaw, and grew into a county and market town.

leicestershire.s: Leicestershire is a county in the East Midlands of England, centred on the city of Leicester. In the late Iron Age it lay in the territory of the Corieltauvi; it later formed part of Mercia and of the Danelaw, and emerged as a shire after the English reconquest of the 10th…

lincoln-england.s: Lincoln is a cathedral city in the East Midlands of England, on the River Witham. It began as the Roman legionary fortress of Lindum, which became a colonia for veterans, later gave its name to the Anglian kingdom of Lindsey and was one of the Five Boroughs of the Danelaw.

lincolnshire.s: Lincolnshire is a large county in the East Midlands of England, stretching from the Humber estuary to the Wash. In the Iron Age it was part of the territory of the Corieltauvi, and its northern part later formed the Anglian kingdom of Lindsey before falling under Mercia and…

landevennec-abbey.s: Landévennec Abbey is a monastery at the mouth of the Aulne on the Crozon peninsula in Finistère, Brittany, traditionally founded around 485 by Saint Guénolé (Winwaloe). In the 9th century it adopted the Benedictine rule under Carolingian influence, and its scriptorium produced…

lile-rousse.s: L'Île-Rousse is a port town on the north-west coast of Corsica, in the Balagne region. Pasquale Paoli founded it in 1758 as a harbour for the Corsican Republic, to end its dependence on Genoese-held ports such as Calvi.

lake-trasimeno.s: Lake Trasimeno is the largest lake of peninsular Italy, a shallow lake in Umbria near the border with Tuscany, west of Perugia, overlooked by the Etruscan city of Cortona. On its northern shore Hannibal ambushed and destroyed a Roman army under Gaius Flaminius in 217 BCE, one…

lectoure.s: Lectoure is a hilltop town in the Gers department of south-western France, the ancient Lactora, chief town of the Lactorates in Roman Gaul. In the Middle Ages it was a principal fortress of the counts of Armagnac.

lourdes.s: Lourdes is a town in the Hautes-Pyrénées department of south-western France, at the foot of the Pyrenees. Its castle on a rock above the Gave de Pau was the chief stronghold of the counts of Bigorre and was held by the English for decades after 1360.

lagny-sur-marne.s: Lagny-sur-Marne is a town on the Marne east of Paris, France, which grew around the abbey of Saint-Pierre. In the 12th and 13th centuries it hosted one of the Champagne fairs, which opened the annual cycle each January and drew merchants from across Europe.

lorvao-monastery.s: The Monastery of Lorvão is a former monastery near Penacova, north-east of Coimbra in Portugal, one of the oldest in the country, with origins before the 10th century. A wealthy house of the Mozarabic frontier under the counts of Coimbra, it became a convent of Cistercian nuns…

leonhard-count-of-gorizia.s: Leonhard was the last count of Gorizia of the Meinhardiner dynasty, ruling from 1462 to 1500. His lands, scattered from the Puster valley to Gorizia, came under pressure from Venice and the Habsburgs.

ludwig-helferich-of-helfenstein.s: Ludwig Helferich of Helfenstein (died 1525) was a Swabian count and the Habsburg governor of Weinsberg, married to an illegitimate daughter of Emperor Maximilian I. On Easter Sunday, 16 April 1525, rebel peasants stormed Weinsberg during the German Peasants' War and forced him…

leiden.s: Leiden is a city in South Holland, Netherlands, on the Old Rhine. It withstood a Spanish siege in 1574, relieved when the dykes were cut, and William the Silent rewarded it with the first Dutch university in 1575.

lamoral-count-of-egmont.s: Lamoral, Count of Egmont (1522–1568), was a general and statesman of the Habsburg Netherlands, celebrated for his victories over the French at Saint-Quentin in 1557 and Gravelines in 1558. With William of Orange and Count Horne he led the noble opposition to Philip II's policies.

lemgo.s: Lemgo is a town in the Lippe district of North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany, founded around 1190 by Bernhard II of Lippe. A member of the Hanseatic League, it prospered from trade and keeps a rich Weser Renaissance townscape.

lippstadt.s: Lippstadt is a town in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany, on the Lippe, founded around 1185 by Bernhard II of Lippe as one of the first planned towns in Westphalia. A Hanseatic town, it was for centuries ruled jointly by the lords of Lippe and the counts of the Mark and their…

lambert-i-count-of-louvain.s: Lambert I (c. 950–1015), called the Bearded, was the first Count of Louvain, a younger son of the Reginarid count Reginar III of Hainaut.

lambert-of-italy.s: Lambert (c. 880–898), of the Widonid dukes of Spoleto, became King of Italy in 891 and was crowned emperor by Pope Formosus in 892 as co-ruler with his father, Guy of Spoleto.

lower-rhenish-westphalian-circle.s: The Lower Rhenish–Westphalian Circle was one of the Imperial Circles of the Holy Roman Empire, created in 1500 for defence, taxation and the keeping of the peace. Covering much of north-western Germany between the Weser and the Low Countries, it included the bishoprics of…

ludenscheid.s: Lüdenscheid is a town in the Sauerland, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. A town of the County of the Mark from the 13th century, it grew through iron working and wire-drawing and later became a centre for making metal buttons and fittings.

lahn.s: The Lahn is a river of western Germany, about 245 km long and a right tributary of the Rhine. It rises in the Rothaar Mountains and flows through Marburg, Giessen, Wetzlar, Weilburg, Limburg and Nassau to join the Rhine at Lahnstein.

ludwigskirche.s: The Ludwigskirche is a Lutheran church in Saarbrücken, Germany, built between 1762 and 1775 to designs by Friedrich Joachim Stengel for Prince William Henry of Nassau-Saarbrücken. Set in the Ludwigsplatz among matching palaces, it is one of the most important Protestant…

landry-count-of-nevers.s: Landry, Count of Nevers, was a Burgundian noble who received the county of Nevers around 990 from his father-in-law Otto-William, count of Burgundy. He founded the first hereditary dynasty of counts of Nevers and also won the county of Auxerre.

lelio-orsi.s: Lelio Orsi was an Italian Mannerist painter and architect from Emilia, active at Novellara and Reggio Emilia. He worked mainly for the Gonzaga counts of Novellara, decorating palace rooms and façades and painting religious works influenced by Correggio and Michelangelo.

lower-bavaria.s: Lower Bavaria is a region and administrative district of south-eastern Bavaria along the Danube, Isar and Inn, with Landshut as its capital. It took shape as a separate duchy in the partition of 1255, ruled by a Wittelsbach line from Landshut, and later as Bavaria-Landshut…

louis-vii-of-france.s: Louis VII was King of the Franks from 1137 to 1180, of the Capetian dynasty. His marriage to Eleanor of Aquitaine brought the vast duchy of Aquitaine under the crown, but after he led the unsuccessful Second Crusade the marriage was annulled in 1152, and Eleanor married Henry…

liebana.s: Liébana is a mountain district in the south-west of Cantabria, northern Spain, enclosed by the Picos de Europa, with Potes as its main town. In the 8th century its monastery of Santo Toribio was home to Beatus of Liébana, author of a famous commentary on the Apocalypse.

lyo.s: Lyø is a small Danish island south-west of Funen in the South Funen Archipelago. In May 1223 King Valdemar II and his son were seized there while hunting by Count Henry I of Schwerin, who held them captive for more than two years.

loretta-of-sponheim.s: Loretta of Sponheim was a countess who governed the Rear County of Sponheim as regent for her young son after her husband's death in 1323. To defend her rights against Archbishop Baldwin of Trier, she seized him in 1328 as he travelled on the Moselle and held him at her castle…

lichtensteig.s: Lichtensteig is a small town in the canton of St Gallen, Switzerland, on the Thur in the Toggenburg valley. Founded by the counts of Toggenburg in the 13th century below their castle, it was the chief town of the valley, and after the Abbey of Saint Gall bought the county in…

landlibell.s: The Landlibell was a charter issued by Emperor Maximilian I in 1511 that set out the defence obligations of the Tyrolean estates. It required the estates and districts to raise fixed contingents of troops for the defence of Tyrol, while exempting them from service outside it.

la-seu-durgell.s: La Seu d'Urgell is a town on the Segre in the Catalan Pyrenees, just south of Andorra. It has been the seat of the bishops of Urgell since late Roman or Visigothic times, and its 12th-century cathedral of Santa Maria is one of the finest Romanesque buildings in Catalonia.

lauterecken.s: Lauterecken is a small town in the Kusel district of Rhineland-Palatinate, where the Lauter flows into the Glan. It belonged to the counts of Veldenz and from 1543 was the residence of the counts palatine of Palatinate-Veldenz, a branch of the Wittelsbach family, until their…

leonardo-i-tocco.s: Leonardo I Tocco was an Italian nobleman from the Kingdom of Naples who received the County Palatine of Cephalonia and Zakynthos in 1357 from Prince Robert of Taranto. He founded the power of the Tocco family in the Ionian Islands, which also included Leucas, and his son Carlo…

leonardo-da-vinci.s: Leonardo da Vinci was an Italian painter, engineer and scientist of the High Renaissance, born at Vinci near Florence. In Milan, where he served Duke Ludovico Sforza from the early 1480s, he painted the Last Supper; his other works include the Mona Lisa and notebooks of…

lorn.s: Lorn is a district of Argyll in the west of Scotland, lying north of Loch Awe around Oban. It takes its name from the Cenél Loairn, a kindred of early medieval Dál Riata, and later formed a lordship held by the MacDougalls and then the Stewarts before passing to the Campbells…

lamekins.s: Lamekins was a ruler of the Curonians in the early 13th century. In 1230 he made an agreement with the papal legate Baldwin of Alna, accepting baptism for himself and his people in return for keeping their lands and freedoms under papal protection rather than crusader rule.

latvians.s: Latvians are a Baltic people native to Latvia, speaking Latvian, one of the two surviving Baltic languages. They formed from the merging of the Latgalians, Selonians, Semigallians and Curonians with assimilated Livonians, under centuries of German, Polish, Swedish and Russian…

lakhpatji.s: Lakhpatji was the Rao of Cutch from 1741 to 1761. A patron of the arts, he founded a school of Braj Bhasha poetry at Bhuj and supported craftsmen such as Ramsinh Malam, who built his Aina Mahal palace.

lecale.s: Lecale is a fertile lowland district of east County Down, Northern Ireland, between Strangford Lough, Dundrum Bay and the Irish Sea, around Downpatrick. It was the heartland of the Dál Fiatach kings of the Ulaid and later of the Anglo-Norman earldom of Ulster, whose castles…

longarus.s: Longarus was a king of the Dardani, the people of Kosovo and the upper Vardar, in the 3rd century BCE. He fought the kingdom of Macedon in the 230s BCE, taking advantage of its troubles under Demetrius II.

lucera.s: Lucera, ancient Luceria, is a town in northern Apulia, Italy, on a hill overlooking the Tavoliere plain. Rome founded a Latin colony there in 314 BCE during the Samnite Wars.

landau.s: Landau in der Pfalz is a town in the Palatinate, in south-western Germany. It became a free imperial city in 1291 and a member of the Decapolis of Alsatian towns in 1521.

lismore-county-waterford.s: Lismore is a town in County Waterford, Ireland, on the River Blackwater. Saint Carthach, also called Mochuda, founded a monastery there in the 7th century that became one of the leading centres of learning in early medieval Ireland and the seat of a bishop.

lewes-delaware.s: Lewes is a town in Delaware, United States, near Cape Henlopen at the mouth of Delaware Bay. It stands near the site of Zwaanendael, the short-lived Dutch whaling settlement of 1631, and calls itself 'the first town in the first state'.

lake-dian.s: Lake Dian, or Dianchi, is a large freshwater lake on the Yunnan–Guizhou Plateau beside Kunming in south-western China, the largest lake in Yunnan. Its shores were the centre of the Dian kingdom, a Bronze Age culture of the last centuries BCE known for its bronze drums and…

lijiashan.s: Lijiashan is an archaeological cemetery near Jiangchuan in central Yunnan, China, belonging to the Dian culture. Excavated from 1972, its tombs, dating from about the Warring States period to the Han dynasty, yielded bronze drums, weapons, cowrie containers and ornaments,…

lower-dir-district.s: Lower Dir is a district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province in north-western Pakistan, with its headquarters at Timergara. It was formed in 1996, when Dir District, created from the princely state of Dir after its abolition in 1969, was divided into Upper and Lower Dir.

labrador.s: Labrador is the mainland part of the Canadian province of Newfoundland and Labrador, a sparsely populated region of tundra and forest on the Atlantic coast. Long inhabited by Innu and Inuit, its interior was disputed between Newfoundland and Canada until the Judicial Committee…

lahore-resolution.s: The Lahore Resolution was adopted by the All-India Muslim League at its session in Lahore in March 1940. It called for independent states in the Muslim-majority areas of north-western and eastern British India, and became the basis of the demand for Pakistan.

luhansk.s: Luhansk is a city in the Donbas region of eastern Ukraine, which grew around a state iron foundry established in 1795. It became an industrial centre of coal mining, metalworking and locomotive building, and was called Voroshilovgrad for much of the Soviet era.

liaoning.s: Liaoning is a province of north-eastern China, on the Bohai Sea and the border with North Korea, with its capital at Shenyang. Its lands, including the Liao River plain and the Liaodong peninsula, were home to the Donghu, Xianbei and other peoples and were contested by…

lintun-commandery.s: Lintun Commandery was one of the four commanderies set up by the Han dynasty after its conquest of Gojoseon in 108 BCE, covering the east coast of the northern Korean Peninsula. Established in 107 BCE, it was abolished in 82 BCE, and its territory was attached to the Lelang…

legend-of-saint-gerard.s: The Legend of Saint Gerard is a Latin life of Gerard, the Venetian-born first bishop of Csanád, who was killed in a pagan uprising in 1046. Its longer version, the Legenda maior, compiled in the 14th century from earlier material, is the main source for the ruler Ahtum and his…

lantfrid.s: Lantfrid was Duke of the Alemanni from about 709 until his death in 730. He is credited with issuing the Lex Alamannorum, the Alemannic law code, and resisted the growing power of the Frankish mayor of the palace Charles Martel, who campaigned against the Alemanni in the 720s.

lex-alamannorum.s: The Lex Alamannorum is the law code of the Alemanni, written in Latin in the early 8th century, probably under Duke Lantfrid. It revised the earlier Pactus Alamannorum, set out compensation payments for injuries and offences, and gave a prominent place to the church and the duke.

leopold-iv-duke-of-anhalt.s: Leopold IV Frederick was Duke of Anhalt-Dessau from 1817 and, after the extinction of the Köthen and Bernburg lines, the ruler of the reunited Duchy of Anhalt from 1863 until his death in 1871. His long reign saw the revolution of 1848 in the Anhalt duchies and the start of…

locris.s: Locris was a region of ancient central Greece, divided into Eastern Locris on the Euboean Gulf and Western, or Ozolian, Locris on the Gulf of Corinth, separated by Phocis and Doris. Its people, the Locrians, founded colonies such as Locri in southern Italy.

louis-cardinal-of-bar.s: Louis of Bar was a French churchman and cardinal who inherited the Duchy of Bar in 1415, after his brothers were killed at the Battle of Agincourt. A younger son of Duke Robert I of Bar, he held several bishoprics during the Western Schism.

landshut.s: Landshut is a city in Lower Bavaria, Germany, on the Isar, and the seat of the region's government. Founded in 1204 by Duke Louis I of Bavaria together with Trausnitz Castle, it was the residence of the dukes of Lower Bavaria and from 1392 to 1503 of Bavaria-Landshut.

lech-river.s: The Lech is a river of western Austria and southern Germany, about 255 kilometres long, flowing from the Vorarlberg Alps north through Tyrol and Bavaria past Augsburg to join the Danube. For much of its course it formed the boundary between Bavarian and Swabian lands.

lex-baiuvariorum.s: The Lex Baiuvariorum is the law code of the Bavarians, written in Latin and compiled probably in the 740s under Frankish influence, drawing on Alemannic, Visigothic and Frankish laws. It names the Agilolfings as the hereditary ducal family and gives special status to five…

liebfrauenmunster-ingolstadt.s: The Liebfrauenmünster, or Church of Our Lady, is the largest church in Ingolstadt, Bavaria. Duke Louis VII the Bearded of Bavaria-Ingolstadt laid its foundation stone in 1425, intending it as a grand church for his capital, and the Late Gothic brick hall church was completed…

landulf-vi-of-benevento.s: Landulf VI was the last Lombard prince of Benevento, ruling jointly with his father Pandulf III from 1038. As Norman adventurers seized the surrounding lands, the citizens placed their city under Pope Leo IX in 1051, and the princes later ruled as papal vassals.

luneburg.s: Lüneburg is a town in Lower Saxony, Germany, south-east of Hamburg. Its salt works, active for about a thousand years until 1980, made it one of the richest members of the Hanseatic League, supplying salt along the Old Salt Road to Lübeck for the Baltic herring trade.

lu-buwei.s: Lü Buwei was a wealthy merchant who became chancellor of the State of Qin. He backed the hostage prince Zichu, who became King Zhuangxiang, and in 249 BCE led the army that annexed the Duchy of Eastern Zhou.

luo-river-henan.s: The Luo River is a tributary of the Yellow River in Henan province, China, flowing about 450 kilometres from the Qinling mountains past Luoyang. Its valley was a heartland of early Chinese civilisation, and Luoyang, the royal capital of the Eastern Zhou, takes its name from it.

liber-census-daniae.s: The Liber Census Daniae, or King Valdemar's Census Book, is a Danish royal land register compiled mainly in the 1230s under Valdemar II. Besides listing royal revenues in Denmark, it contains a survey of the Danish-ruled districts of northern Estonia, naming villages and their…

ludovico-ariosto.s: Ludovico Ariosto was an Italian poet at the court of the Este in Ferrara. His romantic epic Orlando Furioso, first published in 1516 and expanded until 1532, continued Boiardo's tale of Orlando and became one of the most influential poems of the Renaissance.

lorenzino-de-medici.s: Lorenzino de' Medici was a member of a junior branch of the Medici family who murdered his cousin Alessandro, Duke of Florence, in January 1537. He presented the deed as tyrannicide, but the republican exiles failed to profit from it, and Cosimo I de' Medici took power.

ludovica-torelli.s: Ludovica Torelli was Countess of Guastalla and heiress of the Torelli family. In 1539 she sold Guastalla to Ferrante Gonzaga, a general of Charles V, and devoted her fortune to religious works, founding in Milan the Angelic Sisters of Saint Paul, a congregation linked to the…

leczyca-voivodeship.s: The Łęczyca Voivodeship was a province of the Kingdom of Poland and later the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, formed from the former Duchy of Łęczyca after its incorporation into the crown in the 14th century. Its seat was the town of Łęczyca in central Poland.

limbourg.s: Limbourg is a small town in the province of Liège in eastern Belgium, on a rocky spur above the Vesdre. Its castle, built in the early 11th century, was the seat of the counts and later dukes of Limburg, who gave their name to the medieval duchy and, indirectly, to the modern…

lands-of-overmaas.s: The Lands of Overmaas were territories east of the Meuse between Maastricht and Aachen: the lordships of Valkenburg, Dalhem and 's-Hertogenrade (Herzogenrath), often counted together with the neighbouring Duchy of Limburg. They were ruled by the dukes of Brabant from the late…

latgale.s: Latgale is the easternmost historical region of Latvia, centred on Daugavpils and Rēzekne. Unlike the rest of Livonia, it remained under Polish–Lithuanian rule after the Truce of Altmark of 1629 and passed to Russia in 1772, so it stayed largely Catholic.

leuven.s: Leuven (French: Louvain) is a city in the Belgian province of Flemish Brabant, east of Brussels, on the river Dijle. Its counts became dukes of Brabant in the 12th century, and the city was a centre of the medieval cloth trade.

ludovico-iii-gonzaga.s: Ludovico III Gonzaga (1412–1478) was Marquis of Mantua from 1444 and a condottiere in the service of Milan. A patron of humanism and the arts, he employed Andrea Mantegna as court painter and Leon Battista Alberti, who designed the churches of Sant'Andrea and San Sebastiano in…

luigi-i-gonzaga.s: Luigi I Gonzaga (1268–1360) was the founder of Gonzaga rule in Mantua. In 1328 he overthrew Rinaldo dei Bonacolsi, lord of the city, and was made captain of the people, and Emperor Louis IV soon recognised him as imperial vicar.

l-orfeo.s: L'Orfeo is an opera by Claudio Monteverdi to a libretto by Alessandro Striggio, first performed at the Gonzaga court in Mantua in 1607. Retelling the myth of Orpheus and Eurydice, it is one of the earliest operas and the oldest still regularly performed.

lithuanians.s: The Lithuanians are a Baltic people living mainly in Lithuania, on the eastern shore of the Baltic Sea, who speak Lithuanian, one of the two surviving Baltic languages. Their tribes were united in the 13th century under Mindaugas, and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania became one of…

lunigiana.s: Lunigiana is a historical region of north-western Tuscany and eastern Liguria in Italy, around the valley of the Magra. It takes its name from the Roman port of Luna.

lordship-of-stargard.s: The Lordship of Stargard was a territory in south-eastern Mecklenburg around Neubrandenburg, Strelitz and Friedland, named after the castle of Stargard. Part of Brandenburg in the 13th century, it passed to Mecklenburg around 1300 through the marriage of Henry II of…

louise-of-mecklenburg-strelitz.s: Louise of Mecklenburg-Strelitz (1776–1810) was queen of Prussia as the wife of Frederick William III. After Prussia's defeat by Napoleon in 1806 she met him at Tilsit in 1807 to plead for better terms.

ludovico-antonio-muratori.s: Ludovico Antonio Muratori (1672–1750) was an Italian priest and historian, librarian of the Este dukes in Modena from 1700. His Rerum Italicarum Scriptores collected the sources of medieval Italian history and laid the foundations for its critical study.

lanfranc.s: Lanfranc (c. 1005–1089) was an Italian-born scholar and monk who taught at Bec Abbey in Normandy and became a close adviser of William the Conqueror.

leszek-of-raciborz.s: Leszek (c. 1290–1336) was the last Piast Duke of Racibórz in Upper Silesia, ruling from 1306.

la-scala.s: La Scala, the Teatro alla Scala, is the principal opera house of Milan. Designed by Giuseppe Piermarini after the old ducal theatre burned down, it opened in 1778 under Austrian rule on the site of the church of Santa Maria alla Scala, from which it takes its name.

liudolf-duke-of-saxony.s: Liudolf was a Saxon count who led the eastern Saxons in the mid ninth century under the Carolingian king Louis the German. With his wife Oda he founded a convent in 852, which moved to Gandersheim in 856 and became one of the great imperial abbeys.

landhaus-graz.s: The Landhaus in Graz is the seat of the Styrian estates and today of the Styrian state parliament. It was rebuilt in Renaissance style between 1557 and 1565 by the architect Domenico dell'Allio, with a celebrated arcaded courtyard.

louis-iv-of-france.s: Louis IV, called d'Outremer ("from overseas"), was King of West Francia from 936 to 954. The son of Charles the Simple, he grew up in exile in England and was recalled to the throne with the support of Hugh the Great, Duke of the Franks.

lower-silesia.s: Lower Silesia is the north-western part of the historical region of Silesia, along the middle Oder, with Wrocław as its main city. Ruled by Piast dukes and then by Bohemia and the Habsburgs, it was taken by Prussia in 1742 and remained German until 1945.

lubart.s: Lubart was a son of Grand Duke Gediminas of Lithuania who married into the princely house of Galicia-Volhynia and became ruler of Volhynia after 1340. For decades he fought Casimir III of Poland and Louis of Hungary over the former Galician-Volhynian lands, keeping most of…

legnica.s: Legnica (German Liegnitz) is a city in Lower Silesia, Poland, west of Wrocław. Near it the Mongols defeated Duke Henry II the Pious in 1241.

ludwigsburg-palace.s: Ludwigsburg Palace is a Baroque palace north of Stuttgart, built from 1704 to 1733 for Duke Eberhard Louis of Württemberg, who also founded the town of Ludwigsburg beside it. One of the largest Baroque palaces in Germany, it served at times as the ducal residence in place of…

litold-of-znojmo.s: Litold was a Přemyslid prince of Znojmo in southern Moravia, son of Conrad I of Brno. He received the Znojmo appanage around 1092, when his father became Duke of Bohemia.

lakshman-singh-of-dungarpur.s: Lakshman Singh was the last ruling Maharawal of Dungarpur State in southern Rajasthan, succeeding to the throne as a child in 1918. In 1948 he merged his state into the United State of Rajasthan.

lhasa.s: Lhasa is the chief city of Tibet, at an altitude of about 3,650 metres in the valley of the Kyi River. Songtsen Gampo made it the capital of the Tibetan Empire in the 7th century, and the Jokhang temple founded in his time became the holiest shrine of Tibetan Buddhism.

lupus-i-of-aquitaine.s: Lupus was a duke in south-western Gaul in the 670s, recorded as ruling Aquitaine and Gascony on behalf of the Merovingian kings while acting with growing independence. He presided over a church council in the region and is said to have tried to seize Limoges.

liu-fang.s: Liu Fang was a general of the Sui dynasty of China. In 602 he led an army into the Red River delta, where Ly Phat Tu, ruler of the Early Ly dynasty, surrendered, returning northern Vietnam to Chinese rule.

lucius-aurunculeius-cotta.s: Lucius Aurunculeius Cotta was a Roman legate of Julius Caesar in the Gallic Wars. In the winter of 54 BCE he shared command with Quintus Titurius Sabinus of a legion and a half quartered at Atuatuca among the Eburones.

lliria.s: Llíria is a town in the province of Valencia, Spain, about 25 kilometres north-west of the city of Valencia. Above it rises the hill of Tossal de Sant Miquel, site of Edeta, the capital of the Iberian Edetani, and the town continued as the Roman municipium of Edeta, whose…

languedoc.s: Languedoc is a historical region of southern France, stretching from the Rhône towards Gascony and from the Mediterranean to the Massif Central, with Toulouse as its traditional capital. Its name comes from the langue d'oc, the Occitan language.

lake-assad.s: Lake Assad is a reservoir on the Euphrates in northern Syria, created by the Tabqa Dam and filled from 1974. About 80 kilometres long, it is Syria's largest lake and supplies water and electricity to Aleppo and much of the north.

lamos-river.s: The Lamos is a river in Cilicia, in southern Turkey, now called the Limonlu, which flows into the Mediterranean west of Mersin. In the 9th and 10th centuries it marked the frontier between Byzantium and the Arab border zone of the thughur around Tarsus.

laskarid-dynasty.s: The Laskarid dynasty ruled the Empire of Nicaea, the main Byzantine successor state in Asia Minor, from 1204 to 1261. Its emperors, Theodore I Laskaris, John III Doukas Vatatzes, Theodore II Laskaris and the child John IV, rebuilt a Byzantine state and recovered much of Thrace…

lefkandi.s: Lefkandi is an archaeological site on the west coast of Euboea, in Greece, between Chalcis and Eretria. It was a prosperous settlement in the Early Iron Age, when much of Greece was poor and isolated.

laws-of-eshnunna.s: The Laws of Eshnunna are a collection of about sixty legal provisions written in Akkadian around 1800 BCE in the kingdom of Eshnunna, in Mesopotamia. Found on two tablets at Tell Harmal in Baghdad in the 1940s, they set prices, wages and fines and deal with marriage, slavery,…

luis-vernet.s: Luis Vernet was a merchant born in Hamburg who settled in Buenos Aires and in 1828 founded a settlement at Port Louis on East Falkland. In 1829 the United Provinces of the Río de la Plata appointed him political and military commander of the islands.

logting.s: The Løgting is the parliament of the Faroe Islands. It descends from the Alting, the assembly of free men that met at Tinganes in Tórshavn from the Viking Age and is counted among the oldest parliamentary bodies in the world.

ludwig-erhard.s: Ludwig Erhard was a German economist and politician of the Christian Democratic Union who, as director of economics in the western zones, ended price controls alongside the currency reform of 1948. As economics minister of West Germany from 1949 to 1963 under Konrad Adenauer…

la-trinitaria.s: La Trinitaria was a secret society founded in Santo Domingo on 16 July 1838 by Juan Pablo Duarte and his companions to free the eastern part of Hispaniola from Haitian rule. Its members, organised in cells of three, spread the cause of a sovereign Dominican Republic under the…

london-protocol-1830.s: The London Protocol of 3 February 1830 was the agreement by which Britain, France and Russia recognised Greece as an independent sovereign state under a hereditary monarch, after the Greek War of Independence. It set a narrow northern frontier, later widened, and left Crete…

luis-carrero-blanco.s: Luis Carrero Blanco was a Spanish admiral and Francisco Franco's closest political adviser for three decades, serving as under-secretary and then minister of the presidency. In June 1973 Franco made him prime minister, the first since the civil war, expecting him to ensure the…

luxeuil-abbey.s: Luxeuil Abbey was a monastery founded by the Irish missionary Columbanus around 590 at Luxeuil, in the foothills of the Vosges in Burgundy. It became one of the most influential monasteries of Merovingian Gaul, training monks who founded many further houses under Columbanus's…

lons-le-saunier.s: Lons-le-Saunier is a town in eastern France, capital of the Jura department, which grew around salt springs exploited since antiquity. It belonged to the Free County of Burgundy until the French conquest in 1674.

linz-diploma.s: The Linz Diploma was a charter issued by Emperor Ferdinand III at Linz in 1646 confirming Bremen's status as a free imperial city. It strengthened the city against Sweden, which received the surrounding Archbishopric of Bremen as a duchy at the Peace of Westphalia in 1648.
