limes-museum-aalen.s: The Limes Museum in Aalen, Baden-Württemberg, is a museum of the Roman frontier in Germany, opened in 1964 on the site of the largest cavalry fort on the Raetian Limes. The fort housed the ala II Flavia, a cavalry regiment of about 1,000 men.

lauch.s: The Lauch is a river in Alsace, north-eastern France, which rises in the Vosges and flows past Guebwiller and Colmar to join the Ill. Colmar grew on its banks, and the city's Little Venice quarter lies along it.

leutkirch-im-allgau.s: Leutkirch im Allgäu is a town in the Allgäu region of Baden-Württemberg that grew up as the market centre of the Nibelgau district. It was a free imperial city from the 1290s until 1802, a small council-governed town living from linen weaving, and passed to Bavaria and then,…

leopoldina.s: The Leopoldina is Germany's national academy of sciences, based in Halle. It was founded in 1652 in the imperial city of Schweinfurt by four physicians as the Academia Naturae Curiosorum and took its name from Emperor Leopold I, who granted it privileges in 1687.

leica-camera.s: Leica Camera is a German optics company based in Wetzlar, Hesse, which grew from the optical works of Ernst Leitz. The first Leica camera, designed by Oskar Barnack and sold from 1925, used 35 mm cinema film and launched compact photography.

lauter-rhine.s: The Lauter is a river that rises in the Palatinate Forest in Germany and flows south-east past Wissembourg to join the Rhine near Lauterbourg. For much of its lower course it forms the border between France and Germany.

lorch-am-rhein.s: Lorch am Rhein is a small wine town in Hesse on the right bank of the Rhine at the mouth of the Wisper, in the Upper Middle Rhine Valley. From 1919 to 1923 it was the administrative centre of the Free State Bottleneck, a strip of unoccupied Germany cut off between the French…

lippe-punctations.s: The Lippe Punctations were the guarantees given in January 1947 by North Rhine-Westphalia to the former Free State of Lippe when it chose to join that state rather than Lower Saxony. They protected Lippe's property, institutions and cultural heritage, later managed by the…

le-morne-des-sauteurs.s: Le Morne des Sauteurs ('Leapers' Hill'), also called Caribs' Leap, is a cliff at Sauteurs on the northern coast of Grenada. According to French accounts, in 1651 the last Kalinago (Carib) defenders resisting the French colonists leapt from it to their deaths rather than…

lao-theung.s: Lao Theung, 'Lao of the mountain slopes', is a broad Lao category for the mainly Mon-Khmer-speaking peoples of Laos, such as the Khmu, who live chiefly on the middle slopes of the uplands. Regarded as the country's oldest inhabitants, they took part in revolts against French…

la-marsa-convention.s: The La Marsa Convention was an agreement signed on 8 June 1883 between France and Ali III ibn al-Husayn, bey of Tunis. Supplementing the Treaty of Bardo of 1881, it obliged the bey to carry out the administrative, judicial and financial reforms France considered useful,…

louis-eugene-cavaignac.s: Louis-Eugène Cavaignac was a French general and republican politician. After service in the conquest of Algeria, he became minister of war in 1848 and in June crushed the June Days uprising of Paris workers with great bloodshed.

leopold-sedar-senghor.s: Léopold Sédar Senghor was a Senegalese poet, philosopher and statesman, the first president of Senegal from 1960 to 1980. A founder of the Négritude movement with Aimé Césaire, he sat in the French National Assembly from 1945 and led Senegal to independence, briefly within the…

loyada-hostage-crisis.s: The Loyada hostage crisis took place in February 1976, when militants of the Front for the Liberation of the Somali Coast seized a school bus carrying children of French military personnel in Djibouti and drove it to Loyada, on the border with Somalia. French gendarmes and…

leon-blum.s: Léon Blum was a French socialist politician and writer, the first socialist and first Jewish prime minister of France. Leading the Popular Front government from June 1936 to June 1937 and briefly in 1938, he introduced paid holidays, the 40-hour week and collective bargaining.

lanciano.s: Lanciano is a town in the province of Chieti in Abruzzo, central Italy, near the Adriatic coast. As Anxanum it was one of the main centres of the Frentani, an Italic people, and later a Roman municipium.

larino.s: Larino is a town in the province of Campobasso in Molise, southern Italy. As Larinum it was the chief town of the Larinates, a people sometimes counted among the Frentani, and became a Roman municipium; it was the home town of Aulus Cluentius, whom Cicero defended in 66 BCE.

liu-ye.s: Liu Ye ('Willow Leaf') is the legendary first ruler of Funan, a queen named in Chinese histories from the 3rd century onward. According to them, she led an attack on a foreign ship but was defeated by its passenger Kaundinya, or Hun Tian, who married her and founded the ruling…

lozere.s: Lozère is a department of southern France in the Occitanie region, created in 1790 largely from the former Gévaudan, with its prefecture at Mende. Covering granite plateaus, the limestone Causses and part of the Cévennes in the Massif Central, it is the least populous…

lambarene.s: Lambaréné is a town in west-central Gabon on the Ogooué River, capital of Moyen-Ogooué province. In 1913 the Alsatian doctor and theologian Albert Schweitzer founded a hospital at the Protestant mission there, which he ran for most of the rest of his life and for which he…

libreville.s: Libreville is the capital and largest city of Gabon, on the north shore of the Gabon estuary. It was founded in 1849 by the French navy as a settlement for Africans freed from the captured slave ship Elizia, hence its name, 'free town'.

llyn-peninsula.s: The Llŷn Peninsula extends about 50 kilometres into the Irish Sea from north-west Wales, in the county of Gwynedd. It has many Iron Age hillforts such as Tre'r Ceiri, and in the Middle Ages it was a pilgrim route to Bardsey Island.

licata.s: Licata is a town on the south coast of Sicily, at the mouth of the Salso river. It succeeds the Greek city founded around 282 BCE by Phintias, tyrant of Acragas, who resettled the people of Gela there and named it after himself.

lauaki-namulauulu-mamoe.s: Lauaki Namulauʻulu Mamoe was a Samoan orator chief from Savaiʻi, influential in the islands' politics from the late 19th century. In 1908 and 1909 he led the Mau a Pule, a movement of Savaiʻi chiefs opposing the German governor Wilhelm Solf's changes to Samoan government.

luderitz.s: Lüderitz is a port town on the Atlantic coast of southern Namibia. Its bay, Angra Pequena, was visited by Bartolomeu Dias in 1487 or 1488, and Adolf Lüderitz's purchase there in 1883 began German South West Africa.

lothar-von-trotha.s: Lothar von Trotha was a German general who commanded in South West Africa during the war against the Herero and Nama. After the Battle of Waterberg in 1904 he issued an extermination order against the Herero, driving them into the Omaheke desert, where many died of thirst.

lome.s: Lomé is the capital and chief port of Togo, on the Gulf of Guinea near the border with Ghana. Germany made it the capital of the colony of Togoland in 1897 and built a wharf and railways inland.

llanito.s: Llanito is the vernacular speech of Gibraltar, an Andalusian Spanish base mixed heavily with British English through frequent code-switching. It also contains words from Genoese, Maltese, Hebrew and other languages of the settlers who made up Gibraltar's population.

lelang-commandery.s: Lelang was a Chinese commandery set up by the Han dynasty in 108 BCE after its conquest of Gojoseon, with its centre near modern Pyongyang. For four centuries it was a channel for Chinese culture, writing and trade into Korea and Japan, and its tombs have yielded fine…

liaoyang.s: Liaoyang is a city in Liaoning province, north-east China, on the Taizi river. As Xiangping it was the seat of the Liaodong commandery and of the Gongsun warlords at the end of the Han period.

liepaja.s: Liepāja, German Libau, is a port city on the Baltic coast of western Latvia. Long a town of the Duchy of Courland, it passed to Russia in 1795 and grew into an important ice-free port and naval base with heavy emigrant traffic.

la-cosiata.s: La Cosiata was a political movement and revolt in Venezuela in 1826, led by José Antonio Páez against the government of Gran Colombia in Bogotá. It began when Congress summoned Páez to answer charges, and Venezuelan towns backed his refusal.

ludwik-mieroslawski.s: Ludwik Mierosławski was a Polish general, revolutionary and historian. Sentenced to death in Prussia for planning the uprising of 1846, he was freed in the March Revolution of 1848 and led the Greater Poland Uprising that spring, then commanded revolutionary forces in Sicily…

livorno.s: Livorno is a port city on the Ligurian Sea coast of Tuscany, Italy. A small village bought by Florence from Genoa in 1421, it was developed by the Medici grand dukes into a fortified free port, and the Livornine laws of 1591–1593 invited Jewish and other foreign merchants,…

lower-franconia.s: Lower Franconia is an administrative region of Bavaria in Germany, in the north-west of the state along the Main river, with Würzburg as its seat. Largely formed from the lands of the former prince-bishopric of Würzburg and the Aschaffenburg area, it came under Bavaria in 1814…

lakota-people.s: The Lakota, or Teton Sioux, are the westernmost division of the Oceti Sakowin, made up of seven bands including the Oglala, Hunkpapa, Sicangu and Miniconjou. Moving west from Minnesota in the 18th century, they became mounted bison hunters and the leading power of the northern…

leizhou-peninsula.s: The Leizhou Peninsula is the southernmost part of mainland China, in western Guangdong province, separated from Hainan Island by the Qiongzhou Strait. Its eastern coast holds the bay of Guangzhouwan, leased to France in 1898, where the city of Zhanjiang now stands.

lope-de-vega.s: Lope de Vega was a Spanish playwright and poet, one of the leading figures of the Spanish Golden Age. Extraordinarily prolific, he is said to have written some 1,500 plays, of which several hundred survive, including Fuenteovejuna and The Dog in the Manger.

lygdamis-i.s: Lygdamis I was a ruler of Halicarnassus in Caria at the end of the 6th century BCE, under the Achaemenid Empire, and the founder of a dynasty of Carian descent. He was the father of Queen Artemisia I, who fought for Xerxes at Salamis in 480 BCE, and grandfather of Lygdamis II,…

lygdamis-of-naxos.s: Lygdamis was tyrant of the island of Naxos in the Cyclades in the mid-6th century BCE. A Naxian aristocrat, he helped Peisistratus regain power in Athens and in return received his help in seizing Naxos around 540 BCE.

lofoten.s: Lofoten is an archipelago off the coast of Nordland in northern Norway, inside the Arctic Circle, known for its steep mountains and sheltered bays. For over a thousand years it has been the centre of the winter cod fishery, whose dried stockfish was exported south through…

liu-cong.s: Liu Cong was an emperor of the Xiongnu-led Han Zhao state in northern China from 310 to 318. Seizing the throne after killing his brother, he sent generals including Shi Le and Liu Yao against the Jin dynasty; they captured Luoyang in 311 and Chang'an in 316, taking the Jin…

lata-region.s: Lata was the historical name of southern Gujarat in western India, the coastal plain between the Mahi and Tapti rivers, with the port of Bharuch as its chief city. From the 6th to the 10th century it was ruled in turn by the Gurjaras of Nandipuri, branches of the Chalukyas and…

lamphun.s: Lamphun is a city in northern Thailand on the Kuang River, just south of Chiang Mai. As Hariphunchai it was the capital of a Mon Buddhist kingdom from the late first millennium until Mangrai of Lan Na captured it in 1292.

lurs.s: The Lurs are an Iranian people of the Zagros Mountains in western Iran, living mainly in Lorestan, Kohgiluyeh and Boyer-Ahmad and neighbouring provinces. They speak Luri, a language closely related to Persian, and were long organised in pastoral tribes, among them the Bakhtiari.

lake-neuchatel.s: Lake Neuchâtel is the largest lake lying entirely within Switzerland, in the west of the country at the foot of the Jura, with the cities of Neuchâtel and Yverdon on its shores. The site of La Tène at its northern end gave its name to the Celtic culture of the later Iron Age,…

lucius-domitius-ahenobarbus-consul-16-bc.s: Lucius Domitius Ahenobarbus was a Roman general and consul in 16 BCE, husband of Antonia the Elder, Mark Antony's daughter, and grandfather of the emperor Nero. As commander on the Danube and in Germany around 1 BCE he resettled the Hermunduri on the upper Main, marched beyond…

legio-vii-gemina.s: Legio VII Gemina was a Roman legion raised in Hispania by Galba in 68 CE. From the reign of Vespasian it was stationed in north-western Spain to guard the region and its gold mines, and its camp grew into the city of León, whose name derives from 'legio'.

langalibalele.s: Langalibalele was chief of the Hlubi, a Nguni people of Natal, and was renowned as a rainmaker. In 1873 he refused to have the guns his men had earned at the diamond fields registered, and the Natal government treated this as rebellion, broke up the Hlubi location and exiled…

laszlo-rajk.s: László Rajk was a Hungarian communist who served as minister of the interior from 1946 to 1948 and then as foreign minister. In 1949 he was arrested, accused of spying for Tito's Yugoslavia and the West, and condemned in a show trial organised by Mátyás Rákosi; he was executed…

lenin-boys.s: The Lenin Boys were an armed terror detachment of the Hungarian Soviet Republic in 1919, led by József Cserny and associated with Tibor Szamuely. Travelling in an armoured train and in vehicles, they hunted down opponents of the regime and carried out summary executions,…

levedi.s: Levedi was an early leader of the Hungarians, described by Constantine VII as the first of their voivodes when they lived under the authority of the Khazar Khaganate. The Khazar khagan gave him a noble Khazar wife and offered to make him prince of the Hungarians.

lika.s: Lika is a mountainous region of central Croatia, between the Velebit range and the Bosnian border, with Gospić as its main town. In antiquity it was home to the Iapydes.

landnamabok.s: Landnámabók, the Book of Settlements, is a medieval Icelandic work describing the settlement of Iceland from about 870. It names hundreds of the first settlers, their origins, descendants and the land they claimed, region by region around the island.

livonians.s: The Livonians, or Livs, are a Finnic people of the coast of the Gulf of Riga in present-day Latvia. In the early 13th century German crusaders conquered and baptised them, and their name was given to the territory of Livonia.

lleida.s: Lleida is a city on the Segre in western Catalonia, Spain, capital of the province of the same name. It grew from Iltirta, the chief town of the Iberian Ilergetes, which became Roman Ilerda, where Julius Caesar defeated Pompey's legates in 49 BCE.

louis-jolliet.s: Louis Jolliet was a French-Canadian explorer and fur trader born in Quebec. In 1673, with the Jesuit Jacques Marquette, he led the first recorded European expedition down the Mississippi, reaching the mouth of the Arkansas river and establishing that the river flowed into the…

lezhe.s: Lezhë is a town in north-western Albania near the mouth of the Drin. As ancient Lissus it was a fortified Illyrian and Greek settlement where Illyrian kings struck coins, and it later became a Roman town.

lighthouse-of-alexandria.s: The Lighthouse of Alexandria, or Pharos, was a tower built on the island of Pharos at Alexandria in Egypt under the first Ptolemaic kings and completed around 280 BCE. Designed by Sostratus of Cnidus and probably more than 100 metres high, it was counted among the Seven…

ljubljana.s: Ljubljana is the capital and largest city of Slovenia, on the Ljubljanica river. The Roman colony of Emona stood on its site, and as Laibach it was the capital of the Habsburg duchy of Carniola.

lake-ilmen.s: Lake Ilmen is a large shallow lake in Novgorod Oblast in north-western Russia, drained northwards by the Volkhov river towards Lake Ladoga. From the 8th century its shores were settled by the Slavs known as the Ilmen Slovenes, and Novgorod grew up at its northern outlet.

lorsch.s: Lorsch is a town in southern Hesse, Germany, between Worms and the Odenwald. It grew around Lorsch Abbey, founded in 764, which became one of the richest and most famous monasteries of the Carolingian empire and the burial place of East Frankish kings.

lorsch-codex.s: The Lorsch Codex is a cartulary compiled at Lorsch Abbey in Hesse in the late 12th century, recording the abbey's history and copies of thousands of charters of donation from the 8th century onwards. It contains the earliest written mention of hundreds of places in…

lorsch-pharmacopoeia.s: The Lorsch Pharmacopoeia is a medical manuscript written at Lorsch Abbey around 795, the oldest surviving book of medicine from the German-speaking lands. It gathers several hundred remedies drawn from classical and early medieval sources and defends the study of medicine as a…

louis-the-younger.s: Louis the Younger was king of East Francia from 876 to 882, a son of Louis the German. He ruled Saxony, Franconia and Thuringia and later Bavaria, and in 876 defeated his uncle Charles the Bald at Andernach when Charles tried to seize the western lands of his inheritance.

laodicea-on-the-lycus.s: Laodicea on the Lycus was an ancient Greek city in Phrygia, in south-western Anatolia, founded by the Seleucid king Antiochus II in the mid-3rd century BCE. It grew rich under Roman rule from wool, textiles and banking, and its church is one of the seven churches addressed in…

lycus-phrygia.s: The Lycus, now the Çürüksu, is a river of south-western Anatolia in Turkey and a tributary of the Maeander. Its valley held the ancient cities of Laodicea, Hierapolis and Colossae, and carried the main road from the Aegean coast to the interior.

lepontic-language.s: Lepontic is an ancient Celtic language known from about 140 inscriptions found around the Italian lakes and the southern Alps, dated from about the 6th to the 1st century BCE. It was written in an alphabet adapted from Etruscan and is linked to the Golasecca culture.

lipit-ishtar.s: Lipit-Ishtar was the fifth king of the Isin dynasty in southern Mesopotamia. He issued a law code in Sumerian, known from later copies, with a prologue and epilogue and laws on property, inheritance, slaves and marriage.

lysanias-of-chalcis.s: Lysanias was the ruler of the Ituraean principality of Chalcis in the Beqaa valley from about 40 BCE, succeeding his father Ptolemy son of Mennaeus. He supported the Parthian invasion of Syria and Judea in 40 BCE.

lodurva.s: Lodurva is a village about 15 kilometres north-west of Jaisalmer in Rajasthan, India, which served as a capital of the Bhati Rajputs before Rawal Jaisal founded Jaisalmer in 1156. Little of the old town survives, but its Jain temple dedicated to Parshvanatha, rebuilt in later…

leeward-maroons.s: The Leeward Maroons were the Maroon communities of western Jamaica, formed by Africans who escaped slavery and settled in the limestone hills of the Cockpit Country. Led by Cudjoe, they fought the British in the First Maroon War and won a treaty of self-government in 1739.

lakshmibai.s: Lakshmibai, the Rani of Jhansi, was the widow of Raja Gangadhar Rao and a leader of the Indian Rebellion of 1857. After the British annexed Jhansi she took control of the state during the rising and defended its fort in 1858.

laguna-santa-catarina.s: Laguna is a coastal town in southern Santa Catarina, Brazil, founded by Portuguese settlers in the 1670s. In July 1839 rebels of the Ragamuffin War under Davi Canabarro and Giuseppe Garibaldi captured it and proclaimed the short-lived Juliana Republic there.

laguna-province.s: Laguna is a province of the Philippines on the island of Luzon, south-east of Manila, lying along the southern shore of the lake Laguna de Bay. It was a centre of the Philippine Revolution and of resistance in the Philippine-American War.

lingayatism.s: Lingayatism, also called Virashaivism, is a Shaiva devotional tradition founded in 12th-century Karnataka around Basava, a minister at the Kalachuri court of Kalyani. It rejected caste hierarchy, temple ritual and Brahmin priesthood, and its followers wear a small linga as a…

lakshmikarna.s: Lakshmikarna, also called Karna, was the most powerful king of the Kalachuris of Tripuri, ruling from about 1041 to 1073. He campaigned in Bengal, Kalinga and Malwa and, allied with the Chalukya Bhima I, helped defeat Bhoja of the Paramara dynasty.

lubilash-river.s: The Lubilash is a river of the southern Kasai region of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, forming the upper course of the Sankuru, a major tributary of the Kasai. It flows north through the lands of the Kanyok and the Luba-Kasai and is joined by the Mbuji-Mayi River.

lake-ladoga.s: Lake Ladoga, north-east of Saint Petersburg in Russia, is the largest lake in Europe. Its basin linked the Baltic to the river routes of Rus' through the Neva and Volkhov, and Staraya Ladoga on its southern shore was an early Viking-age trading town.

lahijan.s: Lahijan is a town in Gilan province in northern Iran, near the Caspian Sea. From the 14th to the 16th century it was the capital of the Karkiya dynasty, which sheltered the young Safavid leader Ismail there in the 1490s.

lakshmana-sena.s: Lakshmana Sena was a king of the Sena dynasty of Bengal who reigned from about 1178 to about 1206. A patron of Sanskrit literature, he kept at his court the poet Jayadeva, author of the Gita Govinda.

lumbini.s: Lumbini is a site in the Rupandehi district of southern Nepal, near the Indian border, revered as the birthplace of Siddhartha Gautama, the Buddha. The emperor Ashoka visited it and set up an inscribed pillar around 249 BCE recording the Buddha's birth there, and the Khasa…

lesser-kabylia.s: Lesser Kabylia is the eastern part of Kabylia in northern Algeria, a mountainous region around the Babor range between Béjaïa, Sétif and Jijel. Less isolated than Greater Kabylia to the west, it was home from the 16th century to the Kingdom of Ait Abbas, whose lords later led…

limassol.s: Limassol is a port city on the southern coast of Cyprus and the island's second-largest city. It grew near the ancient city-kingdom of Amathus and became important in the Middle Ages: Richard I of England landed there in 1191, defeated Isaac Komnenos and married Berengaria of…

lake-edward.s: Lake Edward is a lake in the Albertine Rift on the border between Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Linked by the Kazinga Channel to Lake George, it drains northwards through the Semliki River into Lake Albert.

lake-batur.s: Lake Batur is a crater lake in the caldera of Mount Batur in Kintamani, north-eastern Bali, and the island's largest lake. Considered sacred, it is believed to feed the springs that water rice terraces across much of Bali, and its goddess is honoured at the temple of Ulun Danu…

linderhof-palace.s: Linderhof Palace is a small rococo-style palace near Ettal in the Bavarian Alps, built for King Ludwig II of Bavaria between 1869 and 1878. It was the only one of his palaces completed in his lifetime and the one in which he lived longest.

lola-montez.s: Lola Montez was the stage name of Eliza Gilbert, an Irish-born dancer and actress who presented herself as Spanish. In 1846 she became the favourite of King Ludwig I of Bavaria, who made her Countess of Landsfeld; her influence and arrogance provoked public anger that merged…

ludwig-iii-of-bavaria.s: Ludwig III was the last king of Bavaria, reigning from 1913 to 1918. Son of the prince regent Luitpold, he served as regent for his insane cousin Otto from 1912 and then had himself proclaimed king.

luitpold-prince-regent-of-bavaria.s: Luitpold was prince regent of Bavaria from 1886 until his death in 1912. A son of King Ludwig I, he took over the government when his nephew Ludwig II was declared insane and deposed, and continued as regent for Ludwig's brother Otto, who was also incapable of ruling.

leopold-i-of-belgium.s: Leopold I was the first king of the Belgians, reigning from 1831 to 1865. A prince of Saxe-Coburg-Saalfeld, he had married Princess Charlotte, heir to the British throne, who died in 1817, and he declined the throne of Greece in 1830.

lhotshampa.s: The Lhotshampa are the Nepali-speaking people of southern Bhutan, mostly descended from migrants who settled the southern foothills from the late 19th century. In the late 1980s and early 1990s Bhutan's national identity policies and a citizenship census led to the departure…

libyssa.s: Libyssa was an ancient town in Bithynia on the northern shore of the Gulf of Nicomedia, near modern Gebze in Turkey. It is remembered as the place where the Carthaginian general Hannibal, who had taken refuge at the court of Prusias I, took poison in the 180s BCE rather than…

llangorse-lake.s: Llangorse Lake is the largest natural lake in south Wales, near Brecon in the Brecon Beacons. A crannog near its northern shore, an artificial island of timber and stone dated by tree rings to the 890s, was a royal residence of the kings of Brycheiniog and is the only one…

lake-albert.s: Lake Albert is a lake of the Albertine Rift on the border between Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, about 160 kilometres long. It is fed by the Semliki River and the Victoria Nile, and the Albert Nile leaves its northern end.

lex-ripuaria.s: The Lex Ripuaria is the law code of the Ripuarian Franks of the Cologne region, written in Latin in the 7th century, probably under King Dagobert I. Based largely on the Salic law, it set out compensation payments for injuries and crimes, rules of procedure and property, and…

ladislaus-i-of-hungary.s: Ladislaus I was king of Hungary from 1077 to 1095. He strengthened royal power and the Church, issued strict laws against theft and defeated Cuman and Pecheneg raiders.

ljudevit-gaj.s: Ljudevit Gaj was a Croatian linguist, journalist and politician, leader of the Illyrian movement for the cultural and national revival of the South Slavs. In 1830 he published a reformed Latin alphabet for Croatian, the basis of the modern script, and from 1835 his newspapers…

li-guangli.s: Li Guangli was a Han Chinese general under Emperor Wu and the brother of the emperor's favourite consort, Lady Li. He led the war against Dayuan in the Ferghana valley, which after a failed first campaign forced the kingdom to submit and surrender its horses in 102 BCE.

llywarch-ap-hyfaidd.s: Llywarch ap Hyfaidd was king of Dyfed in south-west Wales from 892 until his death around 904, the last king of the old Dyfed dynasty. His daughter Elen married Hywel Dda of Seisyllwg, who then took over Dyfed and joined it with his own lands to form the kingdom of Deheubarth.

leap-castle.s: Leap Castle is a tower house near Roscrea in County Offaly, Ireland, built by the O'Carrolls of Ely, probably in the 15th century. It guarded a pass between Ely O'Carroll and Munster and saw fighting both within the O'Carroll family and against English forces.

llanaelhaearn.s: Llanaelhaearn is a village on the Llŷn peninsula in Gwynedd, north-west Wales, below the hillfort of Tre'r Ceiri. Its church holds early Christian inscribed stones, one of which, from the 5th or 6th century, commemorates a man described as Elmetiacos, a man of Elmet.

louis-i-of-etruria.s: Louis I was the first king of Etruria, a son of Duke Ferdinand of Parma. Under the Franco-Spanish agreements of 1800–1801, Napoleon gave him the former Grand Duchy of Tuscany as the Kingdom of Etruria in exchange for his family's claim to Parma.

levuka.s: Levuka is a town on the island of Ovalau, Fiji, founded as a European trading settlement and whaling port in the early 19th century. It was the seat of Cakobau's government, the place where the Deed of Cession was signed in 1874, and the colony's first capital until 1882, when…

lviv.s: Lviv is the largest city of western Ukraine, founded in the mid-13th century by King Daniel of Galicia and named after his son Leo. It passed to Poland in 1349, was the capital of the Austrian crownland of Galicia as Lemberg from 1772 to 1918 and then belonged to Poland until…

lodomeria.s: Lodomeria is the Latinised name of Volodymyr, a town in Volhynia, and of the medieval principality centred on it. Hungarian kings used the title King of Galicia and Lodomeria from the 13th century, and the Habsburgs revived it in 1772 for the Polish lands they annexed in the…

lankatilaka-vihara.s: Lankatilaka is a Buddhist temple near Kandy in central Sri Lanka, built in 1344 under King Bhuvanaikabahu IV of Gampola. Standing on a rock outcrop, its tall brick image house blends Sinhalese and south Indian styles and contains a large seated Buddha.

llancarfan.s: Llancarfan is a village in the Vale of Glamorgan, Wales, site of a monastery founded by Saint Cadoc in the 6th century. It was one of the leading churches of early medieval south Wales and a centre of learning, where Caradog of Llancarfan wrote saints' lives in the 12th century.

llandaff.s: Llandaff is a district of Cardiff, Wales, on the River Taff, and the seat of the diocese of Llandaff. Its church claimed to be the see of the saints Dubricius, Teilo and Euddogwy, and its 12th-century Book of Llandaff preserves charters of earlier kings of Glywysing and Gwent.

llantwit-major.s: Llantwit Major is a town in the Vale of Glamorgan, Wales, whose Welsh name, Llanilltud Fawr, recalls the monastery founded there by Saint Illtud around 500. It was one of the great centres of learning of early Christian Britain, and its church holds a collection of early…

luan.s: Lu'an is a city in western Anhui province, China, in the hills between the Huai and Yangtze rivers. Near it lay the ancient town of Lu, capital of Ying Bu's Kingdom of Jiujiang after 206 BCE.

linguere.s: Linguère is a town in the Louga region of north-central Senegal and the seat of a department of the same name. It lies in the heart of the former Jolof kingdom, whose name survives in the surrounding Djolof country, and is a centre for herding on the edge of the dry Ferlo plain.

lombok-strait.s: The Lombok Strait is a deep channel between the islands of Bali and Lombok in Indonesia, linking the Java Sea with the Indian Ocean. It lies on the Wallace Line, the biological boundary between Asian and Australasian fauna, and is a major route for deep-draught shipping.

luso-africans.s: Luso-Africans were communities of mixed Portuguese and African descent, or Africans of Portuguese culture, who arose on the coasts of West and West-Central Africa from the 15th century. Many descended from lançados, Portuguese traders who settled among African peoples, and…

lake-mweru.s: Lake Mweru is a freshwater lake on the border between Zambia and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, fed by the Luapula River and drained northwards by the Luvua into the Congo system. Its shores and the Luapula valley to the south were the heart of the Lunda kingdom of…

livingstone-zambia.s: Livingstone is a town in southern Zambia on the Zambezi River, close to the Victoria Falls, named after the explorer David Livingstone. It grew up near the new railway bridge over the falls in the early 1900s, became the capital of North-Western Rhodesia in 1907 and of…

luapula-river.s: The Luapula is a river of south-central Africa, part of the upper Congo system, that flows from the Bangweulu swamps north to Lake Mweru and forms much of the border between Zambia and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Its fertile, fish-rich valley was the centre of the…

li-shengtian.s: Li Shengtian was king of Khotan from 912 to 966, known in Khotanese as Viśa' Saṃbhava. A Buddhist ruler of the Visa dynasty, he took a Chinese dynastic name, exchanged embassies with the Later Jin, and married a daughter of Cao Yijin, ruler of the Guiyi Circuit at Dunhuang,…

larnaca.s: Larnaca is a port city on the south coast of Cyprus, built over ancient Kition. Kition was a Late Bronze Age copper-working town, then a Phoenician city-kingdom from the 9th century BCE and the birthplace of Zeno, founder of Stoicism.

luigi-palma-di-cesnola.s: Luigi Palma di Cesnola was an Italian-born soldier, diplomat and collector. After serving in the Union army in the American Civil War, he became American consul in Cyprus, where from 1865 to 1876 he dug at many ancient sites and assembled a huge collection of Cypriot…

lahaul.s: Lahaul is a high mountain valley in Himachal Pradesh, India, north of the Rohtang Pass, drained by the Chandra and Bhaga rivers. Its people combine Tibetan Buddhist and Hindu traditions, and it lay on the trade routes between Kullu and Ladakh, whose kings disputed its control.

leh.s: Leh is the main town of Ladakh in northern India, at about 3,500 m in the upper Indus valley. It was the capital of the Namgyal kings of Ladakh from the 17th century and a staging post on trade routes linking Kashmir, Tibet and Central Asia, and it is overlooked by Leh Palace.

leh-palace.s: Leh Palace is a former royal palace overlooking Leh in Ladakh, India, built by King Sengge Namgyal in the 17th century. Nine storeys high and built of stone, mud brick and timber, it recalls the Potala in Lhasa in style.

lambousa.s: Lambousa is an archaeological site on the north coast of Cyprus near Karavas (Alsancak), on the site of ancient Lapethos. The town flourished in the Roman and early Byzantine periods and was abandoned after Arab raids in the 7th century.

laristan.s: Laristan is a historical region of southern Iran, in the south of Fars province between Shiraz and the Persian Gulf, with its main town at Lar. Arid and hot, it lay on the routes between the Iranian plateau and the Gulf ports.

lazic-war.s: The Lazic War was fought from 541 to 562 between the Byzantine Empire and the Sasanian Empire for control of Lazica, the kingdom of the Lazi on the eastern Black Sea coast. Invited by King Gubazes II, Khosrow I took the fortress of Petra, but Byzantine and Lazic forces retook…

lindum-colonia.s: Lindum Colonia was the Roman town at Lincoln in eastern England. Founded as a legionary fortress around 60 CE, it became a colony for retired soldiers in the late 1st century and one of the main cities of Roman Britain, probably a provincial capital in the 4th century.

liu-jia.s: Liu Jia was a cousin of Liu Bang, founder of the Han dynasty, and a general in the Chu–Han Contention. After Xiang Yu's death in 202 BCE he and Lu Wan conquered the kingdom of Linjiang, and in 201 BCE he was made King of Jing, ruling lands south of the Huai River.

lu-wan.s: Lu Wan was a childhood friend and close follower of Liu Bang, founder of the Han dynasty, born in the same village on the same day. After serving in the wars against Qin and Xiang Yu, he was made King of Yan in 202 BCE.

lori-berd.s: Lori Berd is a ruined medieval fortress town in Lori Province, northern Armenia, on a promontory between the gorges of the Dzoraget and Urut rivers. Founded by King David Anhoghin in the 11th century, it became the capital of the Kiurikian kingdom of Lori.

lysimachia.s: Lysimachia was a Greek city on the isthmus of the Gallipoli peninsula in Thrace, founded by Lysimachus in 309 BCE as his capital. After his death it changed hands among the Hellenistic powers, and Antigonus II Gonatas defeated invading Gauls nearby in 277 BCE.

lower-macedonia.s: Lower Macedonia was the lowland core of the ancient Kingdom of Macedon, the coastal plains around the Thermaic Gulf watered by the Haliacmon and Axios rivers. It held the royal centres of Aigai and Pella and was the home of the Argead kings, who gradually brought the cantons…

lugii.s: The Lugii were a large group of peoples in the region of modern southern Poland, between the Oder and the Vistula, known from Strabo, Tacitus and Ptolemy in the 1st and 2nd centuries CE. They were subject for a time to Maroboduus of the Marcomanni and in 50 CE helped overthrow…

lombok-treasure.s: The Lombok Treasure is a collection of gold, silver and jewels that Dutch troops seized from the palace of the Balinese rulers of Cakranegara on Lombok during the conquest of 1894. Several hundred kilograms of objects were taken to the Netherlands.

lake-debo.s: Lake Debo is a large lake in the Inner Niger Delta of central Mali, formed where the Niger widens between Mopti and Timbuktu. Its area varies greatly with the annual flood.

lichfield.s: Lichfield is a cathedral city in Staffordshire, England. Chad established the seat of the Mercian bishops there in 669, and under King Offa it was briefly an archbishopric, from 787 to 803.

lough-ennell.s: Lough Ennell is a lake in County Westmeath, Ireland, south of Mullingar. Its shores and crannógs, such as Dún na Sciath and Cró-inis, were royal residences of the Clann Cholmáin kings of Mide.

lulach.s: Lulach was king of Scots for a few months in 1057–1058, the stepson of Macbeth and son of Gruoch by her first husband, Gille Coemgáin, mormaer of Moray. Raised to the throne after Macbeth's death, he was killed by Malcolm III on 17 March 1058.

lough-key.s: Lough Key is a lake in County Roscommon, Ireland, near Boyle, scattered with wooded islands. On one of them stood the Rock of Lough Cé, the island fortress of the MacDermots of Moylurg, whose family gave their name to the Annals of Loch Cé.

lion-gate.s: The Lion Gate is the main entrance to the citadel of Mycenae in southern Greece, built around 1250 BCE. Above its lintel a triangular relief shows two lions facing a central column, the only monumental sculpture surviving from Mycenaean Greece.

luanda.s: Luanda is the capital and largest city of Angola, on the Atlantic coast. It was founded in 1575–76 by the Portuguese captain Paulo Dias de Novais as São Paulo de Loanda and became the centre of Portuguese Angola and one of the busiest slave-trading ports in the Atlantic world.

lucala-river.s: The Lucala River is a river of northern Angola and the largest tributary of the Kwanza, which it joins near Massangano. The lands between the Lucala and the Kwanza formed the heartland of the Mbundu kingdom of Ndongo, and the Portuguese built forts along its course during…

life-of-saint-severinus.s: The Life of Saint Severinus is a biography of the monk Severinus of Noricum written by his disciple Eugippius in 511. It describes life in the Roman towns of the Danube province of Noricum in the late 5th century, under the pressure of the Rugians and other barbarian peoples,…

lindisfarne-gospels.s: The Lindisfarne Gospels is an illuminated manuscript of the four Gospels made at the monastery of Lindisfarne in Northumbria around 700–715, traditionally by Bishop Eadfrith. Its decorated carpet pages and initials combine Irish, Anglo-Saxon and Mediterranean styles.

liverpool.s: Liverpool is a port city in north-west England, on the estuary of the Mersey. In the 18th century it became the leading British port in the Atlantic slave trade, and in the 19th century it handled much of Britain's trade with West Africa, including palm oil, as well as cotton…

lyppeios.s: Lyppeios, or Lycceius, was a king of Paeonia in the mid-4th century BCE. He joined the Thracian king Cetriporis and Grabos of the Illyrians in an alliance with Athens against Philip II of Macedon in 356 BCE, but Philip defeated the allies and made Paeonia dependent on Macedon.

llangollen.s: Llangollen is a small town in Denbighshire, north-east Wales, on the River Dee. It is named after the 6th-century saint Collen.

lindisfarne.s: Lindisfarne, or Holy Island, is a tidal island off the coast of Northumberland in north-east England. In 635 the Irish monk Aidan founded a monastery there with the support of King Oswald of Northumbria, and it became a centre of Christian mission and learning, home of Saint…

lake-muhazi.s: Lake Muhazi is a long, narrow lake in eastern Rwanda, north-east of Kigali, with many winding arms between steep hills. Rwandan court traditions place the early core of the Nyiginya kingdom near its shores, from which the Kingdom of Rwanda expanded from the 16th or 17th century.

louis-edouard-bouet-willaumez.s: Louis Édouard Bouët-Willaumez was a French naval officer and colonial administrator who explored and charted the West African coast in the 1830s and 1840s. As commander on the coast and governor of Senegal, he negotiated treaties with rulers at Grand-Bassam, Assinie and in…

lepcha.s: The Lepcha are an indigenous people of Sikkim and the Darjeeling hills, regarded as the earliest inhabitants of Sikkim. They speak a Tibeto-Burman language with its own script and traditionally followed a nature religion before many adopted Buddhism.

lifau.s: Lifau is a place on the north coast of Timor, in the Oecusse exclave of East Timor, where the Portuguese established their first settlement on the island. It became the base of the Topasses and was the seat of the Portuguese governor from 1702 until 1769, when the capital was…

lake-vanern.s: Lake Vänern is the largest lake in Sweden and in the European Union, covering about 5,650 square kilometres in the west of the country. It drains through the Göta älv river to the Kattegat at Gothenburg.

lake-vattern.s: Lake Vättern is the second-largest lake in Sweden, a long, narrow and deep lake of about 1,900 square kilometres in the south of the country. Jönköping lies at its southern end and the abbey town of Vadstena on its eastern shore.

lombards.s: The Lombards were a Germanic people who migrated from the lower Elbe to Pannonia by the early 6th century. In 568, under King Alboin, they invaded Italy and founded a kingdom centred on Pavia, with powerful duchies at Spoleto and Benevento, which lasted until Charlemagne's…

liutprand-king-of-the-lombards.s: Liutprand was king of the Lombards from 712 to 744 and the most powerful of their kings. He strengthened royal authority over the dukes of Spoleto and Benevento, added many laws to the Edict of Rothari and fought the Byzantines in central Italy.

lake-malaren.s: Lake Mälaren is the third-largest lake in Sweden, stretching about 120 kilometres west from Stockholm, where it drains into the Baltic. Its shores were the heartland of the Svear, with Birka, Sigtuna, Uppsala and later Stockholm, and its waters linked the region to Baltic and…

laguna-copperplate-inscription.s: The Laguna Copperplate Inscription is a copper plate found in 1989 near Lumban in Laguna province, the Philippines. Dated to 900 CE, it is written in the Kawi script in Old Malay with Sanskrit and Old Javanese words, and records the cancellation of a debt.

lakandula.s: Lakandula was the ruler of Tondo, on Manila Bay in the Philippines, when the Spanish arrived in 1570–1571. After Miguel López de Legazpi took Manila he accepted Spanish rule and was baptised.

latakia.s: Latakia is the main port city of Syria, on the Mediterranean coast near the ruins of ancient Ugarit. Founded as Laodicea by the Seleucid king Seleucus I around 300 BCE, it was later held by Byzantines, Arabs and the crusader Principality of Antioch.

lavelua.s: Lavelua is the title of the paramount king of Uvea, or Wallis Island, in the Pacific. The kingship emerged from struggles among chiefly lineages after the Tongan conquest of the 15th century.

la-rioja.s: La Rioja is a region and autonomous community of northern Spain on the upper Ebro, with its capital at Logroño. In the Middle Ages it was contested between Pamplona and Castile and was the centre of the small kingdom of Viguera.

lemro-river.s: The Lemro is a river of Rakhine State in western Myanmar, flowing south through the Arakan hills to the Bay of Bengal. Its valley was the centre of the Arakanese kingdoms from the 9th to the 15th century, a period named after the river, with capitals such as Pyinsa, Parein,…

lichfield-gospels.s: The Lichfield Gospels are an 8th-century illuminated gospel book in the Insular style, kept at Lichfield Cathedral in England. In the 9th century it was at Llandeilo Fawr in Wales, and notes written in its margins there include some of the earliest surviving written Welsh.

limbu-people.s: The Limbu, who call themselves Yakthung, are a Tibeto-Burman-speaking people of eastern Nepal and neighbouring Sikkim and Darjeeling. Their homeland, Limbuwan, kept considerable autonomy after it was absorbed into the kingdom of Nepal in the 1770s.

lawazantiya.s: Lawazantiya was a city of Kizzuwatna in south-eastern Anatolia in the 2nd millennium BCE, a centre of the cult of the Hurrian goddess Shaushka, identified with Ishtar. The Hittite queen Puduhepa was the daughter of a priest of the city, and King Hattusili III married her there.

lietuvininkai.s: The Lietuvininkai, or Prussian Lithuanians, were Lithuanian-speaking Lutherans of Lithuania Minor, the north-eastern part of East Prussia. Their region produced the first Lithuanian printed book in 1547 and the poet Kristijonas Donelaitis, and Lithuanian books banned in the…

labyrinth.s: The Labyrinth, in Greek mythology, was the maze built by the craftsman Daedalus for King Minos of Crete to hold the Minotaur. The hero Theseus killed the monster there and found his way out with the thread given to him by Minos's daughter Ariadne.

linyanti.s: Linyanti was the capital of the Kololo kingdom in the mid-19th century, on the Linyanti river in the swamp country of the present-day Zambezi Region of Namibia, near the border with Botswana. The Kololo king Sebetwane ruled from there over the conquered Lozi.

lemkos.s: The Lemkos are an East Slavic people of the Low Beskid and neighbouring Carpathian mountains in south-eastern Poland, with related communities in Slovakia and Ukraine. Many identify as a distinct Rusyn group, while others regard themselves as Ukrainians.

lake-salpeten.s: Lake Salpetén is a small lake in the Petén department of northern Guatemala, just east of Lake Petén Itzá, whose water is notably saline. In the Postclassic period the Kowoj Maya settled its shores, with Zacpetén on a peninsula as their main centre.

lavr-kornilov.s: Lavr Kornilov was a Russian general who became commander-in-chief of the army in July 1917 and was accused of attempting a coup against the Provisional Government in the Kornilov affair that September. After the October Revolution he helped found the anti-Bolshevik Volunteer…

lakshmi.s: Lakshmi is the Hindu goddess of wealth, fortune and prosperity, and the consort of Vishnu. She is often shown seated or standing on a lotus, sometimes flanked by elephants pouring water over her, a form known as Gaja Lakshmi.

lezgins.s: The Lezgins are a Caucasian people of southern Dagestan in Russia and northern Azerbaijan, living mainly in the Samur valley and the neighbouring mountains. They speak Lezgian, a Northeast Caucasian language, and are mostly Sunni Muslims.

lamu-old-town.s: Lamu Old Town is the historic centre of Lamu, on Lamu Island off the northern coast of Kenya. Inhabited for more than seven centuries, it is the oldest and best-preserved Swahili town in East Africa, with narrow streets, coral-stone houses with carved wooden doors, and mosques.

lake-lanao.s: Lake Lanao is the largest lake on the island of Mindanao and the second largest in the Philippines, lying on a high plateau in the province of Lanao del Sur. Its shores are the homeland of the Maranao, whose name means 'people of the lake', and the city of Marawi stands at its…

lanao.s: Lanao is the region around Lake Lanao in north-central Mindanao in the Philippines, the homeland of the Maranao people. Under American rule it was a district of the Moro Province from 1903 and later became a province of the Philippines.

ludowingians.s: The Ludowingians were a German noble dynasty that ruled Thuringia as landgraves from 1131 and also held Hesse. Founded by Louis the Bearded in the 11th century, they built the Wartburg and made their court a centre of courtly poetry.

lao-peoples-revolutionary-party.s: The Lao People's Revolutionary Party is the communist party that has ruled Laos as the only legal party since 1975. It was founded in 1955 as the Lao People's Party, with roots in the Indochinese Communist Party, and led the Pathet Lao in the civil war, taking its present name…

le-code.s: The Hồng Đức Code, formally the Quốc triều hình luật, is the legal code of Vietnam's Later Le dynasty, associated with the Hồng Đức era of Emperor Lê Thánh Tông from 1470 to 1497. Based on Chinese models but adapted to Vietnamese custom, it was notable for protecting the…

lotus-sutra.s: The Lotus Sutra is one of the most influential scriptures of Mahayana Buddhism, composed in India around the 1st century CE. It teaches that all beings can attain Buddhahood and that the Buddha uses skilful means to lead them.

lanuvium.s: Lanuvium was an ancient Latin city in the Alban Hills, south-east of Rome, now the town of Lanuvio. A member of the Latin League, it received Roman citizenship after the Latin War in 338 BCE.

leto.s: Leto was a Greek goddess, daughter of the Titans Coeus and Phoebe and mother by Zeus of the twin gods Apollo and Artemis. According to myth, Hera's jealousy forced her to wander until she gave birth on the island of Delos.

lamian-war.s: The Lamian War was a revolt of Athens, the Aetolian League and other Greek states against Macedonian rule after the death of Alexander the Great in 323 BCE. The Greeks besieged the regent Antipater in Lamia, but Macedonian reinforcements arrived, the Athenian fleet was…

lebou-people.s: The Lebou are a people of Senegal living mainly on the Cap-Vert peninsula around Dakar, closely related to the Wolof in language. Traditionally fishermen and farmers, they won independence from the kingdom of Cayor in the 1790s and governed themselves through elected leaders…

limoges.s: Limoges is a city on the Vienne river in west-central France and the historic capital of the Limousin. Founded by the Romans as Augustoritum, it took its name from the Gallic Lemovices.

livy.s: Livy (Titus Livius) was a Roman historian from Patavium (Padua) who wrote Ab Urbe Condita, a history of Rome from its foundation in 142 books, of which 35 survive. Writing under Augustus, he is a principal source for early Rome, the Punic Wars and Rome's wars with Gauls,…

lisieux.s: Lisieux is a town in Normandy, north-western France, in the Calvados department. Under Rome it was Noviomagus Lexoviorum, the chief town of the Gallic Lexovii, and from the 6th century it was the seat of a bishopric.

liao-river.s: The Liao River is the main river of southern Manchuria in north-east China, flowing about 1,345 km to the Bohai Sea. The grasslands of its upper basin were the homeland of the Khitan, whose Liao dynasty took its name from the river.

liguria.s: Liguria is a region of north-western Italy along the Gulf of Genoa, between the Maritime Alps, the Apennines and the sea, with its capital at Genoa. It takes its name from the ancient Ligures, whose lands Augustus organised as Regio IX of Italy.

lurin-river.s: The Lurín is a river of Peru's central coast that reaches the Pacific south of Lima. Its valley holds the great shrine of Pachacamac near its mouth and was the heartland of the Ychsma polity before the Inca conquest.

langres.s: Langres is a hilltop town in the Haute-Marne department of north-eastern France, on a plateau near the sources of the Marne. As Andematunnum it was the chief town of the Gallic Lingones and then a Roman city, and from late antiquity it was the seat of a bishopric whose bishops…

lipari.s: Lipari is the largest of the Aeolian Islands in the Tyrrhenian Sea north of Sicily. Inhabited since the Neolithic and rich in obsidian, it was settled around 580 BCE by Greeks from Cnidus and Rhodes, whose city of Lipara fought Etruscan pirates and later sided with Carthage.

liu-ziye.s: Liu Ziye, known as the Former Deposed Emperor (Qianfei), was the sixth emperor of the Liu Song dynasty in southern China, reigning from 464 to 466. Succeeding his father Emperor Xiaowu as a teenager, he became notorious for cruelty, killing senior ministers and many of his own…

larache.s: Larache is a port city on the Atlantic coast of northern Morocco at the mouth of the Loukkos river, near the ruins of ancient Lixus. A Saadi port, it was handed to Spain in 1610, recaptured by the Alaouite sultan Moulay Ismail in 1689, and was again under Spanish rule as part…

loukkos.s: The Loukkos is a river of north-western Morocco that rises in the Rif mountains and reaches the Atlantic at Larache. The Phoenician, Mauretanian and Roman town of Lixus stood on a hill above its estuary, and in 1578 the Battle of Alcácer Quibir, or of the Three Kings, was…

lohkot.s: Lohkot (Loharkot) was a mountain fortress in the Pir Panjal range, in the Poonch region, the ancestral seat of the Lohara dynasty of Kashmir. Mahmud of Ghazni besieged it in 1015 and again in 1021, but its strong position, snow and bad weather forced him to withdraw both…

leeuwarden.s: Leeuwarden is a city in the northern Netherlands, capital of the province of Friesland. It grew from medieval mound settlements into the main town of Frisia, and from the 16th century it was the seat of the Habsburg and later Dutch stadtholders of Friesland, including the…

lemnos.s: Lemnos is a Greek island in the northern Aegean Sea, near the entrance to the Dardanelles. Valued in antiquity and the Middle Ages for its grain and strategic position, it was held in turn by Athens, the Byzantines, Venetian lords after the Fourth Crusade, the Genoese…

lord-of-mann.s: Lord of Mann is the title of the ruler of the Isle of Man. The Stanley family, granted the island in 1405, styled themselves Kings of Mann until 1504 and then Lords; the lordship passed to the dukes of Atholl in 1736, and its sovereign rights were sold to the British Crown in…

leon-battista-alberti.s: Leon Battista Alberti was an Italian humanist, architect and writer, one of the founding figures of Renaissance art theory. His treatises On Painting and On the Art of Building set out the principles of perspective and of classical architecture.

litani-river.s: The Litani is the longest river wholly within Lebanon, about 140 kilometres long. It rises in the Beqaa Valley near Baalbek, flows south between the Lebanon and Anti-Lebanon ranges, then turns west through a deep gorge below Beaufort Castle to reach the Mediterranean north of…

lord-of-the-isles.s: Lord of the Isles, in Latin Dominus Insularum, was the title of the Clan Donald rulers of the Hebrides and western Highlands, first used by John of Islay in 1336. The lords ruled almost as independent princes until James IV forfeited the lordship in 1493.

lichtenstein-saxony.s: Lichtenstein is a small town in western Saxony, Germany, north-east of Zwickau. It grew up around a castle that became one of the possessions of the Schönburg family, who held the lordship for centuries under Saxon overlordship.

lucania.s: Lucania was an ancient region of southern Italy, named after the Oscan-speaking Lucanians who occupied it from the 5th century BCE. Lying between the Tyrrhenian Sea and the Gulf of Taranto, it included Greek cities such as Poseidonia (Paestum), Elea and Metapontum.

lugus.s: Lugus was a god of the ancient Celts, known from inscriptions in Spain, Gaul and elsewhere, sometimes in the plural form Lugoves. His name survives in place names such as Lugdunum, modern Lyon, and he is widely linked with the Irish Lugh and the Welsh Lleu.

lycians.s: The Lycians were the people of Lycia in south-western Anatolia, speaking an Indo-European Anatolian language written in their own alphabet. Probably descended from the Bronze Age Lukka, they were known for their rock-cut tombs and their federation of cities, the Lycian League.

lunavada.s: Lunavada is a town in eastern Gujarat, India, near the Mahi river, and the headquarters of Mahisagar district. Founded according to tradition in 1434, it was the capital of the princely state of Lunavada, ruled by a Solanki Rajput dynasty, until the state merged into…

la-galigo.s: La Galigo, or Sureq Galigo, is the epic cycle of the Bugis of South Sulawesi in Indonesia, composed in Buginese verse and handed down in manuscripts. It tells of the descent of the gods to earth and the adventures of the hero Sawérigading and his son I La Galigo, many of them…

lake-matano.s: Lake Matano is a lake in the highlands of South Sulawesi, Indonesia, and at about 590 metres one of the deepest lakes in the world. The surrounding hills hold rich deposits of iron and nickel ore, which made the area an early source of iron for Luwu and other kingdoms of…

limyra.s: Limyra was a city of eastern Lycia, near modern Finike on the south coast of Turkey. In the 4th century BCE it was the capital of the dynast Pericles, whose monumental tomb-shrine overlooks the city, and its cliffs are cut with hundreds of rock tombs.

lyciarch.s: The Lyciarch was the president of the Lycian League, the federation of the cities of ancient Lycia in south-western Asia Minor. Elected each year by the league's assembly, he presided over its meetings and, in the Roman imperial period, over the provincial cult of the emperors.

ly-thuong-kiet.s: Lý Thường Kiệt was a general and court official of the Lý dynasty of Đại Việt (Vietnam). In 1075–1076 he led a pre-emptive invasion of Song China, sacking Yongzhou, and in 1077 he defeated the Song counter-invasion at the Như Nguyệt river north of Thăng Long.

luzon.s: Luzon is the largest and most populous island of the Philippines, home to the capital, Manila. Before Spanish rule it held trading polities such as Tondo and Maynila, linked to China and Brunei.

lex-flavia-malacitana.s: The Lex Flavia Malacitana is the municipal charter of Malaca (Málaga) in the Roman province of Hispania Baetica, issued under the emperor Domitian around 81–84 CE. Bronze tablets bearing it and the charter of nearby Salpensa were found near Málaga in 1851.

liberation-of-paris.s: The Liberation of Paris was the freeing of the French capital from German occupation in August 1944. As Allied armies advanced from Normandy, the French Resistance rose in the city on 19 August, and the Free French 2nd Armoured Division under General Leclerc entered on 24–25…

laozi.s: Laozi is the sage credited with the Daodejing, the founding text of Daoism, traditionally placed in the sixth century BCE as an older contemporary of Confucius, though many historians date the text later and regard the man as partly or wholly legendary. The work's teaching of…

lusici.s: The Lusici were a West Slavic tribe living in what is now Lower Lusatia, in eastern Germany, and gave the region its name. They were conquered by Margrave Gero in 963 and later came under the March of Lusatia.

league-of-san-genesio.s: The League of San Genesio was an alliance of Tuscan cities, including Florence, Lucca and Siena, formed in 1197 at San Genesio near San Miniato after the death of Emperor Henry VI. Backed by Pope Innocent III, it rejected imperial control of Tuscany and ended the old March of…

leitha.s: The Leitha is a river about 180 kilometres long that flows from Lower Austria into Hungary, where it joins the Moson arm of the Danube. For much of its course it formed the historical border between Austria and Hungary.

leopold-i-margrave-of-austria.s: Leopold I, called the Illustrious, was the first Babenberg ruler of the eastern march of Bavaria that became Austria. Emperor Otto II gave him the march in 976, and he pushed its frontier east along the Danube against the Magyars, ruling from Melk.

lubben.s: Lübben is a town in the Spreewald, Brandenburg, Germany. It was the seat of the estates and government of the Margraviate of Lower Lusatia, and passed from Saxony to Prussia in 1815.

lobau.s: Löbau is a town in Upper Lusatia in Saxony, Germany, between Bautzen and Görlitz. In 1346 it was one of the six founding towns of the Lusatian League, and it often hosted the league's meetings.

lubawa.s: Lubawa, in German Löbau, is a town in northern Poland, in present-day Warmian-Masurian Voivodeship. After the Teutonic Order's conquest it became the seat of the bishops of Culm, who had a castle there and ruled the surrounding district as their own territory.

libanukshabash.s: Libanukshabash was a king of Marhashi, a land east of Elam in south-eastern Iran, in the 21st century BCE. Under the Third Dynasty of Ur relations with Marhashi were friendly, and King Shulgi of Ur married one of his daughters to Libanukshabash, part of a policy of dynastic…

le-chevalier-errant.s: Le Chevalier errant ('The Knight Errant') is an allegorical romance in French prose and verse written by Marquis Thomas III of Saluzzo in the 1390s, while he was a prisoner in Turin. It follows a knight through the courts of Love, Fortune and Knowledge and presents gatherings…

ludovico-ii-marquis-of-saluzzo.s: Ludovico II was Marquis of Saluzzo from 1475 to 1504, a Renaissance prince allied with France. Around 1480 he had the Buco di Viso tunnel cut under the Alps to trade with Provence, and he made Saluzzo a lively court.

lacydon.s: The Lacydon was the natural harbour around which the Greek colony of Massalia was founded by settlers from Phocaea around 600 BCE. A sheltered inlet east of the Rhône delta, it served the city's trade throughout antiquity and the Middle Ages.

luenha-river.s: The Luenha is a river of southern Africa that rises in Zimbabwe, where it is known as the Ruenya, and flows north-east into Mozambique to join the Zambezi above Tete. Its confluence with the Zambezi was the site of Massangano, the fortified stronghold of the Afro-Portuguese Da…

lacumazes.s: Lacumazes was a young king of the Massylii in Numidia around 206 BCE. The son of Oezalces, he was placed on the throne by the noble Mazaetullus after the death of his brother Capussa.

lake-shinji.s: Lake Shinji is a brackish lake in Shimane Prefecture in western Japan and one of the largest lakes in the country. Linked to the Sea of Japan through Lake Nakaumi, it lies beside the city of Matsue, whose castle was built near its shore in the early seventeenth century.

la-turbie.s: La Turbie is a village in the Alpes-Maritimes, south-eastern France, on a height above Monaco. It is known for the Tropaeum Alpium, a monument built in 7–6 BCE to celebrate Augustus' conquest of the Alpine peoples, whose names are listed in its inscription.

lydiadas.s: Lydiadas was tyrant of Megalopolis in Arcadia in the third century BCE. In 235 BCE he laid down his power and brought the city into the Achaean League, where he was elected general several times and became a rival of Aratus of Sicyon.

lake-baikal.s: Lake Baikal is a rift lake in southern Siberia, Russia, the deepest lake in the world at about 1,640 metres and the largest freshwater lake by volume, holding more than a fifth of the world's unfrozen fresh surface water. Fed chiefly by the Selenga, it is home to many species…

limbazi.s: Limbaži, German Lemsal, is a town in the Vidzeme region of northern Latvia, north-east of Riga. It grew up around a castle of the bishops, later archbishops, of Riga on lands once held by the Livonians, and became one of the oldest towns in the country and a member of the…

lisht.s: Lisht, or el-Lisht, is a village and archaeological site on the west bank of the Nile south of Memphis in Egypt. It holds the pyramids of Amenemhat I and Senusret I, the first two kings of the Twelfth Dynasty, surrounded by tombs of their officials.

luchuan-pingmian-campaigns.s: The Luchuan–Pingmian campaigns were a series of Ming Chinese military expeditions from 1436 to 1449 against the Shan state of Mong Mao, called Luchuan by the Chinese, on the south-western frontier of Yunnan. They were directed against the ruler Si Renfa, who had expanded his…

limbin-confederacy.s: The Limbin Confederacy was an alliance of Shan princes formed in the mid-1880s to oppose King Thibaw of Burma and to put a rival prince, the Limbin Prince, on the throne. Its leading members included the saophas of Mongnai and Lawksawk.

lambityeco.s: Lambityeco is an archaeological site in the Valley of Oaxaca, Mexico, near Tlacolula, occupied mainly between about 600 and 800 CE as Monte Albán declined. A Zapotec town that produced salt, it is known for its well-preserved elite residences, tombs and stucco friezes and…

lazarica-church.s: The Lazarica Church is a medieval Serbian Orthodox church in Kruševac, built in the 1370s or 1380s as the court church of Prince Lazar. Dedicated to Saint Stephen, it is one of the finest examples of the Morava school of architecture, with a trefoil plan and richly carved…

lakhdhirji-waghji.s: Lakhdhirji Waghji was the Thakore Sahib, later Maharaja, of Morvi in Kathiawar from 1922 until the state joined the United State of Saurashtra in 1948. He continued his father Waghji II's development of railways, the port of Navlakhi and local industry, making Morbi a centre…

laconia.s: Laconia is a region of the south-eastern Peloponnese in Greece, centred on the Eurotas valley between the Taygetus and Parnon mountains. In the Mycenaean age it held the kingdom remembered in Homer as that of Menelaus, and from the Archaic period it was the territory of Sparta.

latmian-gulf.s: The Latmian Gulf was an inlet of the Aegean on the west coast of Anatolia, at the mouth of the Maeander River, on which stood the Greek cities of Miletus, Myus and Priene. Silt carried by the river gradually filled it, cutting the cities off from the sea, and its inner part…

le-corbusier.s: Le Corbusier was a Swiss-born French architect, designer and urban planner and one of the pioneers of modern architecture. His buildings, such as the Villa Savoye, the Unité d'Habitation in Marseille and the chapel at Ronchamp, and his plans for Chandigarh in India shaped…

lu-jia.s: Lü Jia was chancellor of the kingdom of Nanyue in southern China, serving several of its kings over decades. In 112 BCE, opposing the plan of the queen dowager and the young king Zhao Xing to submit to the Han dynasty, he killed them and the Han envoys and enthroned Zhao Jiande.

long-walk-of-the-navajo.s: The Long Walk of the Navajo was the forced removal of the Navajo people by the US Army in 1864 from their homeland in present-day Arizona and New Mexico to the Bosque Redondo reservation. Some 9,000 people were marched about 480 km on foot in many groups, and hundreds died on…

lobengula.s: Lobengula was the second and last king of the Ndebele kingdom in present-day Zimbabwe, succeeding his father Mzilikazi in 1870 and ruling from Bulawayo. Pressed by concession-hunters, he signed the Rudd Concession in 1888, which Cecil Rhodes's British South Africa Company used…

leith.s: Leith is the port district of Edinburgh in Scotland, on the Firth of Forth at the mouth of the Water of Leith. For centuries Edinburgh's harbour and a centre of trade with the Baltic and the Low Countries, it was the departure point of the first Darien expedition in 1698.

long-island-sound.s: Long Island Sound is a tidal estuary of the Atlantic Ocean between Connecticut and Long Island, New York, in the United States, about 180 km long. Its northern shore was settled by English Puritans from the 1630s, who founded New Haven and other coastal towns.

luis-de-carvajal-y-de-la-cueva.n: Luis de Carvajal y de la Cueva
luis-de-carvajal-y-de-la-cueva.s: Luis de Carvajal y de la Cueva was a Portuguese-born Spanish conquistador and governor who in 1579 received a royal grant to found the New Kingdom of León in north-eastern New Spain. He began settling it in 1582, founding early settlements in the area of present-day Monterrey.

lenape.s: The Lenape, also called the Delaware, are an Algonquian-speaking Indigenous people whose homeland covered the Delaware River valley, New Jersey and the lower Hudson valley, including Manhattan. They traded furs with Dutch and Swedish colonists in the 17th century and made…

lurio-river.s: The Lúrio is a river in northern Mozambique that flows about 600 km east from the Niassa highlands to the Indian Ocean. For much of its course it separates Niassa and Cabo Delgado provinces to the north from Nampula province to the south.

livingstonia.s: Livingstonia is a town in northern Malawi that grew from the Free Church of Scotland mission named after David Livingstone. The mission was founded at Cape Maclear on Lake Malawi in 1875 and moved to the high plateau above the lake in 1894 under Robert Laws.

lusaka.s: Lusaka is the capital and largest city of Zambia, on a plateau in the south-centre of the country. It grew from a small settlement on the railway line and replaced Livingstone as the capital of Northern Rhodesia, officially from 1935.

longmen-grottoes.s: The Longmen Grottoes are Buddhist cave temples cut into limestone cliffs on both banks of the Yi river south of Luoyang, Henan, China. Begun around 493 under the Northern Wei, after the court moved to Luoyang, they were extended under the Tang dynasty and contain about 100,000…

lashio.s: Lashio is the largest town of northern Shan State in Myanmar. It was the starting point of the Burma Road, built in 1937–1938 to carry supplies from the railhead at Lashio to Kunming in Nationalist China; Japanese forces captured it in April 1942, cutting the route.

la-libertad-region.s: La Libertad is a region on the northern coast of Peru, extending inland into the Andes, with its capital at Trujillo. Its coastal valleys were the heartland of the Moche culture and later of the Chimú kingdom, whose capital Chan Chan lies near Trujillo.

laredo.s: Laredo is a city on the north bank of the Rio Grande in Texas, facing Nuevo Laredo in Mexico. It was founded in 1755 by Tomás Sánchez as part of José de Escandón's colonisation of Nuevo Santander, and in 1840 it was the claimed seat of the short-lived Republic of the Rio Grande.

locrians.s: The Locrians were an ancient Greek people of central Greece, divided into the eastern Locrians facing Euboea and the Ozolian Locrians on the Gulf of Corinth, separated by Doris and Phocis. Colonists from Locris founded Locri Epizephyrii in southern Italy, whose lawgiver…

linares.s: Linares is a town in the province of Jaén in Andalusia, southern Spain, near the ruins of the ancient Iberian city of Castulo. Its lead and silver mines, worked since antiquity, made it one of the world's leading lead producers in the 19th century.

la-goulette.s: La Goulette is a port town on the narrow channel linking the Lake of Tunis with the Gulf of Tunis, serving as the harbour of Tunis. Its fortress was captured by Charles V in 1535 and held by Spain until an Ottoman force under Sinan Pasha took it in 1574.

lycortas.s: Lycortas of Megalopolis was a statesman and general of the Achaean League in the early 2nd century BCE and the father of the historian Polybius. A close ally of Philopoemen, he led the league after Philopoemen was killed by the Messenians, recovering Messene in 182 BCE.

legio-iii-augusta.s: Legio III Augusta was a Roman legion stationed in North Africa from the reign of Augustus into the 5th century. Based first at Ammaedara, then Theveste and from the 120s at Lambaesis in Numidia, it guarded the frontier and built roads and towns.

lachit-divas.s: Lachit Divas is an annual day of commemoration held in Assam, India, on 24 November, the birthday of Lachit Borphukan, the Ahom general who defeated the Mughal army at the Battle of Saraighat in 1671. It is marked by state ceremonies, schools and civic bodies as a celebration…

lakshmi-singha.s: Lakshmi Singha was king of the Ahom kingdom of Assam from 1769 to 1780, the youngest son of Rudra Singha to reign. Early in his reign the Moamoria rebellion broke out; the rebels seized the capital Rangpur, captured him and held power for several months before royalists retook…

lentienses.s: The Lentienses were an Alemannic people of the fourth century living north of Lake Constance, probably around the later Linzgau. They raided Raetia in 355 and were punished by Constantius II, and in 378 they crossed the frozen Rhine into Alsace, where Gratian's army crushed…

leuthari.s: Leuthari was an Alemannic duke who, with his brother Butilin, led a Frankish and Alemannic army into Italy in 553 during the Gothic War between the Byzantine Empire and the Ostrogoths. After raiding southern Italy he turned north with his plunder, but his army was ravaged by…

la-massana.s: La Massana is one of the seven parishes of Andorra and the name of its main town, in the north-west of the principality on the Valira del Nord. It includes the villages of Arinsal and Pal, whose ski slopes form the Vallnord area, and the Comapedrosa, at 2,942 metres the…

la-plata.s: La Plata is a city in Argentina, capital of the province of Buenos Aires, founded in 1882 by Governor Dardo Rocha after the city of Buenos Aires was federalised as the national capital. It was laid out on a planned grid crossed by diagonal avenues, and its university and…

leopoldo-galtieri.s: Leopoldo Galtieri was an Argentine general who headed the military junta as president from December 1981 to June 1982. Facing economic crisis and growing protest, he ordered the invasion of the Falkland Islands in April 1982, and he was forced to resign after the British…

luis-federico-leloir.s: Luis Federico Leloir was an Argentine biochemist who received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1970 for discovering sugar nucleotides and their role in the way the body builds and stores carbohydrates. He did most of his work at a small private institute in Buenos Aires, and…

lyceum-classical.s: The Lyceum was a sanctuary and gymnasium of Apollo Lykeios outside the walls of Athens, where Aristotle opened his school in 335 BCE. His followers, the Peripatetics, continued teaching there under Theophrastus and later heads, collecting books and research in natural science,…

ludwig-van-beethoven.s: Ludwig van Beethoven was a German composer, born in Bonn, who lived in Vienna from 1792. His nine symphonies, piano sonatas, string quartets and opera Fidelio bridged the Classical and Romantic eras, and he went on composing after becoming almost completely deaf.

lillie-langtry.s: Lillie Langtry was a Jersey-born actress and society beauty, the daughter of the dean of Jersey, known as the Jersey Lily. She became famous in London society in the late 1870s, was a mistress of the Prince of Wales, the future Edward VII, and from 1881 had a successful stage…

li-jinzhong.s: Li Jinzhong was a Khitan chief who, with his brother-in-law Sun Wanrong, led a major revolt against the Tang empire under Wu Zetian in 696, after a famine and harsh treatment by the governor of Yingzhou. He took Yingzhou and proclaimed himself khagan, but died later that year.

li-kaigu.s: Li Kaigu was a general of the Tang dynasty, of Khitan origin, sent by Wu Zetian to pursue the Goguryeo and Mohe followers who had fled east after the Khitan revolt of 696. He defeated and killed the Mohe chief Geolsa Biu, but in 698 he was routed by Dae Joyeong at Tianmenling,…

lozi-people.s: The Lozi, earlier called the Luyi or Aluyana, are a people of the upper Zambezi floodplain in western Zambia, whose kingdom of Barotseland was ruled by the Litunga. Their culture is shaped by the annual flood of the plain, marked by the Kuomboka ceremony.

lealui.s: Lealui is the dry-season capital of the Litunga, the king of the Lozi, on the Barotse floodplain of the upper Zambezi in western Zambia, near Mongu. Lewanika made it his capital in the late nineteenth century.

limulunga.s: Limulunga is the high-water capital of the Litunga, the king of the Lozi, on the edge of the Barotse floodplain near Mongu in western Zambia. It was established in the 1930s as a residence above the flood, and the Litunga moves there from Lealui each year in the Kuomboka…

lochner-concession.s: The Lochner Concession was the agreement signed on 27 June 1890 between Lewanika, Litunga of Barotseland, and Frank Lochner, agent of Cecil Rhodes's British South Africa Company. Lewanika believed he was placing his kingdom under the protection of Queen Victoria, but the…

livadeia.s: Livadeia, ancient Lebadea, is a town in Boeotia, central Greece, today the capital of the Boeotia regional unit. In antiquity it was famous for the oracle of Trophonius, consulted by visitors who descended into an underground chamber, an experience described by Pausanias.

lysis-of-taras.s: Lysis of Taras was a Pythagorean philosopher of the fifth and early fourth centuries BCE from Taras in southern Italy. After the persecution of the Pythagoreans in Italy he settled at Thebes, where, according to ancient tradition, he became the teacher of the young Epaminondas.

limbang.s: Limbang is a town and division in the Malaysian state of Sarawak on the island of Borneo, lying along the Limbang River between the two parts of Brunei. It belonged to the Sultanate of Brunei until 1890, when Charles Brooke, Rajah of Sarawak, annexed it, splitting Brunei's…

licinius.s: Licinius was Roman emperor from 308 to 324. In 313 he and Constantine the Great agreed the policy of religious toleration known as the Edict of Milan, and he went on to defeat Maximinus Daia and rule the eastern provinces.

lester-b-pearson.s: Lester B. Pearson was a Canadian diplomat and Liberal prime minister of Canada from 1963 to 1968.

luther-bible.s: The Luther Bible is Martin Luther's translation of the Bible into German, from the Hebrew and Greek, with the New Testament published in 1522 and the complete Bible in 1534. Widely printed and read, it shaped the standard written German language and served as the main Bible of…

lake-zurich.s: Lake Zürich is a lake in northern Switzerland, about 40 kilometres long, stretching south-east from the city of Zürich, which stands where the Limmat flows out of it. Its shores belong mainly to the canton of Zürich, with parts in Schwyz and St.

limmat.s: The Limmat is a river in northern Switzerland that flows out of Lake Zürich through the city of Zürich and runs north-west for about 35 kilometres to join the Aare. The old town of Zürich lies on both banks.

lindenhof.s: The Lindenhof is a hill and public square in the old town of Zürich, above the left bank of the Limmat. A late Roman fort stood there, protecting the customs post of Turicum, and it was later the site of a Carolingian palace.

locarno.s: Locarno is a town in the canton of Ticino in southern Switzerland, on the northern shore of Lake Maggiore. Ruled by the Swiss confederates from 1513, it expelled its Protestant community in 1555, and many of the exiles, including the Orelli and Muralt families, settled in…

locarno-treaties.s: The Locarno Treaties were agreements negotiated at Locarno in Switzerland in October 1925 and signed in London that December. Germany, France and Belgium accepted their common borders, with Britain and Italy as guarantors, and Germany agreed arbitration with its eastern…

lovedale-missionary-institution.s: Lovedale was a mission school founded in 1841 by the Glasgow Missionary Society near Alice in the Eastern Cape. Under principals such as James Stewart it grew into the leading institution for African education in southern Africa, with schools, a press and trades training.

legio-xii-fulminata.s: Legio XII Fulminata, the 'Thunderbolt' legion, was a Roman legion traced back to the armies of Julius Caesar. From the later first century CE it was based at Melitene in Cappadocia, guarding the upper Euphrates frontier.
