lutetia.s: Lutetia was the Gallo-Roman town on the Seine that grew into Paris, the chief town of the Gallic Parisii. Caesar held an assembly of Gaul there in 53 BCE, and in 52 BCE it was burned during the fighting against his legate Labienus.

lead-mosque-shkoder.s: The Lead Mosque is an Ottoman mosque below Rozafa Castle at Shkodër in northern Albania, built in 1773–74 by Mehmed Pasha Bushati. Named after the lead sheets that once covered its domes, it follows the classical Ottoman style of Istanbul.

lord-byron.s: Lord Byron was an English Romantic poet, author of Childe Harold's Pilgrimage and Don Juan, and one of the most famous literary figures of his age. On his travels in 1809 he visited Ali Pasha of Ioannina at Tepelenë, an encounter he described in Childe Harold.

little-rann-of-kutch.s: The Little Rann of Kutch is a seasonal salt marsh in Gujarat, India, south-east of the Great Rann of Kutch. Flooded during the monsoon and a dry salt flat for the rest of the year, it is worked by Agariya salt-makers and is home to the Indian Wild Ass Sanctuary, the last…

larut.s: Larut is a district of northern Perak, Malaysia, centred on the town of Taiping. Rich tin deposits found there in the mid-19th century drew thousands of Chinese miners, and rivalry between Chinese secret societies over the mines led to the Larut Wars of the 1860s and early 1870s.

lucius-antonius.s: Lucius Antonius was a Roman politician, the youngest brother of Mark Antony, and consul in 41 BCE. With Antony's wife Fulvia he raised forces against Octavian over the settlement of veterans in Italy, but was besieged at Perusia in the Perusine War.

lycaon-of-arcadia.s: Lycaon is a mythical king of Arcadia in Greek legend, son of Pelasgus. In the best-known story he served Zeus a meal of human flesh to test the god and was turned into a wolf as punishment.

louisbourg.s: Louisbourg was a fortified French town on Cape Breton Island, then Île Royale, in what is now Nova Scotia, Canada, built from 1713 to guard the Gulf of St Lawrence and the cod fishery. New England forces captured it in 1745, but it was returned to France in 1748; the British…

landak-river.s: The Landak is a river of West Kalimantan, Indonesia, a tributary of the Kapuas that joins it at Pontianak. Its upper valley was the seat of the old Landak sultanate and an area of gold and diamond working.

leopold-anton-von-firmian.s: Leopold Anton von Firmian was prince-archbishop of Salzburg from 1727 to 1744. In 1731 he issued an edict expelling his Protestant subjects, and some 20,000 left, most of them settling in East Prussia at the invitation of King Frederick William I.

league-of-cambrai.s: The League of Cambrai was an alliance formed at Cambrai in December 1508 by Pope Julius II, Emperor Maximilian I, Louis XII of France and Ferdinand II of Aragon against the Republic of Venice. Its armies crushed the Venetians at Agnadello in 1509, but the allies soon fell out,…

leine.s: The Leine is a river in Lower Saxony, Germany, flowing about 280 kilometres north from Thuringia through Göttingen and Hanover to join the Aller. Its valley formed the heart of the Guelph principalities of Göttingen and Calenberg, and the bishops of Hildesheim held lands…

lausanne-disputation.s: The Lausanne Disputation was a public religious debate held in Lausanne in October 1536, after Bern conquered Vaud. Guillaume Farel, Pierre Viret and John Calvin defended the Reformed theses against Catholic speakers, and Bern used the outcome to impose the Reformation…

lavaux.s: Lavaux is a region of terraced vineyards on the north shore of Lake Geneva in the canton of Vaud, Switzerland, between Lausanne and Vevey. The terraces were built from the 11th century under monasteries and the bishops of Lausanne, who owned much of the land.

land-of-lebus.s: The Land of Lebus is a historical region on both banks of the middle Oder around the town of Lebus, in modern Brandenburg and western Poland. Held by the Piast dukes of Poland and Silesia, it was taken by the margraves of Brandenburg around 1250 and became part of the…

lebus.s: Lebus is a small town on the Oder in Brandenburg, Germany, north of Frankfurt (Oder). Once a Slavic stronghold, it became in the 12th century the seat of a Polish bishopric under Gniezno, which later moved to Fürstenwalde, and it gave its name to the surrounding Land of Lebus.

lidzbark-warminski.s: Lidzbark Warmiński (German Heilsberg) is a town in north-eastern Poland. Its brick Gothic castle, built in the 14th century, was the residence of the prince-bishops of Warmia for more than four centuries, until the region passed to Prussia in 1772.

ladenburg.s: Ladenburg is a small town on the Neckar between Heidelberg and Mannheim in Baden-Württemberg, Germany. As Roman Lopodunum it was the chief town of a district on the Neckar.

lykhny.s: Lykhny is a village in the Gudauta district of Abkhazia, near the Black Sea coast. It was a residence of the Shervashidze princes of Abkhazia, whose palace ruins stand beside a 10th-century church with medieval wall paintings.

lake-beloye.s: Lake Beloye, the White Lake, is a large lake in Vologda Oblast in northern Russia, covering about 1,100 square kilometres. Its outflow, the Sheksna, runs south to the Volga.

labourd.s: Labourd (Basque Lapurdi) is one of the three historic Basque provinces of France, on the Atlantic coast near Bayonne, with Ustaritz as its old seat of assembly. It was a viscounty and later part of the English duchy of Aquitaine before returning to the French crown in 1451,…

landulf-i-of-capua.s: Landulf I, called the Old, was the Lombard gastald, or count, of Capua in the early 9th century. During the civil wars of the Principality of Benevento in the 830s and 840s he made Capua practically independent.

lake-galich.s: Lake Galich is a shallow lake in Kostroma Oblast in central Russia, covering about 75 square kilometres, with the town of Galich on its south-eastern shore. Its basin was settled by the Finnic Merya before Slavic colonisation in the early Middle Ages.

lambert-of-hersfeld.s: Lambert of Hersfeld was a Benedictine monk of Hersfeld Abbey in Hesse and one of the leading German chroniclers of the 11th century. His Annals, a world chronicle that becomes detailed from 1040, give a vivid and hostile account of King Henry IV's reign, the Saxon revolt and…

lullus.s: Lullus was an Anglo-Saxon monk from Wessex who joined Saint Boniface's mission in Germany and succeeded him as bishop, later archbishop, of Mainz. Around 769 he refounded Hersfeld as a Benedictine abbey, which became one of the richest monasteries of the Frankish realm.

latgalians.s: The Latgalians were a Baltic tribe of eastern Latvia, settled along the Daugava and in the uplands to the east by the late first millennium. Their lands included the principalities of Jersika, Koknese and Talava, and some had become Orthodox Christians under Rus' influence.

lengvenis.s: Lengvenis, baptised Simeon, was a son of Grand Duke Algirdas of Lithuania and a brother of Jogaila. He held the appanage of Mstislavl from about 1390, served Novgorod for a time as its prince and military commander, and is credited with leading the Smolensk banners at the…

louis-alexandre-berthier.s: Louis-Alexandre Berthier was a French marshal and Napoleon's chief of staff from 1796 to 1814. He occupied Rome in 1798, when the Roman Republic was proclaimed, and organised the staff work behind Napoleon's campaigns.

la-chaux-de-fonds.s: La Chaux-de-Fonds is a town in the Jura mountains of the canton of Neuchâtel, Switzerland, at about 1,000 metres. Rebuilt on a grid plan after a fire in 1794, it grew into a world centre of watchmaking, and together with Le Locle it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site for its…

le-locle.s: Le Locle is a town in the Jura mountains of the canton of Neuchâtel, Switzerland, near the French border. Watchmaking took root there around 1700, traditionally through Daniel JeanRichard, and it became with La Chaux-de-Fonds a world centre of the industry; the two towns are a…

ludwig-of-oettingen-wallerstein.s: Prince Ludwig of Oettingen-Wallerstein was a Bavarian statesman who served King Ludwig I as interior minister from 1832 to 1837 and led the government again in 1847–1848, during the crisis over the king's affair with Lola Montez. He had given up the headship of his house to…

lake-pleshcheyevo.s: Lake Pleshcheyevo is a lake in Yaroslavl Oblast, Russia, on whose south-eastern shore stands Pereslavl-Zalessky. In the late 1680s and early 1690s the young Peter the Great built a flotilla of small ships there, regarded as a forerunner of the Russian navy, and his surviving…

laba-river.s: The Laba is a river of the north-western Caucasus, a left tributary of the Kuban about 210 kilometres long, formed by the Greater and Lesser Laba, which rise on the slopes of the Main Caucasus Range. Its valley was home to Circassian tribes such as the Temirgoy, Hatuqwai and…

lutsk.s: Lutsk is a city in north-western Ukraine on the Styr river, capital of Volyn Oblast. A town of medieval Volhynia, it became the main seat of the Lithuanian prince Lubart, whose brick castle still stands.

lezaky.s: Ležáky was a small settlement in eastern Bohemia, in the Chrudim district of the Czech Republic, destroyed by the Nazis on 24 June 1942 in reprisal for the assassination of Reinhard Heydrich. A radio transmitter of the Czechoslovak resistance had been hidden there.

lidice.s: Lidice is a village near Kladno in the Czech Republic, destroyed by the Nazis on 10 June 1942 in reprisal for the assassination of Reinhard Heydrich. The men were shot, the women sent to Ravensbrück concentration camp and most of the children murdered, and the village was razed.

lokoja.s: Lokoja is a city in central Nigeria at the confluence of the Niger and Benue rivers, capital of Kogi State. An early British trading and missionary station, it served from 1900 as the first headquarters of the Protectorate of Northern Nigeria under Frederick Lugard, before the…

louis-hippolyte-lafontaine.s: Louis-Hippolyte LaFontaine was a French-Canadian politician who led the Reformers of Canada East after the union of 1841. In alliance with Robert Baldwin he formed the ministry of 1848 that brought responsible government to the Province of Canada.

lygonia.s: Lygonia was a proprietary province in present-day southern Maine, based on the Plough Patent of 1630, which the English Puritan lawyer Alexander Rigby bought in 1643. Its claims overlapped those of Sir Ferdinando Gorges's Province of Maine, and in 1646 English commissioners…

leislers-rebellion.s: Leisler's Rebellion was an uprising in colonial New York from 1689 to 1691, after news of the Glorious Revolution and the collapse of the Dominion of New England. The German-born merchant and militia captain Jacob Leisler seized control of the colony in the name of William and…

leopoldo-odonnell.s: Leopoldo O'Donnell was a Spanish general and politician of Irish descent who led the Liberal Union and served three times as prime minister between 1856 and 1866. His long government of 1858 to 1863 waged the Hispano-Moroccan War of 1859–1860, for which he was made Duke of…

lord-william-campbell.s: Lord William Campbell was a Scottish naval officer, governor of Nova Scotia from 1766 to 1773 and the last royal governor of South Carolina, arriving in Charleston in 1775. Unable to control the revolutionary authorities, he fled to a British warship in September 1775.

luigj-gurakuqi.s: Luigj Gurakuqi was an Albanian writer and politician from Shkodër who signed the declaration of independence at Vlorë in 1912 and served as minister of education in Ismail Qemali's provisional government. He promoted Albanian-language schooling and literature, and later served…

lorrin-a-thurston.s: Lorrin A. Thurston was a Honolulu lawyer and publisher, grandson of American missionaries, who led the Committee of Safety that overthrew Queen Liliʻuokalani in January 1893.

lithuanian-activist-front.s: The Lithuanian Activist Front was an anti-Soviet resistance organisation founded in Berlin in November 1940 by Kazys Škirpa. It organised the June Uprising of 1941 when Germany invaded the Soviet Union and formed the Provisional Government of Lithuania, which the Germans…

lake-patzcuaro.s: Lake Pátzcuaro is a highland lake in Michoacán, Mexico, at about 2,000 metres above sea level. Its basin was the heartland of the Purépecha state, with the capitals Pátzcuaro, Ihuatzio and Tzintzuntzan on its shores, and its island of Janitzio is famous for Day of the Dead…

li-yiji.s: Li Yiji was a Chinese scholar and adviser to Liu Bang, founder of the Han dynasty, during the Chu–Han Contention. Sent as an envoy to Qi, he persuaded its king Tian Guang to submit to Han, but the general Han Xin attacked Qi regardless; believing himself betrayed, Tian Guang…

long-ju.s: Long Ju was a general of Xiang Yu, king of Western Chu, during the Chu–Han Contention. Sent with a large army to help Qi against the Han general Han Xin, he was defeated and killed at the Battle of Wei River, where Han Xin is said to have released a dam of sandbags upstream to…

lingqu.s: The Lingqu is a canal in Xing'an county, Guangxi, southern China, completed around 214 BCE on the orders of Qin Shi Huang to supply his armies campaigning against the Baiyue. About 36 kilometres long, it links the Xiang River, flowing to the Yangtze, with the Li River, flowing…

lanzhou.s: Lanzhou is the capital of Gansu province in north-western China, on the upper Yellow River. Known in Sui times as Jincheng, it guarded a crossing of the Yellow River on the road to the Hexi Corridor and the Silk Road, and was the base of the rebel Xue Ju, who founded a…

lapulapu.s: Lapulapu was a chief of Mactan, an island off Cebu in the central Philippines, who refused to submit to Spain. On 27 April 1521 his warriors defeated a Spanish landing party at the Battle of Mactan and killed Ferdinand Magellan.

lucius-munatius-plancus.s: Lucius Munatius Plancus was a Roman general and politician. A legate of Julius Caesar in Gaul, he founded the colonies of Lugdunum (Lyon) and Augusta Raurica around 44–43 BCE, and later changed sides between Mark Antony and Octavian.

liber-paradisus.s: The Liber Paradisus is a law of the commune of Bologna, issued in 1256 and recorded in 1257, which freed the serfs of the city's countryside by buying their freedom from their lords. It lists the names of nearly 6,000 serfs and their owners, and the freed peasants became…

louis-rwagasore.s: Prince Louis Rwagasore was a Burundian nationalist, son of Mwami Mwambutsa IV, who led the UPRONA party to victory in the elections of September 1961. He became prime minister but was assassinated in October 1961 by a Greek gunman hired by politicians of a rival party.

la-violencia.s: La Violencia was a civil conflict in Colombia between supporters of the Liberal and Conservative parties, usually dated from 1948 to 1958. Sparked by the assassination of Jorge Eliécer Gaitán, it spread through the countryside in massacres, guerrilla war and police terror,…

la-demajagua.s: La Demajagua was the sugar estate of Carlos Manuel de Céspedes near Manzanillo in eastern Cuba. There, on 10 October 1868, Céspedes freed his slaves and proclaimed Cuban independence in the Grito de Yara, beginning the Ten Years' War.

lorenzo-de-medici.s: Lorenzo de' Medici, called the Magnificent, was the effective ruler of the Republic of Florence from 1469 until his death. He survived the Pazzi conspiracy of 1478, in which his brother Giuliano was killed, and worked to keep peace among the Italian states through diplomacy.

l-escalade.s: L'Escalade was a surprise night attack on Geneva on 11–12 December 1602 by troops of Charles Emmanuel I, Duke of Savoy, who tried to scale the city walls with ladders. The citizens beat off the assault, and the Treaty of Saint-Julien of 1603 recognised the city's independence…

leman-department.s: Léman was a department of the French Republic and Empire created in 1798, after France annexed the Republic of Geneva. Its capital was Geneva, and it took its name from Lake Geneva, Lac Léman in French.

lord-william-bentinck.s: Lord William Bentinck was a British soldier and statesman. As British commander in Sicily he landed at Genoa in April 1814, took the city from the French and encouraged a restored republic, which the Congress of Vienna then gave to the Kingdom of Sardinia.

lithuanian-jews.s: Lithuanian Jews, or Litvaks, were the Jewish community of the lands of the historic Grand Duchy of Lithuania, centred on Vilnius, known as the 'Jerusalem of Lithuania'. From the 18th century they were renowned for Talmudic scholarship, led by figures such as the Vilna Gaon,…

liber-abaci.s: Liber Abaci (the Book of Calculation) is a treatise on arithmetic completed by Leonardo of Pisa, known as Fibonacci, in 1202 and revised in 1228. It taught the Hindu–Arabic numerals and their use in commercial arithmetic, such as bookkeeping, currency conversion and the…

luchino-dal-verme.s: Luchino dal Verme was an Italian condottiero from Verona who served the Visconti of Milan and the Republic of Venice. In 1364 Venice hired him to command the army that put down the Revolt of Saint Titus in Crete, and he retook Candia in May of that year.

lower-valais.s: The Lower Valais is the French-speaking western part of the canton of Valais in Switzerland, along the Rhône from below Sion to Lake Geneva. Conquered in stages from Savoy by the German-speaking Upper Valais in 1475 and 1536, it was ruled as a subject territory until 1798,…

leuk.s: Leuk is a small town in the canton of Valais, Switzerland, on a terrace above the Rhône close to the boundary between German and French speech. It was the seat of one of the seven tenths (Zenden) of the Republic of the Valais and keeps a medieval bishop's castle and town hall…

lausanne.s: Lausanne is a city on the northern shore of Lake Geneva, the capital of the Swiss canton of Vaud. It was the seat of a bishopric from about 600, and its bishops ruled the town as princes until Bern conquered Vaud in 1536 and introduced the Reformation.

lingga-islands.s: The Lingga Islands are an archipelago south of Singapore in the Riau Islands province of Indonesia, centred on Lingga Island. After the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824 they formed, with the Riau Islands, the Dutch-protected Riau-Lingga Sultanate, whose sultans resided at Daik on…

lanceiros-negros.s: The Lanceiros Negros ('Black Lancers') were cavalry units of enslaved and freed black men who fought for the Riograndense Republic during the Ragamuffin War in southern Brazil, on the promise of freedom. In November 1844 many were killed in a surprise attack at Porongos, an…

londinium.s: Londinium was the Roman city on the site of London, founded around 50 CE at the lowest bridging point of the Thames. Destroyed by Boudica's revolt in 60 or 61, it was rebuilt and became the largest city and probable capital of Roman Britain, with a forum, basilica,…

libya-inferior.s: Libya Inferior, also called Libya Sicca, was a late Roman province created by Diocletian's division of Cyrenaica around 300 CE. It covered the dry eastern part of the region, the Marmarica between Cyrenaica and Egypt, with Paraetonium as its chief town, while the western…

latium.s: Latium was the region of central Italy between the Tiber and the Bay of Naples, inhabited by the Latins, who gave their name to the Latin language. Rome rose to dominate the Latin League and absorbed the region after the Latin War of 340–338 BCE.

lucretia.s: Lucretia was, according to Roman tradition, a noblewoman whose rape by Sextus Tarquinius, son of the king, and her subsequent suicide provoked the overthrow of the Roman monarchy in 509 BCE. Her story, told by Livy, became a celebrated subject of later literature and art,…

lambaesis.s: Lambaesis was a Roman military base and city in Numidia, in north-eastern Algeria, at the foot of the Aurès Mountains. From the early 2nd century it was the headquarters of the Third Augustan Legion, which guarded the African frontier, and from around 198 the seat of the…

lucius-postumius-megellus.s: Lucius Postumius Megellus was a Roman general and politician of the Samnite Wars, consul in 305, 294 and 291 BCE. According to Livy, in his second consulship he stormed the Etruscan city of Rusellae, taking some 2,000 prisoners.

la-graufesenque.s: La Graufesenque is an archaeological site near Millau in southern France, the remains of the Roman pottery centre of Condatomagus. In the 1st century CE its workshops produced vast quantities of red-gloss terra sigillata pottery, exported across the Roman world from Britain to…

lihula.s: Lihula is a small town in western Estonia, in Lääne County. In the early 13th century its stronghold was the centre of the Estonian land of Läänemaa, and in 1220 Oeselian islanders destroyed a Swedish garrison there.

lembitu.s: Lembitu was an Estonian elder of Sakala, based at the hillfort of Lehola, who led resistance to the German crusaders in the early 13th century. He built alliances among the Estonian lands and sought help from Novgorod and Pskov.

livonian-chronicle-of-henry.s: The Livonian Chronicle of Henry is a Latin chronicle of the conquest and conversion of Livonia and Estonia by German crusaders, written around 1225–1227 by Henry of Livonia, a priest who took part in the events. Covering the years from about 1180 to 1227, it is the main…

lacantun-river.s: The Lacantún is a river of the Lacandon Forest in eastern Chiapas, Mexico, and a tributary of the Usumacinta. In the 17th century the independent Lacandon Ch'ol Maya had their town of Sakbajlan near its banks, until Spanish expeditions from Guatemala and Chiapas reached it in…

lake-miramar.s: Lake Miramar is a lake in the Lacandon Forest of eastern Chiapas, Mexico. In the 16th century its island town of Lacam Tun was the stronghold of the Ch'ol-speaking Lacandon Maya, who raided Spanish-held areas until an expedition destroyed it in 1586.

la-pampa-province.s: La Pampa is a province of central Argentina, with its capital at Santa Rosa, covering part of the pampas plains and the drier lands to the west. Until the Conquest of the Desert of 1878–1879 it was largely held by Ranquel and Mapuche peoples.

lhokseumawe.s: Lhokseumawe is a city on the north coast of Aceh province in Sumatra, Indonesia. The remains of Samudera Pasai, one of the first Muslim states of Southeast Asia, including the tomb of Sultan Malik al-Salih dated 1297, lie nearby.

la-reforma.s: La Reforma was a period of liberal reform in Mexico that began after the Revolution of Ayutla overthrew Antonio López de Santa Anna in 1855. Laws such as the Ley Juárez and the Ley Lerdo curtailed the legal privileges of the Church and the army and forced the sale of corporate…

ley-juarez.s: The Ley Juárez was a Mexican law of November 1855, drafted by Benito Juárez as minister of justice, that abolished the special courts of the clergy and the military for civil cases. Part of the liberal programme of La Reforma, it was the first of the reform laws that limited…

ley-lerdo.s: The Ley Lerdo was a Mexican law of June 1856, named after the finance minister Miguel Lerdo de Tejada, that required the Church and civil corporations, including indigenous communities, to sell their landed property. Intended to create a class of small landowners and raise…

la-guaira.s: La Guaira is the main port of Venezuela, on the Caribbean coast just north of Caracas, from which it is separated by the coastal mountain range. Fortified in the colonial era, it handled much of the country's trade, including cocoa exports.

lyon.s: Lyon is a city in east-central France at the confluence of the Rhône and Saône. Founded in 43 BCE as the Roman colony of Lugdunum, it became the capital of the Three Gauls and later a seat of the Burgundian kings.

lesbos.s: Lesbos is a large Greek island in the north-eastern Aegean, close to the coast of Anatolia, with its chief town at Mytilene. Probably the Lazpa of Hittite texts, it was home in the archaic period to the poets Sappho and Alcaeus and to the rival cities of Mytilene and Methymna.

lombok.s: Lombok is an island of Indonesia's West Nusa Tenggara province, lying between Bali and Sumbawa and dominated by the volcano Rinjani. It was home to several Sasak principalities before Balinese princes of Karangasem conquered much of it in the 17th and 18th centuries.

lielupe.s: The Lielupe is a river of central Latvia, formed near Bauska by the meeting of the Mūša and Mēmele, which rise in Lithuania. It flows about 119 km across the Zemgale plain to the Gulf of Riga near Jūrmala.

lower-creek.s: The Lower Creek were the Muscogee towns on the Chattahoochee and Flint rivers in present-day Georgia and Alabama, distinguished from the Upper Creek towns further west. Many spoke Hitchiti rather than Muscogee.

lakshman-sena.s: Lakshman Sena was the last major king of the Sena dynasty of Bengal, reigning in the late 12th and early 13th centuries. His court at Nabadwip patronised Sanskrit poets, among them Jayadeva, the author of the Gita Govinda.

longhouse-religion.s: The Longhouse Religion is a Haudenosaunee faith founded by the Seneca prophet Handsome Lake after his visions of 1799. It combines the traditional cycle of thanksgiving ceremonies with a moral code, the Gaiwiio, that condemned alcohol and witchcraft and stressed family life.

lyubech.s: Lyubech is a small town on the Dnieper in Chernihiv Oblast, northern Ukraine. Mentioned in the Primary Chronicle under the year 882, it is one of the oldest towns of Kievan Rus' and lay in the land of the Severians.

lazarevskoye.s: Lazarevskoye is a resort settlement on the Black Sea coast of Russia, now part of the city of Sochi in Krasnodar Krai. It grew from a Russian fort founded in 1839 during the conquest of the Circassian coast and named after Admiral Mikhail Lazarev.

labayu.s: Labayu was ruler of Shechem in the hill country of Canaan in the mid-14th century BCE, known from the Amarna letters. While professing loyalty to the pharaoh, he enlarged his territory at the expense of neighbouring Egyptian vassals, provoking complaints from the rulers of…

liwa-oasis.s: Liwa Oasis is a crescent of date-growing oases on the northern edge of the Rub' al Khali desert in the south of the emirate of Abu Dhabi. It was the home of the Bani Yas tribes and of the Al Nahyan family before they moved their seat to Abu Dhabi island in the 1790s.

lewis-pelly.s: Lewis Pelly was a British officer and diplomat who served as Political Resident in the Persian Gulf from 1862 to 1872. After the war between Bahrain and the Qataris in 1867, he signed an agreement with Muhammad bin Thani in 1868 that effectively recognised Qatar as distinct…

lysippus.s: Lysippus was a Greek sculptor from Sicyon, active in the 4th century BCE and one of the most prolific bronze-workers of antiquity. He introduced slimmer proportions with smaller heads, seen in his Apoxyomenos, an athlete scraping himself, and was the court sculptor of…

llanmelin.s: Llanmelin is an Iron Age hillfort near Caerwent in Monmouthshire, south-east Wales, defended by multiple ramparts and ditches. Occupied from around the 4th century BCE until the Roman conquest, it is thought to have been a major centre of the Silures before the Romans moved…

lawrence-wong.s: Lawrence Wong (born 1972) is a Singaporean politician who became the fourth prime minister of Singapore in May 2024, succeeding Lee Hsien Loong. An economist and former civil servant, he co-chaired the government's task force on the COVID-19 pandemic and served as finance…

lingaraja-temple.s: The Lingaraja Temple is the largest temple of Bhubaneswar in Odisha, dedicated to Shiva as Harihara. Built in the 11th century, mainly under the Somavamshi kings, it is the high point of the Kalinga style, with a curving tower about 55 m high rising over a walled compound of…

limes-sorabicus.s: The Limes Sorabicus was the eastern frontier zone of the Carolingian Empire facing the Slavic Sorbs, running roughly along the Saale and the Elbe in present-day central Germany. Set up after Charlemagne's campaigns against the Sorbs in the early 9th century, it was a line of…

lot-et-garonne.s: Lot-et-Garonne is a department of south-western France in the Nouvelle-Aquitaine region, named after the Lot and Garonne rivers, which meet within it, with its prefecture at Agen. Created in 1790 from parts of the old provinces of Guyenne and Gascony, it is an agricultural…

lingnan.s: Lingnan ('south of the ranges') is the historical name for the region of southern China beyond the Nanling Mountains, covering modern Guangdong, Guangxi and Hainan and at times northern Vietnam. Conquered by the Qin and then ruled by the independent kingdom of Nanyue, it was…

liu-yan-southern-han.s: Liu Yan (889–942) was the founding emperor of Southern Han, one of the Ten Kingdoms of 10th-century China. Succeeding his brother Liu Yin as military governor of Lingnan at Guangzhou, he proclaimed himself emperor of Great Yue in 917 and renamed the state Han in 918.

liu-yin-southern-han.s: Liu Yin (874–911) was a Chinese general of the late Tang dynasty who became military governor of Lingnan at Guangzhou in the early 10th century. From a family enriched by the southern trade, he built up an autonomous regional power that the Later Liang dynasty recognised by…

longwu-emperor.s: The Longwu Emperor (1602–1646), Zhu Yujian, was the second emperor of the Southern Ming. Proclaimed at Fuzhou in 1645 with the support of the Zheng family of Fujian, he tried to organise resistance to the Qing, but the merchant-admiral Zheng Zhilong abandoned him.

land-apportionment-act.s: The Land Apportionment Act of 1930 was a law of the British colony of Southern Rhodesia that divided land by race. It reserved about half of the country, including the best farmland and the towns, for the small white minority and confined Africans, the great majority, to…

lu-xiufu.s: Lu Xiufu (1236–1279) was a Chinese official of the Southern Song dynasty and one of its last loyalist leaders. After the Mongols took the capital Lin'an in 1276, he and the general Zhang Shijie led the remnant court in flight along the southern coast.

leipzig.s: Leipzig is a city in Saxony, eastern Germany, that grew from a medieval market town into one of Europe's great trade-fair centres. Its university, founded in 1409, and its book trade made it a centre of learning, and Johann Sebastian Bach worked there from 1723.

lille.s: Lille is a city in northern France near the Belgian border, historically the chief town of Walloon Flanders. Part of the County of Flanders and later the Burgundian and Habsburg Netherlands, it was taken by Louis XIV in 1667 and became French by the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle…

laayoune.s: Laayoune is the largest city of Western Sahara, near the Atlantic coast and the seasonal river Saguia el-Hamra. Founded by Spain in 1938 as a military post, it grew into the capital of the colony of Spanish Sahara and the outlet for the phosphates of Bou Craa.

los-adaes.s: Los Adaes was a Spanish mission and presidio near present-day Robeline in north-western Louisiana, founded in 1721 to block French expansion from Natchitoches. From 1729 to 1772 it served as the capital of the province of Texas.

lycurgus-of-sparta.s: Lycurgus was the legendary lawgiver of Sparta, credited by the Spartans with their constitution of two kings, council of elders and assembly, and with the strict system of public education, communal messes and military discipline. Ancient writers placed him between the…

liberation-tigers-of-tamil-eelam.s: The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam were a Tamil separatist militant organisation in Sri Lanka, founded in 1976 by Velupillai Prabhakaran to create an independent Tamil state, Tamil Eelam, in the north and east. During the civil war from 1983 they controlled large areas, ran…

linzi.s: Linzi was the capital of the State of Qi for most of the Zhou period until its conquest by Qin in 221 BCE, on the site of the modern district of Linzi in Zibo, Shandong. One of the largest cities of the Warring States period, it was famous for its crowded markets, its wealth…

les-cayes.s: Les Cayes is a port city on the southern coast of Haiti, capital of the Sud department. In the colonial and revolutionary periods it was the main town of the southern peninsula and the stronghold of André Rigaud, who based his separate southern government there in 1810–1811.

li-kui.s: Li Kui was a minister of Marquis Wen of Wei in the late 5th century BCE and an early Legalist reformer. He promoted the full use of farmland and state granaries to steady grain prices, and compiled the Canon of Laws, which tradition says Shang Yang took to Qin.

lord-xinling.s: Lord Xinling, personal name Wei Wuji, was a prince of the State of Wei and one of the Four Lords of the Warring States period, famed for their thousands of retainers. In 257 BCE he stole his brother's military tally, seized command of the Wei army and relieved the Qin siege of…

lord-mengchang.s: Lord Mengchang, personal name Tian Wen, was a prince and minister of the State of Qi in the late 4th and early 3rd centuries BCE, one of the Four Lords of the Warring States period. Holding the fief of Xue, he kept several thousand retainers, whose tricks, such as imitating a…

liaodong.s: Liaodong is the region of north-east China east of the Liao River, including the Liaodong Peninsula between the Bohai Sea and Korea Bay. Held by the State of Yan and then by Chinese empires as a commandery, it was later contested by Goguryeo, the Khitan, the Jurchen and the…

liulihe.s: Liulihe is an archaeological site in Fangshan District, south-west of Beijing, identified as the early capital of the Western Zhou State of Yan. Excavations since the 1970s have uncovered a walled town and a cemetery whose bronzes record the enfeoffment of the Duke of Shao's…

li-mu.s: Li Mu was a general of the State of Zhao in the 3rd century BCE. Stationed on the northern frontier, he destroyed a large Xiongnu army in the 240s BCE, and he later defeated Qin invasions in 233 and 232 BCE.

lian-po.s: Lian Po was a leading general of the State of Zhao in the 3rd century BCE, known for victories over Qi and Qin. At Changping in 260 BCE he held a defensive line against Qin until Zhao replaced him with Zhao Kuo, whose army was destroyed.

lin-xiangru.s: Lin Xiangru was a minister of the State of Zhao in the 3rd century BCE. In a famous episode he took the He Shi jade disc to the Qin court and, seeing that the king would not hand over the promised cities, sent it safely back to Zhao.

lippe-river.s: The Lippe is a river in western Germany, about 220 km long, rising near Paderborn and flowing west through Westphalia to join the Rhine at Wesel. In antiquity it was a main route of Roman advances into Germania, with legionary bases such as Oberaden and Haltern along its banks.

leon-humblot.s: Léon Humblot was a French naturalist and adventurer who went to Grande Comore in 1884 to collect plants. He backed Said Ali of Bambao as sultan of the whole island, and in 1886 obtained both a French protectorate and a concession over much of the island's land.

linggabuana.s: Linggabuana was king of Sunda in western Java from about 1350 to 1357. He travelled to Majapahit with his daughter Dyah Pitaloka for her marriage to King Hayam Wuruk, but was killed with his followers in the Battle of Bubat after refusing Gajah Mada's demand that she be…

lancaster-pennsylvania.s: Lancaster is a city in south-eastern Pennsylvania, in a fertile farming county near the lower Susquehanna River. The area was home to the Susquehannock, and after their decline the Conestoga lived nearby; in 1763 the Paxton Boys killed the last Conestoga there.

louis-de-geer.s: Louis De Geer was a Dutch-born merchant and industrialist who became the leading entrepreneur of 17th-century Sweden. Settling there in the 1620s, he developed the ironworks of Uppland, brought in Walloon smiths, became the main arms supplier of the Swedish crown during the…

lower-march-al-andalus.s: The Lower March (al-Thaghr al-Adna) was the western frontier district of Umayyad al-Andalus, facing the Christian kingdom of León. Centred first on Mérida and later on Badajoz, founded in the 870s by the rebel Ibn Marwan, it was one of three marches alongside the Middle and…

lahari-bandar.s: Lahari Bandar was the main seaport of lower Sindh in the 16th and 17th centuries, on a branch of the Indus delta near Thatta, in today's Pakistan. Under the Tarkhans and then the Mughals it traded with Gujarat, the Persian Gulf and the Portuguese, but the silting of the river…

lake-buir.s: Lake Buir is a freshwater lake on the border between eastern Mongolia and Inner Mongolia in China, linked by the Orshuun River to Hulun Lake. The grasslands around the two lakes were home to the medieval Tatar tribes and other steppe peoples.

lubombo-mountains.s: The Lubombo Mountains are a long, narrow range of hills in southern Africa, running north to south along the borders of South Africa, Eswatini and Mozambique. Formed of volcanic rock, they separate the lowveld of Eswatini from the coastal plain of Mozambique.

lade-trondheim.s: Lade is an area of Trondheim, Norway, on the Lade peninsula east of the city centre, once a great farm and seat of power. From the 9th to the early 11th century it was the residence of the earls of Lade, who ruled Trøndelag and at times much of Norway, among them Haakon…

lae.s: Lae is the second-largest city of Papua New Guinea and capital of Morobe Province, at the mouth of the Markham River on the Huon Gulf. It grew in the 1920s and 1930s as the air base for the Bulolo goldfields, and Amelia Earhart took off from there on her last flight in 1937.

lucius-verus.s: Lucius Verus was Roman emperor from 161 to 169 CE, ruling jointly with his adoptive brother Marcus Aurelius, the first time two emperors shared power as equals. He nominally led the war against Parthia of 161–166, whose returning armies spread the Antonine Plague.

leucon-i.s: Leucon I was ruler of the Bosporan Kingdom from 389 to 349 BCE, of the Spartocid dynasty. He took Theodosia and extended his rule over the Sindi and Maeotians east of the Kerch Strait, turning a union of Greek cities into a territorial state.

laus.s: Laus was an ancient Greek city on the Tyrrhenian coast of southern Italy, near the mouth of the Lao river in modern Calabria, founded as a colony of Sybaris. Near it, in 389 BCE, the Lucanians crushed an army of Thurii and its Italiote allies.

lualaba.s: The Lualaba is the upper course of the Congo River, flowing north through the south-east of the Democratic Republic of the Congo from the Katanga highlands to Boyoma Falls near Kisangani, below which it is called the Congo. In the 19th century its banks, with trading towns…

lal-kot.s: Lal Kot is the earliest identifiable fortified city of Delhi, a citadel in the south of the modern city whose building is attributed to the Tomara king Anangapala II in the 11th century. The Chahamana ruler Prithviraj Chauhan extended it as Qila Rai Pithora in the 12th…

lau-islands.s: The Lau Islands are a scattered group of about sixty islands in eastern Fiji, lying towards Tonga, with Lakeba and Vanua Balavu among the largest. Close contact with Tonga brought Tongan settlers and Wesleyan Christianity, and in the mid-19th century the Tongan noble Enele…

licario.s: Licario was a knight of Italian descent from Euboea who, after a quarrel with the Lombard lords of the island, entered the service of the Byzantine emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos. In the 1270s he led Byzantine campaigns that recaptured much of Euboea and several Aegean…

lupus-of-troyes.s: Lupus of Troyes was bishop of Troyes in Gaul from about 427 until his death around 478 and is venerated as a saint. With Germanus of Auxerre he travelled to Britain around 429 to oppose Pelagianism.

lexden-tumulus.s: The Lexden Tumulus is a large burial mound at Lexden, on the western edge of Colchester in Essex, dating to about 15–10 BCE. Excavated in 1924, it held the cremated remains of a person of high rank with rich grave goods, including Roman imports and a silver medallion bearing…

lorca.s: Lorca is a city in the Region of Murcia in south-eastern Spain, on the Guadalentín river below a large castle. It was one of the seven towns named in the treaty of 713 between the Visigothic lord Theodemir and the Muslim conquerors.

laufilitonga.s: Laufilitonga was the last Tuʻi Tonga, the sacred paramount chief of Tonga. During the civil wars of the early 19th century he was defeated in 1826 by Tāufaʻāhau, the future King George Tupou I, who went on to unite the islands under his own rule.

lewiston-new-york.s: Lewiston is a town in Niagara County, in western New York, on the Niagara River below the falls and across from Queenston, Ontario. The reservation of the Tuscarora Nation, which settled among the Seneca after migrating north from North Carolina in the 18th century, lies…

lycophron-of-pherae.s: Lycophron of Pherae was the first tyrant of Pherae in Thessaly, seizing power around 406 BCE. Aiming to dominate all Thessaly, he defeated the Larissaeans and other rivals in 404 BCE and he fought the aristocratic families of Larissa and Pharsalus in the following years.

lugalbanda.s: Lugalbanda was a legendary king of Uruk named in the Sumerian King List, said to be the father of Gilgamesh and the husband of the goddess Ninsun. Two Sumerian epic poems tell of his adventures in the mountains while campaigning with Enmerkar against Aratta, including his…

lavanaprasada.s: Lavanaprasada was a chief of the Vaghela branch of the Chaulukya family of Gujarat. In the early 13th century he and his son Viradhavala acted as regents and generals for the weak Chaulukya king Bhima II, defending the kingdom against Muslim and Yadava attacks from their base…

luna-vasahi.s: The Luna Vasahi is a white marble Jain temple dedicated to Neminatha in the Dilwara temple complex at Mount Abu, Rajasthan, India. It was built in 1230 by the minister Tejapala, brother of Vastupala, in memory of his son Lunasimha.

linh-nam-chich-quai.s: The Linh Nam chich quai ('Strange Tales from Linh Nam') is a collection of Vietnamese legends written in classical Chinese, compiled in its surviving form in the 15th century. It tells the origins of the Vietnamese people from Lac Long Quan and Au Co, the Hung kings of Van…

landes-forest.s: The Landes forest is a vast pine forest in south-west France, covering about a million hectares of the Landes of Gascony between the Gironde and the Adour. Until the 19th century the region was mostly sandy heath and marsh, grazed by shepherds on stilts.

le-puy-en-velay.s: Le Puy-en-Velay is a town in the Massif Central of southern France, capital of the Haute-Loire department, built among volcanic pinnacles. As Anicium it replaced Ruessium as the seat of the bishops of the Velay in late antiquity.

lake-fundudzi.s: Lake Fundudzi is a lake in the Soutpansberg mountains of Limpopo province, South Africa, formed when a landslide dammed the Mutale river. It is sacred to the Venda people, who believe it is guarded by a python god and by the spirits of their ancestors.

libro-doro.s: The Libro d'Oro, or Golden Book, was the official register of the patrician families of the Republic of Venice, recording the births and marriages that qualified men to sit in the Great Council. Kept from the early 16th century, it embodied the closed hereditary nobility…

las-cogotas.s: Las Cogotas is an Iron Age hillfort near Cardeñosa in the province of Ávila, Spain, and one of the main oppida of the Vettones. Excavated by Juan Cabré from 1927, it had two walled enclosures, a large cremation cemetery and stone boar sculptures.

lescar.s: Lescar is a town near Pau in the Pyrénées-Atlantiques department of south-western France. Usually identified with the Roman town of Beneharnum, which gave its name to Béarn, it was an early seat of the viscounts and the see of the bishops of Lescar until 1790.

liuvigild.s: Liuvigild (Leovigild) was king of the Visigoths from about 568 to 586 and the main architect of their kingdom in Hispania. He made Toledo his capital, fought the Byzantines in the south, subdued the Cantabrians and in 585 annexed the Suebic kingdom of Galicia.

life-of-methodius.s: The Life of Methodius is an Old Church Slavonic biography of Saint Methodius, apostle of the Slavs, written in Moravia soon after his death in 885, probably by one of his disciples. With the Life of Constantine-Cyril it is the main source for the Byzantine mission to Great…

ladislaus-iv-of-hungary.s: Ladislaus IV, called the Cuman after his mother's people, was king of Hungary from 1272 to 1290. Crowned as a child, he struggled with baronial factions throughout his reign.

litovoi.s: Litovoi was a Romanian voivode of the 13th century whose land lay along the Jiu and Olt in what became Oltenia, known from Hungarian royal charters. Béla IV's charter of 1247 to the Knights Hospitaller left his knezate in Romanian hands, and a charter of 1285 says that a…

lothian.s: Lothian is the region of south-eastern Scotland between the Firth of Forth and the Lammermuir Hills, around Edinburgh. Home of the Votadini and the British kingdom of Gododdin, it was conquered by Northumbria in the 7th century and passed to the kings of Scots in the 10th and…

lucien-bonaparte.s: Lucien Bonaparte was a younger brother of Napoleon. As president of the Council of Five Hundred he secured the success of the coup of 18 Brumaire in 1799, but he later quarrelled with Napoleon and settled in the Papal States as Prince of Canino.

la-tadampare-puang-ri-magalatung.s: La Tadampare Puang ri Ma'galatung was an Arung Matoa, or elected ruler, of the Bugis kingdom of Wajo in South Sulawesi around the turn of the 16th century. Bugis chronicles remember him as Wajo's wisest ruler, a statesman whose sayings on government, justice and the rights of…

lake-tempe.s: Lake Tempe is a shallow lake in South Sulawesi, Indonesia, lying mainly in Wajo Regency west of the town of Sengkang. It is fed by rivers from the surrounding lowlands, and its size varies greatly between the wet and dry seasons.

luhya-people.s: The Luhya, or Abaluhya, are a Bantu-speaking people of western Kenya made up of some eighteen sub-groups, such as the Bukusu, Maragoli, Wanga and Tiriki, who speak closely related languages. They live mainly in the fertile farming country between Mount Elgon and Lake Victoria.

lyna.s: The Łyna, in German the Alle, is a river of about 290 kilometres that rises in the Masurian lake district of northern Poland and flows north through Olsztyn and Lidzbark Warmiński into Russia's Kaliningrad Oblast, where it joins the Pregolya. Its valley was settled by the…

liugong-island.s: Liugong Island is a small island at the entrance to the harbour of Weihai in Shandong, China. It was the base of the Qing Beiyang Fleet, which was destroyed there by Japan in the Battle of Weihaiwei in 1895.

lough-gill.s: Lough Gill is a freshwater lake on the border of counties Sligo and Leitrim in north-west Ireland, drained by the Garavogue River through the town of Sligo. It holds many small islands, among them Innisfree, made famous by W.

lakkundi.s: Lakkundi is a village in Gadag district, Karnataka, India, that was a prosperous town and mint under the Western Chalukyas and the Hoysalas in the 11th and 12th centuries. It holds dozens of temples and stepped wells in the ornate later Chalukya style, among them the Brahma…

little-turtle.s: Little Turtle, Mihšihkinaahkwa in Miami, was a war leader of the Miami people. With the Shawnee leader Blue Jacket he led the Western Confederacy to victories over Josiah Harmar in 1790 and Arthur St.

li-clan-of-longxi.s: The Li clan of Longxi was a prominent aristocratic family of north-western China, from the Longxi commandery in today's Gansu. It claimed descent from the Han general Li Guang, and Li Gao, founder of the Western Liang state in 400, came from it.

li-deming.s: Li Deming (981–1032) was a Tangut ruler and the son of Li Jiqian. Succeeding his father in 1004, he made peace with the Song dynasty while extending Tangut rule westwards into the Hexi Corridor, where Ganzhou was taken from the Uyghurs in 1028.

li-jiqian.s: Li Jiqian (963–1004) was a leader of the Tanguts of the Ordos region. When his kinsman surrendered the family's hereditary territories to the Song dynasty in 982, he refused, fled into the steppe and waged a long war against the Song, allying with the Liao dynasty.

liejiaomi.s: Liejiaomi was a ruler (kunmo) of the Wusun in the 2nd century BCE. According to the Han histories he was raised among the Xiongnu after his father was killed, and he later led the Wusun west to the Ili valley and the Issyk-Kul basin, driving out the Yuezhi.

liu-xijun.s: Liu Xijun was a Han dynasty princess, daughter of Liu Jian, Prince of Jiangdu, sent by Emperor Wu around 105 BCE to marry the aged Wusun ruler Liejiaomi as part of an alliance against the Xiongnu. After his death she married his grandson and successor, according to Wusun custom.

leifeng-pagoda.s: The Leifeng Pagoda is a Buddhist pagoda on Sunset Hill on the south shore of West Lake in Hangzhou, China. It was built in 975 by Qian Chu, the last king of Wuyue.

lai-junchen.s: Lai Junchen (651–697) was a secret police official under Wu Zetian, notorious for using torture and forced confessions against her opponents. With his colleagues he compiled a manual on fabricating charges, the Classic of Entrapment.

liu-heita.s: Liu Heita (died 623) was a general of the rebel leader Dou Jiande in the wars after the fall of the Sui dynasty. After the Tang captured and executed Dou in 621, his former officers rose under Liu Heita, who quickly recovered Dou's lands in Hebei and proclaimed himself Prince…

lulin.s: The Lülin, or 'Green Forest', were a rebel movement that arose around 17 CE in the hills of Hubei against Wang Mang's Xin dynasty. In 23 they enthroned a Han kinsman as the Gengshi Emperor, and their armies captured Chang'an, where Wang Mang was killed.

lake-xochimilco.s: Lake Xochimilco was one of the five linked lakes of the Valley of Mexico, lying in its southern part. The Xochimilca and later the Aztecs farmed its shallow waters with chinampas, raised fields built of mud and vegetation.

li-zuoche.s: Li Zuoche was a strategist of the state of Zhao in the wars that followed the fall of the Qin dynasty. Captured by the Han general Han Xin after the Battle of Jingxing in 204 BCE, he was treated with honour and advised Han Xin to win over the state of Yan by diplomacy instead…

liu-rengong.s: Liu Rengong (died 914) was a late Tang warlord who became military governor of Lulong Circuit, centred on Youzhou near modern Beijing, in the 890s. He fought off the rival warlord Zhu Wen but in 907 was overthrown and imprisoned by his son Liu Shouguang, who later proclaimed…

lake-yaxha.s: Lake Yaxha is a lake in the Petén department of northern Guatemala. The Maya city of Yaxha, one of the largest Classic sites of the region, stands on a ridge along its northern shore, and the Postclassic island site of Topoxte lies in the lake.

longxi-commandery.s: Longxi Commandery was a commandery established by the state of Qin in the early 3rd century BCE in the upper Wei River valley of south-eastern Gansu. Retained by the Qin and Han empires, it guarded the routes to the west, and it gave its name to the Li clan of Longxi, from…

lasta.s: Lasta is a mountainous historic region of north-central Ethiopia, in the Amhara Region, centred on the town of Lalibela. It was the homeland of the Agaw Zagwe dynasty, which ruled Ethiopia from about the 12th century until 1270.

la-mojana.s: La Mojana is a low-lying wetland region of northern Colombia, in the departments of Sucre, Bolívar, Córdoba and Antioquia, where the San Jorge and Cauca rivers approach the Magdalena. In pre-Columbian times the Zenú built a vast network of canals and raised fields there to…

lake-manasarovar.s: Lake Manasarovar is a high freshwater lake in Ngari, western Tibet, at about 4,600 metres, south of Mount Kailash. It is sacred to Hindus, Buddhists, Jains and followers of Bon, and pilgrims walk around its shores.

li-mi-sui-dynasty.s: Li Mi was a Chinese aristocrat and rebel leader at the end of the Sui dynasty. After joining the failed revolt of Yang Xuangan in 613, he became leader of the Wagang rebels in Henan, seized the great granaries near Luoyang and besieged the city held by Wang Shichong.

lingshou.s: Lingshou was the capital of the state of Zhongshan from about 380 BCE until its conquest by Zhao in 296 BCE. Its remains lie near Pingshan in Hebei, China, where excavations since the 1970s have uncovered city walls, workshops and royal tombs, including the tomb of King Cuo…

livonian-crusade.s: The Livonian Crusade was the conquest and Christianisation of present-day Latvia and Estonia by German crusaders, chiefly the bishops of Riga and the Livonian Brothers of the Sword, with Danish forces in northern Estonia, from about 1198 to 1290. The Livs, Latgalians,…

lithuanian-civil-war-1432-1438.s: The Lithuanian Civil War of 1432–1438 was fought over the throne of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania between Švitrigaila and Sigismund Kęstutaitis, who was backed by Poland. Sigismund's victory at Pabaiskas (Wiłkomierz) in 1435 decided the war in his favour and kept Lithuania in…

liege-wars.s: The Liège Wars were a series of conflicts between the Prince-Bishopric of Liège and the Burgundian dukes Philip the Good and Charles the Bold, whose relative Louis de Bourbon had been imposed as bishop. The Liégeois were defeated at Brustem in 1467, and after a further rising…

liberators-civil-war.s: The Liberators' civil war was the Roman civil war that followed the assassination of Julius Caesar in 44 BCE. The Second Triumvirate of Mark Antony, Octavian and Lepidus fought the assassins, led by Marcus Junius Brutus and Gaius Cassius Longinus, who styled themselves…

lithuanian-crusade.s: The Lithuanian Crusade was the series of campaigns by the Teutonic Order and the Livonian Order against the pagan Grand Duchy of Lithuania from the late thirteenth century. The orders raided Lithuania nearly every year, and Lithuania struck back into Prussia and Livonia.

lebanese-civil-war.s: The Lebanese Civil War was fought from 1975 to 1990 among Lebanon's sectarian militias, Palestinian groups and outside powers. Christian, Muslim and Druze factions fought over political power, and Syria and Israel invaded and occupied parts of the country.

long-turkish-war.s: The Long Turkish War was fought from 1593 to 1606 between the Habsburg monarchy and the Ottoman Empire, mainly in Hungary, with Transylvania, Wallachia and Moldavia joining the Habsburg side for a time. Neither side won decisively, despite the Ottoman victory at Mezőkeresztes…

lithuanian-wars-of-independence.s: The Lithuanian Wars of Independence were the three wars that newly independent Lithuania fought after the First World War: against Soviet Russia, against the West Russian Volunteer Army, known as the Bermontians, and against Poland. Lithuania defeated the Soviet and Bermontian…

lam-son-uprising.s: The Lam Sơn uprising was the revolt led by Lê Lợi against the Ming dynasty, which had occupied Vietnam since 1407. Starting from Lam Sơn in Thanh Hóa, the rebels fought a long guerrilla war and then besieged the Ming in Đông Quan.

lithuanian-soviet-war.s: The Lithuanian–Soviet War was fought between newly independent Lithuania and Soviet Russia from December 1918, when the Red Army advanced westwards after the German withdrawal and took Vilnius. Lithuanian volunteers, helped by German volunteer units, halted the advance and…

liberal-wars.s: The Liberal Wars were a civil war in Portugal from 1828 to 1834 between liberal constitutionalists supporting the young Queen Maria II and absolutists led by her uncle Miguel, who had seized the throne. Maria's father, the former Brazilian emperor Pedro, landed at Porto in…
